source_snapshot.title: Spices, shipwrecks and ancient trade routes: Louvre Abu Dhabi explores 1,000 years of Indian Ocean history
source_snapshot.text: Visitors to Louvre Abu Dhabi's latest exhibition begin their journey in darkness, lights above mimicking a star-filled sky. It's a reminder of a time when sailors relied on the heavens to navigate the Indian Ocean, carrying spices, precious stones and textiles between distant civilisations. Such voyages connected communities from East Africa and the Arabian Peninsula to India, China and South-East Asia, establishing commercial and cultural relationships that developed over centuries. Their history is explored in Spices and Wonders: Sailing the Indian Ocean, opening at Louvre Abu Dhabi on Wednesday, October 14, and running until February 14, 2027. Organised in partnership with the Guimet National Museum of Asian Arts in Paris, the exhibition brings together about 240 artworks and historical objects from 24 lenders, covering maritime exchange from antiquity to the 17th century. Among them are archaeological discoveries, jewellery, religious artefacts and objects recovered from shipwrecks. Six detailed models of historic vessels and specially created maps illustrate how sailors crossed vast waters and transported goods between continents. The exhibition places the Arabian Gulf at the centre of its narrative, examining the region's historical role in these networks. “The story is told from here, and that is something we consider very important at Louvre Abu Dhabi: telling the story from the region,” says Guilhem Andre, the museum's director of scientific, curatorial and collections management “This has never really been done on this scale before.” The exhibition features loans from institutions including the Asian Civilisations Museum in Singapore, the National Museum of the Philippines and the Al Sabah Collection in Kuwait . Pierre Baptiste, director of collections and curatorial staff at the Guimet in Paris, says the exhibition explores how people established relationships through commerce and spiritual exchange. The Arabian Gulf's pearl industry provides a significant regional example. Pearls harvested from its waters travelled to markets in India and beyond, while materials such as carnelian were traded across the ocean from ancient times. Later networks expanded the circulation of gemstones, jewellery , furniture and textiles. Andre said the objects revealed how discoveries of new sources of gold, spinels, rubies and emeralds influenced jewellery production. Diplomatic gifts also feature, demonstrating how valuable objects helped establish relationships between rulers and communities. Beyond the goods themselves, the exhibition examines the techniques that made these journeys possible. Its opening gallery recreates the darkness experienced by ancient navigators, who relied on stars and coastal landmarks to determine their position. “The main idea was to give visitors a sense of what people at the time experienced,” Baptiste says. Subsequent galleries explore navigational instruments, including the kamal, used in Arab and Indian maritime traditions, and the astrolabe. Twenty-four maps created specifically for the exhibition trace the routes connecting ports across the ocean. Six large ship models represent Arabian, South-East Asian, Chinese, Portuguese and Spanish maritime traditions. Andre says they were constructed in South Africa over the course of a year, drawing on extensive historical research. The models are accompanied by objects recovered from shipwrecks, offering evidence of the cargo these vessels carried. Baptiste says advances in underwater archaeology since the 1990s have enabled researchers to recover significant quantities of material from sunken ships, including objects originating in China, India, Spain and Mexico. Among the most valuable commodities were spices, which commanded high prices alongside luxury products such as jewellery and textiles. Cultural exchange is another central theme. A Buddha sculpture from present-day Pakistan, loaned by the Guimet, reflects the influence of ancient Greek and Roman artistic traditions on Buddhist sculpture. The final gallery examines four religious traditions that spread across the Indian Ocean, showing how beliefs travelled along the same routes as commercial goods. Andre says merchants and pilgrims often crossed these waters for different purposes, carrying objects and practices that became part of life in distant communities. “Religion was not separate from trade,” he says. “They were all part of the same relationships and exchanges.” The exhibition also offers a perspective on maritime history that predates the expansion of European influence in Indian Ocean commerce during the 17th and 18th centuries. Baptiste says the decision to conclude the historical narrative in the 17th century was deliberate, allowing visitors to understand the networks that existed long before European powers became prominent in the region. These earlier connections, he says, laid the foundations for the expansion of international commerce in subsequent centuries. “We wanted to approach the history of commercial relationships from a multicultural perspective,” he says. “Europe was only one part of this story.” Spices and Wonders: Sailing the Indian Ocean runs at Louvre Abu Dhabi from October 14, 2026, until February 14, 2027. The exhibition will subsequently travel to the Guimet in Paris, where it will be presented from May 12 to September 6, 2027.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai's shared housing rules will lead to better quality of life for those on low incomes, says official
source_snapshot.text: Dubai's crackdown on overcrowded and illegally sub-let apartments will result in a better life for residents on low incomes, a senior official from the emirate's municipality has said. The Dubai Municipality's shared housing guide sets standards for building design, occupancy, health and safety, shared amenities and approved locations. It gives landlords until September 1, 2027, to comply with the new requirements across 43 designated areas of the emirate. Nasser Al Shaibani, structural control section manager at Dubai Municipality, said most tenants living in shared accommodation previously did not have any contracts "or any legal backbone to their residential status”. “With this law, tenants can have a one or two-month contract, which gives them the flexibility to change, to go and come back while having legal support," he said. “This will have a big impact on Dubai, as we'll see people moving to better housing and a better quality of life.” The new regulations address unregulated residential practices , prevent rooms from being subdivided, and protect the privacy and rights of owners and occupants. The new law requires buildings to be designated as either individual or family-shared housing. “Each building should be designated only for individuals or only for families; you cannot mix both permits within one building,” Mr Al Shaibani said. “Within this year, we are giving the building owners time to get the necessary approval from Dubai Municipality, Dubai Land Authority, Civil Defence and Rera. “During this time, Dubai Municipality will keep on monitoring those buildings. We will continue visiting and we will do the inspections. This period does not exempt them from unpermitted building modification." The municipality has received six applications for shared-housing permits so far. Three of them have been approved through the Build in Dubai platform. Apartment blocks designated for shared accommodation are close to public transport and workplaces to reduce commuter traffic and encourage people to walk or cycle. A 2025 Dubai workforce report by Edenred UAE found that 60 per cent of workers earned less than Dh5,000 ($1,361) a month, creating strong demand for affordable housing. While the new regulations aim to improve housing standards, industry operators caution that higher costs could make it harder to provide affordable accommodation for all. Rayan Hanna, founder and chief executive of Next House, an affordable housing platform in Dubai specialising in short-term rentals, backed the regulations but said the sector still faces challenges. “Although subdividing apartments into smaller rooms, commonly known as partitions, and operating shared rooms in residential units was prohibited, this type of accommodation has existed across Dubai for years,” Mr Hanna told The National . “A clearer legal framework for shared housing creates opportunities for experienced operators, property owners and institutional investors. “I also believe we will see stronger enforcement against illegally subdivided and overcrowded apartments in premium residential areas, with shared housing gradually moving towards designated locations.” Next House caters to professionals visiting Dubai who are looking for short to medium-term rental agreements. Under the new standards, shared accommodation must include kitchens, sanitary facilities and designated areas for dining, recreation, laundry and clothes drying. Bedrooms must be at least five square metres per person. There must be at least one toilet for every four occupants and one shower for every six people. Kitchen space must provide at least one square metre per person, and buildings must provide bicycle parking for at least 10 per cent of residents. Landlords found in breach of the regulations can be fined up to Dh500,000 ($136,147) for a first offence, with repeat offenders facing a maximum penalty of Dh1 million. Mr Hanna, who has amended his business model to comply with the latest rules, said affordability remained the biggest challenge for many people moving to Dubai for work. He said operators may need to generate about Dh2,000 to Dh3,000 per rentable room per month to make the model financially attractive for investors and property owners. “Many people relying on bed spaces simply cannot afford more than Dh700–Dh900 a month,” he said. “The new regulations introduce minimum space requirements, which are important improvements, but they also increase operating and development costs. “The real challenge is finding the balance between making housing safe and compliant, and making it attractive for investors. I don't think these regulations alone will solve Dubai's affordable housing problem, but they're certainly a step in the right direction.” Dubai is one of the world's fastest-growing cities , with its population of about 4.8 million forecast to increase to six million by 2040. The city's infrastructure is expanding alongside its population, with extensions to public transport networks and existing communities.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Health Board of Directors reviews progress on Hamdan Bin Rashid Cancer Hospital, new Diabetes Center
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 15th October, 2026 (WAM) -- In a meeting chaired by H.H. Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum, Chairman of the Board of Directors of Dubai Health, and attended by H.H. Sheikh Mansoor bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice Chairman of the Board, the Dubai Health Board of Directors convened to review the latest developments on two landmark projects — the Hamdan Bin Rashid Cancer Hospital and the new Diabetes Center — and discuss future initiatives.Held at the Dubai Health headquarters, the meeting was also attended by Dr. Raja Easa Al Gurg, His Excellency Abdulla Abdul Rahman Al Shaibani, Walid Saeed Al Awadhi, Mohammed Hassan Al Shehhi, Professor Sir Ian Andrew Greer, Dr. Amer Sharif, and Dr. Hanan Al Suwaidi.The Board commended the advances made on the Hamdan Bin Rashid Cancer Hospital, including construction progress, the development of the hospital's global partnerships strategy, and the appointment of a Chair of Cancer Care.The hospital will be a landmark addition to Dubai's healthcare landscape, offering comprehensive care that meets the highest international standards, with a patient and family-centred approach that elevates the overall treatment experience.The Board also reviewed progress on the new Diabetes Center, which was approved in November 2024 and is set to open early next year. The facility will expand access to preventive care, advance treatment programmes, and promote early detection and healthier lifestyles.H.H. Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum welcomed the Board members and acknowledged their commitment to advancing strategic projects that support the Dubai 2040 Urban Master Plan, which aims to develop vibrant, healthy, and inclusive communities in line with the city's growth.H.H. said: "As Dubai continues to grow, developing future-ready healthcare infrastructure is essential to meeting the needs of our population, and fulfilling our leadership's vision of a sustainable, integrated health system that places people and their quality of life at the forefront of priorities.”He also expressed his appreciation for the dedication of Dubai Health's teams, and his confidence in their ability to continue raising the bar for healthcare services, reinforcing Dubai's position as a leading healthcare destination.H.H. Sheikh Mansoor bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum said: "We are committed to building an integrated academic health system that unites clinical care, medical education, and research, fostering a culture of innovation and knowledge. We are working to develop specialised medical talent, advance research, and translate findings into practical applications that improve diagnosis, treatment, and patient outcomes.”Dr. Raja Easa Al Gurg said: "The Hamdan Bin Rashid Cancer Hospital and the new Diabetes Center are meaningful additions to Dubai's healthcare landscape. Together, they will support early detection, advance care pathways, and improve the experience of patients and their families”.Following the meeting, H.H. Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum and H.H. Sheikh Mansoor bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum witnessed the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Dubai Health and the Mohammed Bin Rashid Housing Establishment (MBRHE).The agreement aims to facilitate Dubai Health employees’ access to housing services by simplifying procedures, providing direct channels for requests and inquiries, and organising awareness workshops on available services and initiatives, helping improve the employee experience.By supporting employees with their housing needs, the MoU also aims to attract and retain young national talent in Dubai's healthcare sector, providing the stability that enables them to thrive professionally and play an active role in shaping the future of health in Dubai.Mohammed Hassan Al Shehhi, CEO of MBRHE, said: “Our partnership with Dubai Health reflects our commitment to making housing services more accessible and supporting employees’ well-being and family stability. By simplifying procedures, providing direct channels for inquiries, and organising awareness workshops, we aim to make it easier for Dubai Health employees to benefit from available housing services and initiatives”.He added: “This agreement also reflects the importance of collaboration between government entities in delivering services that put people first and contribute to a better quality of life, in line with Dubai’s vision to advance public services and community well-being.”Dr. Amer Sharif, CEO of Dubai Health, said: “We are committed to building partnerships that support our employees’ well-being and family stability, while making it easier for them to access services that meet their needs. We believe in creating a motivating work environment for our people, and value our collaboration with MBRHE in making housing services more accessible and contributing to their quality of life.”

source_snapshot.title: What should employer do if domestic worker stops working?
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Employers in the UAE must report a domestic worker's absence within five days if the worker stops reporting for duty without a valid reason and their whereabouts are unknown, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MoHRE) has said.The ministry clarified that employers are required to submit a report when a domestic worker leaves work without their knowledge and they are unable to establish the worker's whereabouts or contact them..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..The report, officially known as a Domestic Worker Absence from Work complaint, must be submitted through the ministry's approved service channels within five days of the worker's unexplained absence.How employers can report an absent domestic workerEmployers can submit the report through the official MoHRE website or the MOHRE UAE mobile app.They should access the ministry's domestic worker services, select the absence-from-work reporting service, complete the application with the required details and submit it for processing.The ministry's official guidance confirms that the five-day reporting requirement applies specifically to domestic workers. It differs from the rules governing private-sector employees, for whom an absence report generally applies after more than seven consecutive days.Employers can also seek guidance on the application process or follow up on requests through the ministry's customer service number: 600590000.MoHRE urged employers to consult its official website for details of the application procedures and available channels..UAE workers can report 11 types of labour violations to MOHRE.UAE fines 42 domestic worker recruitment offices over 135 labour law violations.UAE outlines four cases requiring domestic worker agencies to issue refunds.How to report unpaid salaries anonymously in the UAE

source_snapshot.title: Zayed Authority for People of Determination, Abu Dhabi Police launch Sign Language Voice platform to enhance police services for hearing-impaired people
source_snapshot.text: ABU DHABI, 15th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Abu Dhabi Police General Headquarters, in collaboration with Zayed Authority for People of Determination, affiliated with the Department of Community Development – Abu Dhabi, has launched the Sign Language Voice platform, a product of the strategic partnership between the two entities.The platform aims to enhance access to police services for deaf and hard-of-hearing people, enabling them to communicate easily and independently through a digital channel that uses sign language. The initiative contributes to faster response times, improved service quality, and an enhanced customer experience.The platform forms part of Abu Dhabi Police’s ongoing efforts to leverage innovative digital solutions to develop a more efficient and inclusive police service ecosystem, in line with the Abu Dhabi Government’s vision for smart, human-centred services. Zayed Authority for People of Determination contributed its specialised expertise in empowering deaf people, helping ensure the development of an innovative solution that addresses their needs, facilitates access to services, and enhances their independence and privacy throughout the communication process.The Sign Language Voice platform provides a direct visual communication channel with a certified sign language interpreter, enabling immediate and accurate communication between customer service employees and deaf customers. This helps reduce the time required to access interpretation services when needed, expedite transactions, improve service quality, and promote equal access to government services.The collaboration between the two entities has encompassed numerous initiatives and projects aimed at supporting and empowering People of Determination, promoting the use of sign language, exchanging expertise, developing support services, and leveraging modern technologies to remove barriers faced by deaf people. The platform is set to be rolled out across police stations in the emirate of Abu Dhabi, further facilitating access to services and enhancing the customer experience.Abdullah Abdulalee Al Humaidan, Acting Director General of Zayed Authority for People of Determination, said that the launch of the Sign Language Voice platform reflects the success of the strategic partnership between the Authority and Abu Dhabi Police General Headquarters. He noted that it demonstrates both entities’ commitment to leveraging innovation and technology to develop more inclusive government services, in line with the aspirations of the UAE’s wise leadership to empower People of Determination and enhance their quality of life.He said: “Our strategic partnership with Abu Dhabi Police General Headquarters is an institutional partnership that has contributed, over the years, to the implementation of numerous impactful initiatives and projects, with a direct positive impact on the development of services provided to People of Determination. The launch of the Sign Language Voice platform builds on this collaboration and embodies a shared vision founded on the belief that empowering People of Determination begins with removing barriers to accessing services and harnessing modern technologies to develop smart solutions that enable deaf people to communicate with police services easily, efficiently and independently.“Zayed Authority for People of Determination continues to work with its strategic partners to develop initiatives and services for different groups of People of Determination, particularly deaf people, by promoting the use of sign language, adopting innovative digital solutions, and launching impactful projects that contribute to advancing social inclusion and empowering People of Determination to participate actively across all aspects of life. These efforts align with the emirate of Abu Dhabi’s vision to build a more inclusive society and enhance quality of life.”Major General Imran Ahmed Al Mazrouei, Director of the Human Resources Sector at Abu Dhabi Police, said that the launch of the Sign Language Voice platform represents a significant addition to the police services ecosystem. He noted that it reflects Abu Dhabi Police’s commitment to fostering an inclusive institutional environment that places people at the heart of its priorities and empowers deaf People of Determination through innovative digital solutions that facilitate efficient and independent access to services and provide a more seamless and flexible experience.He explained that the success of such initiatives relies on investing in human capital and continuously developing employees’ skills and readiness to engage effectively with all members of society, alongside leveraging modern technologies, institutional partnerships, and knowledge exchange. These efforts contribute to developing services that are more flexible and responsive to diverse needs while reinforcing the principles of inclusion, equal opportunity, and accessibility.He noted that Abu Dhabi Police continues to adopt impactful and sustainable initiatives that combine the capabilities of its human resources with technological innovation, enhancing the quality of services provided, supporting quality of life, and advancing the Abu Dhabi Government’s vision for a more inclusive and sustainable society.The launch of the Sign Language Voice platform builds on a longstanding partnership between Abu Dhabi Police and Zayed Authority for People of Determination. Over the years, the collaboration has encompassed several areas, including promoting the use of sign language, developing support services, exchanging expertise, and creating innovative solutions that address the needs of People of Determination, culminating in the use of modern digital technologies to facilitate deaf people’s access to government services.

source_snapshot.title: Aldar acquires nine residential buildings in Sharjah for AED1.1 billion
source_snapshot.text: ABU DHABI, 15th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Aldar on Thursday announced an AED1.1 billion forward purchase agreement with Arada for three residential blocks comprising over 1,100 units across nine buildings in Aljada, Sharjah’s flagship mixed-use master development.The transaction marks Aldar’s first real estate investment in the emirate and expands its develop-to-hold pipeline to AED21 billion. The transaction will add more than 1,100 units to Aldar’s portfolio, with the assets to be delivered by Arada in Q4 2029.Building on the recently announced AED15 billion development partnership between Aldar and Arada, the transaction provides Aldar with access to Sharjah’s large and growing residential market through an established integrated community. The investment also broadens Aldar’s geographic exposure while adding a high-quality residential opportunity with attractive long-term fundamentals.Talal Al Dhiyebi, Group Chief Executive Officer of Aldar, said the investment in Aljada marks the group's entry into Sharjah's residential market and expands its portfolio of rental properties, in line with its "develop-and-hold" strategy. He added that Aldar looks forward to further strengthening its partnership with Arada.Ahmed Alkhoshaibi, Group Chief Executive Officer of Arada, said: “This transaction is a strong vote of confidence in both Aljada and the Sharjah residential market more broadly. This investment marks another step in our growing partnership with Aldar, and we look forward to identifying further opportunities to work together across sectors.”Aljada is a leading mixed-use master development in Sharjah, spanning 2.2 million sqm and expected to comprise approximately 25,000 residential units at full build-out, with an anticipated gross sales value of AED35 billion.Residential handovers have been underway since 2021, with over 8,800 units delivered across multiple districts.The community is supported by completed lifestyle, hospitality, education and retail infrastructure, including the Madar family entertainment district, two international schools, two hotels, the Nest student housing complex and more than 300,000 sq ft of occupied retail space.The community is within easy reach of Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Road and Al Dhaid Road, seven minutes from Sharjah International Airport and around 20 minutes from Dubai International Airport, providing strong connectivity to both Sharjah and Dubai.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai registers 196,000 new vehicles in six months, more than 1,000 a day
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: More than 196,000 new vehicles were registered in Dubai during the first half of 2026, averaging over 1,000 a day, as population growth, urban expansion and economic activity continued to drive demand for transport services across the emirate.Dubai's Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) recorded 196,042 first-time vehicle registrations between January and June, equivalent to more than 32,000 a month..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..Ahmed Mahboob, CEO of the RTA's Licensing Agency, said the sustained increase in vehicle registrations reflected Dubai's rapid population, urban and economic growth, which has led to greater demand for vehicle registration and inspection services, according to Al Bayan. He added that the authority is responding by developing an integrated service system based on advanced technologies and smart solutions to streamline procedures, speed up transactions and improve the accuracy of vehicle inspections and licensing.The RTA uses electronic data-sharing systems with relevant authorities, smart verification of vehicle and owner information, and advanced technical inspection equipment.It has also introduced updated inspection standards for electric vehicles and is incorporating artificial intelligence and machine learning into its operations.Mahboob noted that the services and initiatives available through the RTA's website and mobile application are helping accelerate procedures, improve service quality and increase customer satisfaction.Vehicle testing centres to increase to 35 by 2030Dubai currently has 30 vehicle testing centres operating across the emirate, with plans to increase the number to 35 by 2030 to accommodate growing demand.Mahboob stated that the expansion would support the emirate's continued urban and population growth while improving accessibility, operational efficiency and customer experience.The RTA also operates a centralised technical inspection system that consolidates vehicle testing data, standardises procedures and strengthens oversight across all inspection centres.The system automatically calculates inspection results, improving accuracy and supporting regulatory compliance. The authority also uses advanced technologies at its Smart Monitoring Centre alongside field inspections to strengthen supervision.Al Satwa roundabout Separately, the RTA has completed the conversion of Al Satwa roundabout into a signalised intersection, including upgrades to the surrounding road infrastructure.The project is expected to cut journey times by 50 per cent and reduce waiting times and traffic queues by up to 60 per cent during peak hours.The authority said the improvements would increase traffic efficiency on roads connecting to the intersection and improve safety for motorists and pedestrians.

source_snapshot.title: Hamdan Bin Rashid Foundation launches sixth season of Future Science Challenge
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 16th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Hamdan Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Foundation for Medical and Educational Sciences has launched the sixth season of the Future Science Challenge, following more than a 600 percent increase in participation since its inception five years ago.Held under the theme "The Future of Roads & Mobility" and the slogan "The Smarter Road", the competition targets gifted and talented Arab students aged 10 to 17, with team registration open until 24th October 2026.The new season focuses on the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), sensors and smart systems to develop practical solutions that can make roads and mobility systems safer, smarter and more efficient.Participating teams will identify real-world challenges and develop technology-based solutions in areas including traffic management, road safety, parking, emergency response and infrastructure.Humaid Mohammed Al Qatami, Chairman of the Board of Trustees of Hamdan Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Foundation for Medical and Educational Sciences, said participation had grown by more than 600 percent, reflecting increasing interest among Arab students in science, technology and innovation.He stressed the importance of equipping students with critical thinking, analytical and problem-solving skills, noting that AI and IoT offer opportunities to move beyond using technology to developing innovative solutions that benefit communities.Al Qatami said the competition's focus on roads and mobility reflected broader efforts to build safer, more efficient and sustainable cities.He also encouraged students to embrace teamwork and collaboration, emphasising that scientific progress depends on combining diverse knowledge, skills and perspectives.Dr. Khalifa Al Suwaidi, Executive Director of Hamdan Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Foundation for Medical and Educational Sciences, explained that the Future Science Challenge is an online competitive platform designed to develop the skills of gifted and talented Arab students in science, technology and innovation through multidisciplinary applied learning, while encouraging them to use scientific and technological knowledge to address real-world problems and develop innovative solutions.Dr. Al Suwaidi said the online competition had attracted more than 150 student teams from schools and educational institutions across Arab countries.He added that the new season includes a training programme to support participating teams and supervisors in developing their projects. Three training webinars will be held on 7th November, 21st November and 19th December 2026, while final project submissions will be accepted from 18th February to 17th March 2027, leading up to the closing ceremony and announcement of the winners on 29th April 2027.Dr. Al Suwaidi highlighted the role of sponsors, partners, teachers, supervisors and parents in supporting students, adding that the competition provides opportunities for practical learning, experimentation, collaboration and skills development.

source_snapshot.title: Zayed International Airport launches daily Berlin flights with Condor
source_snapshot.text: ABU DHABI, 16th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Zayed International Airport (AUH) announced on Friday the launch of Condor’s new daily, year-round service between Berlin and Abu Dhabi. The new route, operated by an Airbus A320neo, marks the first scheduled direct connection between the two capitals on Condor’s network.Condor’s codeshare partnership with Etihad Airways strengthens connectivity between Germany and Abu Dhabi by providing passengers travelling from Berlin the ability to connect to destinations across Etihad’s network, while travellers from Abu Dhabi can access Condor’s network through Berlin and beyond.The route supports the continued growth of Abu Dhabi’s tourism sector, offering visitors from Germany greater access to the emirate’s cultural and leisure attractions. It also strengthens the movement of people and supports closer commercial links between Abu Dhabi and Berlin.Carsten Nørland, Chief Commercial Officer of Abu Dhabi Airports, said the launch of Condor’s daily, year-round Berlin service strengthens direct connectivity between two dynamic, outward-looking capitals. "Through our partnership with Condor and Etihad Airways, Zayed International Airport (AUH) is connecting Abu Dhabi with Berlin and beyond, supporting greater opportunities for tourism, business and trade while reinforcing Abu Dhabi’s position as a leading global destination," he added. Haitham Ali Khamis, Acting Director of Tourism Products Development, Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi, stated, “The launch of Condor’s direct service from Berlin is an important step in expanding Abu Dhabi’s reach within the German market. Germany has consistently been a valuable source of visitors, and improved accessibility will help introduce even more travellers to the unique experiences on offer across the emirate.”Dr. Pierre Dominique Prümm, Chief Commercial Officer at Condor Airlines, said, “Together with our codeshare partner Etihad Airways, we are offering our guests not only an attractive direct service to Abu Dhabi, but also seamless connections to numerous destinations across Asia, Australia and Africa. This close cooperation brings together the strengths of both networks and gives our guests even more travel options for both leisure and business.”Lena Havia, Vice President Alliances & Joint Ventures at Etihad Airways, stated, “By bringing together our complementary networks, we are providing guests in Berlin with daily, year-round access to Abu Dhabi, as well as seamless onward connections across Etihad’s network. This is a valuable addition to what we offer in Germany, and a partnership we look forward to growing.”The route adds to Etihad's expanding presence in Germany, which already includes 35 flights a week and a Frankfurt–Abu Dhabi link, with further weekly services planned as the partnership develops.

source_snapshot.title: DCT Abu Dhabi unveils participating artists, locations for 2nd edition of Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial
source_snapshot.text: ABU DHABI, 16th October, 2026 (WAM) -- The Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi (DCT Abu Dhabi) has revealed the list of participating artists and locations for the second edition of the Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial.Led by Artistic Director Elvira Dyangani Ose, who also serves as Artistic Director of the Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa (MOCAA), the Biennial is set to weave art into the fabric of the emirate.Opening in Al Ain on 23rd October 2026 and Abu Dhabi on 15th November 2026, this edition centres on “Home: A Glossary for a Communal Sense of Place”, approaching 'home' not as a static location, but as an ever evolving, shared human experience.Through site-responsive installations, research-led practices and communal encounters embedded within civic landscapes, the exhibition prioritises sustained engagement - inviting audiences to interact with art while establishing meaningful connections between artists, communities and place.The 2026–2027 edition brings together 21 visionary artists presenting public artwork installations that explore urbanscapes, collective memory, material culture and civic participation through monumental, interactive and multi-sensory works.Bringing together prominent Emirati and International artists, the roster includes - Akram Zaatari, Asunción Molinos Gordo, blaxTARLINES, Céleste Boursier-Mougenot, Elena del Rivero, Ibrahim Mahama, Iván Argote, Jean-Marie Appriou, Kapwani Kiwanga, Khalid Al Banna, Laure Prouvost, Marinella Senatore, M'barek Bouhchichi, Mercedes Azpilicueta, Nari Ward, Reena Saini Kallat, Roudhah Al Mazrouei, Shama Al Hamed, Serge Attukwei Clottey, Vica Pacheco, and Yinka Shonibare.Across Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Biennial will unfold across a range of public and cultural locations, including Mina Zayed (MiZa), Souq Al Mina, Saadiyat Cultural District (the park between Zayed National Museum and Louvre Abu Dhabi), Hidd Al Saadiyat and selected locations across Al Ain, embedding contemporary art within the emirate's diverse urban and cultural landscapes.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai eases villa construction rules for Emiratis, allows second family homes
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Dubai Municipality has introduced new regulations allowing Emirati homeowners greater flexibility to expand their villas, build second homes for family members and add residential annexes, under an initiative designed to ease housing pressures and support family stability.The changes, introduced under the Home First initiative, include allowing homeowners to reduce building setbacks to 1.5 metres, construct a second floor covering the full area of the first floor and build a separate villa for family use..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..However, the municipality has set conditions governing the changes, including a minimum age of 18 for beneficiaries of a second villa and written consent from neighbours where construction removes the required setback along a shared boundary, Emarat Al Youm reported. The regulations also set limits on the height, size and location of family accommodation and service annexes, while prohibiting the construction of certain structures before the main villa is completed.The municipality said the initiative is intended to provide flexible housing options for Emirati families, reduce living costs and meet changing accommodation needs while strengthening family stability and community cohesion.Greater flexibility for villa extensionsUnder the revised planning and construction requirements, Emirati homeowners may reduce setbacks to 1.5 metres on all sides of their properties without additional conditions.The municipality has also permitted setbacks to be eliminated along boundaries adjoining neighbouring properties or access lanes, provided that all habitable spaces receive adequate lighting in accordance with the Dubai Building Code.Windows must not face the neighbouring property or access lane, and homeowners must obtain signed approval from the neighbour if the setback along their shared boundary is removed..Renting a bedspace in Dubai? How to check if your building is approved under new rules. The revised rules also allow a second floor to cover 100 per cent of the first-floor area without additional restrictions. Homeowners may continue to add stairwell enclosures and lift rooms.Second villas permitted for family membersThe municipality has established three conditions for constructing a second villa on the same plot for private family use.Applications must be intended to accommodate first-degree relatives or meet social needs. Homeowners must also sign an undertaking confirming that the additional villa will be used exclusively for private family purposes.The beneficiary of the second villa must be at least 18 years old when the application is submitted.Subject to the application, homeowners may also provide the second villa with its own boundary wall, entrance and utility meter.The changes are intended to help families provide separate accommodation for relatives while making better use of existing residential plots..5 major UAE rule changes announced in October: What residents need to know. New provisions for family annexesThe municipality has also eased restrictions on residential family annexes, allowing construction without setbacks along neighbouring properties and access lanes, subject to a maximum height of eight metres.Where the main villa has not yet been built, applicants must submit a preliminary master plan covering the entire plot, showing the proposed locations of the family annex, main villa and service annex.Plans for family accommodation must include at least two bedrooms, a living room and associated facilities.Windows facing neighbouring properties or access lanes are prohibited. Where a family annex or service annex faces the street, its architectural design must be consistent with the surrounding appearance.Strict conditions for service annexesThe revised regulations allow service annexes of up to two storeys, ground and first floor, with a maximum height of eight metres.Setback requirements vary depending on the number of floors and the annex's position relative to the main villa and neighbouring properties..Dubai's shared housing law takes effect, fines of up to Dh1 million for repeat violations. For a single-storey service annex, the municipality allows construction without a setback from the neighbouring property.A two-storey service annex may also be built without a setback from the neighbour, but a minimum distance of 1.5 metres must then be maintained between the annex and the main villa.If the setback from the neighbouring property is retained, a two-storey annex may be built without a separation gap from the main villa.Alternatively, homeowners may retain a 1.5-metre setback along the neighbouring property and access lane while eliminating the separation between the annex and the villa. Neighbour approval is required where the setback between the service annex and the neighbouring property is removed.The municipality has prohibited the construction of a service annex before the main residential villa.It has also ruled out two-storey service annexes where the main villa consists of a ground floor only.Service annexes must retain a linear or elongated design. Where an annex faces the street, its architectural appearance must complement the main villa and its surroundings, and its frontage must not exceed 30 per cent of the property's street-facing boundary.Windows facing neighbouring properties are prohibited where the annex is built directly against the shared boundary..Dubai approves 44 areas for shared housing buildings and villas, some revealed.Dubai bans mixing families and individuals in shared housing units.Dubai reveals areas where shared housing will be allowed and restricted: Check if yours is on the list.Dubai shared housing law: Who can rent, sublet and face fines of up to Dh1 million

source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 17th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Culture and Arts Authority (Dubai Culture) has opened registration for the 31st International Symposium on Electronic/Emerging Art (ISEA2026 Dubai), taking place from 6th to 15th November 2026 under the theme "ELYAH: Constellating Place, Data and Identity".Set to be the symposium’s largest edition to date, the event will bring together artists, researchers, and innovators from around the world to explore the intersection of art, science, and technology and exchange perspectives on the future of contemporary creative practice.The event supports Dubai Culture’s efforts to advance the digital arts ecosystem, deliver on its Digital Arts Roadmap objectives, and empower local talent. It also reinforces Dubai’s position as a global cultural reference, a leader in innovation, a driver of the creative economy, rooted in Emirati heritage.The symposium combines an in-person Artistic Programme across Dubai with an Online Academic Programme accessible from anywhere in the world. The Online Academic Programme will feature Special Track panels and workshops from 6th to 9th November, followed by the main academic conference sessions from 10th to 14th November 2026.Registration for the artistic programme across Dubai is free, while access to the online academic programme requires a paid ticket. All participants must register and will receive a personal QR code for their exclusive use at artistic programme venues.Access details for the Online Academic Programme will be sent to the email address used to book. Students receive a 50 percent discount when booking with a valid university email address. To register, visit isea2026.eventshub.ai.Maitha Ali Al Blooshi, Director of the Emerging Arts Department at Dubai Culture and Executive Director of ISEA2026, highlighted the symposium’s role in connecting artistic and academic communities and enriching dialogue on the future of digital and emerging arts.She said, “ISEA2026 Dubai offers audiences the opportunity to discover innovative artistic experiences that demonstrate the creative possibilities of technology and engage with new perspectives from artists and researchers around the world. Opening registration invites local talent to learn from these experiences, refine their skills, and expand their professional networks, strengthening their capacity to experiment and innovate."The symposium also reflects Dubai Culture’s commitment to creating an environment that encourages research and collaboration and supports the sustainable growth of digital and emerging arts.”Al Blooshi added that hosting the international symposium reflects Dubai’s global leadership in embracing innovative artistic experiences and its ability to attract creative practitioners, researchers and specialists from diverse cultures.The programme will feature over 100 artworks and 145 academic papers, more than 50 artist talks and panel discussions, and over 10 workshops, over 45 Special Track workshops, panels and presentations, seven Eco Lab workshops and more than 20 institutional presentations within the Online Academic Programme.Exhibitions, live and audio-visual performances, installations, interactive and immersive experiences will take place across Dubai, inviting audiences to engage with works that explore the relationship between people, place and technology.ISEA is one of the world’s leading platforms exploring the relationship between art, science and technology. Its 31st edition will examine four core themes: Charting Constellations, Celestial Dialogues, Eco-Tech Futures and Starlinked Worlds.Charting Constellations focuses on place, digital geographies, identity and community. Celestial Dialogues explores cultural exchange, storytelling and collaboration. Eco-Tech Futures examines environmental responsibility and sustainable technology, while Starlinked Worlds considers the relationship between technology and human experience, including ethical, philosophical and speculative futures.

source_snapshot.title: Najah 2026 to have its largest footprint to date as it expands to Al Ain for first
source_snapshot.text: ABU DHABI, 17th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Najah, the Middle East’s premier higher education fair, is set to open its 20th edition in Abu Dhabi, marking a major milestone in a journey spanning two decades. This year, Najah will have its largest footprint to date as it expands to Al Ain for the first time; a step that reflects its established position as the UAE’s leading higher education event for the past 20 years.The milestone comes at an important time for higher education in the UAE. The sector is growing rapidly, but it is also being reshaped by advances in technology and changing labour-market needs.With demand rising and study choices becoming broader and more varied, Najah 2026 gives students, parents, teachers and counsellors direct access to university admissions teams, scholarship opportunities, academic programme information and practical guidance on studying in the UAE and abroad.With the strategic support of the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research, the Najah 2026 series begins with Najah Abu Dhabi from 18–21 October at ADNEC Centre Abu Dhabi, followed by Najah Dubai from 25–27 October at Dubai World Trade Centre. The inaugural Najah Al Ain will take place on 2 & 3 November at ADNEC Centre Al Ain.As Najah marks two decades, this year’s event will bring together more than 100 universities from over 20 countries, giving students the opportunity to speak directly with admissions representatives and explore undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, scholarships and international study pathways.Najah Abu Dhabi has also been extended to four days in 2026, with a series of enhancements designed specifically to make access easier for school groups and enhance their experience throughout the visit.Dima Al Sadi, Portfolio Manager, Najah Expo, said: “The 20th edition of Najah is an important milestone for us as organisers, but the real significance lies in what those 20 years have meant. Over the years, the event has been a platform for thousands of conversations that have helped students and families make more informed decisions about their future.”She added: “We are seeing a fundamental shift in higher education, and the choices facing students are becoming more complex by the day. Selecting an institution is only part of the decision. Students are also weighing the skills that will prepare them for the future, emerging career opportunities and the global pathways their qualifications can open up. Najah gives them a unique setting to engage directly with leading experts and international education institutions, and to gain the clarity they need to make choices that best suit their educational journey.”The inaugural Najah Al Ain will take place on 2 & 3 November at ADNEC Centre Al Ain, bringing together more than 50 local and international universities. It will give students and parents the opportunity to explore the latest higher education opportunities in the UAE and overseas in person, while accessing trusted guidance on admissions, scholarships and study options.The event will host higher education institutions from more than 10 countries, including the UAE, the United States, Canada, Australia, the United Kingdom, Germany, Spain, Hungary and Malaysia.Al Sadi concluded: “Launching Najah Al Ain is a natural next step in Najah’s growth. The city has a strong student and school community, and bringing universities directly to them makes educational opportunities easier to access. We want students to explore their options, speak to the right people and leave with a clearer sense of what comes next.”

source_snapshot.title: Hamdan bin Mohammed announces SWS Board Technology as winner of Dubai-it Award for projects in field of Economy
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 17th October, 2026 (WAM) -- H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Defence, and Chairman of The Executive Council of Dubai, recognised SWS Board Technology as the winner of the Dubai-it Award in the field of Economy.The project was recognised for successfully developing one of the world’s largest manufacturing operations for snow and water sports boards, leveraging its expertise in composite materials to build an advanced industrial ecosystem in Dubai serving global markets.H.H. Sheikh Hamdan said, “Who would have imagined that one of the world’s largest snowboard manufacturing operations would emerge from a city that was once desert? The Dubai-it Award for Projects in the Field of Economy goes to SWS Board Technology.”He added, “Rainier Nouhra started SWS in Dubai. Today, it produces half of the world’s kiteboards and wakeboards and one-third of its snowboards, with a capacity exceeding 450,000 boards a year. Its products reach global markets, with more than 6 million boards sold. It has earned the trust of leading snow and water sports brands. Its Dubai-made boards have reached the world’s biggest competitions, including the Winter Olympic Games.”H.H. Sheikh Hamdan concluded, “This is Dubai-it, seeing opportunity where others least expect it, and turning it into extraordinary achievement, with excellence in record time. Congratulations to the SWS Board Technology team.”SWS Board Technology manufactures nearly half of the world’s kiteboards and wakeboards, as well as approximately one-third of the world’s snowboards, with an annual capacity exceeding 450,000 boards and its entire output exported to international markets.Rainier Nouhra combined his passion with his expertise in engineering and composite manufacturing to build a global manufacturing business from Dubai. He invested in developing his teams and strengthening their technical capabilities, using research and development to enhance product quality and manufacturing efficiency.Drawing on Dubai’s strategic location, advanced infrastructure and logistics networks, he expanded exports to markets worldwide and built long-term partnerships with leading snow and water sports brands.The company has successfully built an integrated industrial chain covering every stage of production, from research, development, and engineering, through manufacturing and quality control, to global distribution, solidifying its status as the primary partner for leading global brands in snow and water sports.Beyond expanding its production capabilities, the project has pioneered advanced board-manufacturing technologies and developed fully recyclable board programmes capable of reusing around 95 percent of a board’s materials to produce new ones, driving resource efficiency and advancing circular economy principles.Mohammad Abdullah Al Gergawi, Chairman of The Executive Office of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President, Prime Minister and Ruler of Dubai, stated, “Our leadership has taught us that ambition goes beyond geography and convention. Presenting the Dubai-it Award for Projects in the field of Economy to SWS Board Technology recognises that approach. In a field where the region had little presence, the project grew from Dubai to become one of the world’s largest, competing at the highest standards of quality and earning the trust of leading global brands.”He added, “The Dubai-it Award was launched to show the world Dubai’s philosophy of work, embodied in projects and achievements across every sector. What once seemed impossible is now a reality we live and take pride in, here in Dubai, made possible by bold ambition, speed in execution, and excellence in delivery.”The project exemplifies the Dubai-it economic philosophy by translating technical expertise into large-scale industrial capability, capitalising on Dubai’s advanced infrastructure, strategic location, and global connectivity to establish a world-class manufacturing sector.SWS Board Technology’s victory underscores how Dubai provides a fertile environment for ambitious ventures to innovate, scale, and access international markets, demonstrating that advanced manufacturing remains a key driver in boosting the emirate's economic competitiveness as a global hub for business, industry, and innovation.

source_snapshot.title: Liwa International Festival 2027 to take place in Al Dhafra Region
source_snapshot.text: ABU DHABI, 18th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Under the patronage of H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Ruler’s Representative in Al Dhafra Region, Liwa International Festival 2027 (Liwa 2027) will take place from 11th December 2026 to 2nd January 2027 at Liwa desert in Al Dhafra Region. The festival will feature a reimagined Liwa Village, a new international entertainment show, motorsport championships, heritage experiences and family activities.Liwa International Festival 2027 is organised by the Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi (DCT Abu Dhabi) in collaboration with Liwa Sports Club, Al Dhafra Municipality, Abu Dhabi Police, Abu Dhabi Media Network, Abu Dhabi Sports Council, Abu Dhabi Heritage Authority, and Al Dhafra Hospitals - Seha.Held around Tal Moreeb, the UAE's tallest dune at more than 300 metres, the festival has evolved over more than two decades, since 2001, bringing together Emirati heritage, sport, entertainment and family-friendly activities. Last year, the festival welcomed more than 700,000 visitors over 23 days and received the Best Festival of the Year award at the Middle East Events Awards 2026.Liwa Village returns at the heart of the festival, with more than half of its rides and attractions either new or reimagined this year. New experiences include the Circus Swinger, Tagada and Space Tower, alongside activities such as Play Strike, Ninja Challenge, Pixel Run and Desert Heist, Drift Trike, Target Shooting and Climb Quest.The Bungee Jump will also make its debut, while returning attractions include the Ferris Wheel, Bumper Cars, Slingshot, Booster, Classic Cars, Go Water Kart, Mini Tank Paint Ball, House of Horror, Maze Adventure and 4x4 Track.Nitro Circus will make its festival debut on 19th to 20th December 2026, with 15+ athletes performing freestyle motocross (FMX), bicycle motocross (BMX), choreographed performances and pyrotechnics across three shows.Organised by Liwa Sports Club, the festival will feature motorsport and desert sports competitions, including Freestyle Display (11-12 and 21-22 December 2026), Motorbike Drag Race (13th December 2026), Falcon Race (14-16 December 2026), Sand Freestyle Display (18th-19th and 27th-28th December 2026), Liwa UTV Track (20 December 2026), Traditional Pigeon Race (22-23 December 2026), Liwa Burnout Challenge (24 December 2026) and Liwa Drift (25th-26th December 2026).The programme will culminate in the Tal Moreeb Car Championship finale, from 30th December - 2nd January 2027.Visitors can also participate in sporting and fitness activities including the Liwa Sign Climb Challenge (19 December 2026), a cycling race (21st December 2026), the Liwa Festival Community Run (23rd December 2026), a padel tournament (24th–25th December 2026) and a fitness tour (29 December).Liwa International Festival 2027 continues to celebrate Emirati heritage and traditions. Presented by Abu Dhabi Heritage Authority, the Heritage Village, inspired by a traditional Emirati neighbourhood (Al Fareej), will offer demonstrations and hands-on activities introducing families and younger generations to traditional Emirati life, customs and practices.The House of Poetry and Poets will introduce visitors to Nabati poetry and its role in expressing community values, experiences and traditions.Visitors can learn about falconry at the Falconry Tent through live displays and demonstrations covering the raising, training and care of falcons, and the tools used in the practice. Young visitors can also take part in workshops to make model falcon hoods.The traditional games and heritage experiences area features interactive activities suitable for different ages, including Teelah and Karabi, tug of war, camel riding, a palm-climbing simulation, and workshops in making palm-leaf products (khoos) and weaving.The Emirati Majlis will introduce visitors to Emirati social etiquette, including entering, greeting, seating, welcoming guests and honouring them, highlighting the role of the majlis in preserving customs across generations.Visitors can also learn about Emirati Gahwa presentation, serving traditions and the etiquette of Emirati hospitality through a live workshop.Beyond the main festival site, activations across Al Dhafra Region will include the Liwa Sign landmark, retail and dining at Dhafeer Fort, Al Meel Fort and Al Yabana Fort, traditional Emirati crafts at Khanour Fort, and a cultural experience at Mezairaa Fort inspired by Liwa’s history and heritage.The festival’s first official app will also be launched, allowing visitors to explore the event calendar, stay up to date with the latest announcements, select and book camping spots and RV parking spaces, and explore commercial participation opportunities at the festival.

source_snapshot.title: UAE schools reopen on Monday after mid-term break: What parents need to know
source_snapshot.text: Abu Dhabi: Thousands of students across the UAE will return to classrooms on Monday, October 19, following the first-term mid-term break, as public and private schools that observed the holiday resume lessons and turn their attention to academic assessments and preparations for the remainder of the term.The return marks the end of a week-long break that began on October 12 under the academic calendar for 2026–2027..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..However, reopening dates may differ among private schools following other curricula, depending on their approved academic calendars and the requirements of the relevant local education authorities.The Ministry of Education's academic calendar sets out the school year for public schools and private institutions following its curriculum, while allowing some flexibility for other private schools.Focus shifts to academic performanceWith students returning to classrooms, schools face the task of identifying learning gaps, reviewing assessment results and providing additional support to pupils who have fallen behind.The remaining weeks of the term offer an opportunity to assess how well students have mastered the material covered so far, rather than simply completing the prescribed lessons.Schools will also need to monitor attendance, evaluate the effectiveness of academic support and keep parents informed about their children's progress.Identifying pupils who need additional help, providing targeted interventions and measuring improvements will be among the priorities as the first term moves towards its final assessments.Clear communication with families will also be important, particularly when explaining assessment results and the steps needed to improve academic performance.Do all private schools return on October 19?The Ministry of Education's calendar applies to public schools and private schools following the ministry curriculum.However, local education authorities may approve exceptions for private schools operating other curricula, allowing them to split their mid-term break between October and February according to their operational requirements.The total break under this arrangement must not exceed five school days. Private schools in Sharjah are subject to separate regulatory arrangements.Parents whose children attend schools following international or other non-ministry curricula should therefore check their school's approved calendar to confirm the return date.When is the next UAE school holiday?Under the approved 2026–2027 academic calendar, the next major break will be the winter holiday, beginning on December 14, 2026.Students will return to school on Monday, January 4, 2027, after the holiday ends on January 3.The spring break will run from April 5 to April 11, 2027, with classes resuming on April 12.The final school day of the academic year is scheduled for July 2, 2027.The current school year began on August 31, 2026.UAE school calendar for 2027–2028The Ministry of Education has also announced the academic calendar for the following two years, giving schools and families greater certainty when planning holidays and other commitments.The 2027–2028 academic year will begin on August 30, 2027.The first-term mid-term break will run from October 11 to 17, with students returning on October 18.The winter holiday will begin on December 13, 2027, and end on January 2, 2028, with classes resuming on January 3.Spring break will take place from March 27 to April 2, 2028, followed by a return to classrooms on April 3.The academic year will end on June 30, 2028.UAE school calendar for 2028–2029The following academic year will begin on August 28, 2028.The first mid-term break is scheduled from October 16 to 22, with classes resuming on October 23.The winter holiday will run from December 11, 2028, to January 1, 2029, followed by the return of students on January 2.Spring break is scheduled for late March and the beginning of April, with students returning on April 2, 2029.The final day of the academic year will be June 29, 2029.Why the three-year calendar mattersThe Ministry of Education introduced the three-year academic calendar to provide a more predictable schedule for schools, teachers, students and parents.The framework establishes the beginning and end of each school year, major holidays and assessment periods, supporting advance planning and continuity in education.It is also intended to balance classroom instruction with scheduled breaks, giving schools a consistent structure for delivering the curriculum and monitoring student progress..No October source_snapshot.title: Schneider Electric delivers energy, digital backbone of Skyports Infrastructure's VDX, world's first purpose-built commercial vertiport in Dubai
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 19th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Schneider Electric, a global energy technology leader, has successfully supported Skyports Infrastructure, a global leader in vertiport infrastructure for electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, in delivering the electrical and digital backbone of VDX, the world's first purpose-built commercial vertiport, by Dubai International Airport.The vertiport, which reached technical completion in April 2026, and was certified for eVTOL operations in July 2026, is the first and flagship vertiport in Dubai's planned air taxi network. Further vertiports are in development at Dubai Marina, Downtown Dubai, and Palm Jumeirah.Designed to handle up to 170,000 passengers a year, it represents a new class of transportation. This new class of transportation calls for a new class of energy infrastructure: high-power charging that keeps Joby Aviation’s aircraft ready between flights, electrical systems engineered to aviation-grade safety standards, and real-time intelligence connecting power, charging, and building systems across the facility.Schneider Electric partnered with Skyports to engineer the energy and digital backbone that makes this possible. The architecture spans digital low-voltage switchboards, a building management system, EcoStruxure Power Operation at VDX integrated with the Dubai Marina Vertiport, ION9000 power quality monitoring, connected power meters, capacitor banks, and Galaxy UPS protecting critical systems.Every element serves one of three outcomes:Operational resilience keeps the vertiport flight-ready, with real-time visibility into the health of critical power and building systems so potential issues are addressed before they reach operations.Energy intelligence optimises consumption across the facility and enables aircraft charging that adapts dynamically to demand.Network scalability turns the vertiport into a blueprint: a standardised digital architecture that shares infrastructure status automatically with flight scheduling and charging systems, and can be replicated at every station that follows.Once the site is fully operational, Schneider Electric's solutions are expected to deliver energy savings of up to 25% across the facility.The project supports the Dubai 2040 Urban Master Plan and its 20-Minute City policy, which envisions a city where residents reach most of their daily destinations within 20 minutes. Journeys that take 45 minutes by road are expected to take approximately 12 minutes by air, placing Dubai among the first cities in the world to make electric air travel part of everyday urban mobility.“Charging electric aircraft creates some pretty significant and rapidly changing power demands,” said Gareth Wilson, General Manager, Dubai, Skyports Infrastructure. “At the same time, the terminal and all of its critical systems need to stay fully operational.We chose Schneider Electric to provide us with power infrastructure that is resilient, responsive and intelligent. Most importantly, the scalable approach gives us something we can replicate across the wider Dubai network. As we continue to add more vertiports, it provides us with a baseline that we can confidently continue to roll out.”"Our collaboration with Skyports Infrastructure marks a significant step towards redefining the future of urban mobility," said Amel Chadli, Gulf Cluster and Countries President at Schneider Electric."The vertiport at Dubai International Airport, VDX, reflects Dubai's position as a global leader in adopting the technologies that will define the next generation of transport. As Skyports' energy technology partner, our role is to provide the energy and digital infrastructure that enables safe, reliable and efficient operations from day one, with an architecture built to scale as the network expands across the city."

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Municipality introduces smart navigation system with audio for visually impaired people
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Dubai Municipality has become the first government entity in the UAE to introduce NaviLens, a smart navigation system that helps people who are visually impaired find their way around public spaces and access information independently, the civic body revealed on Monday.The technology is among the highlights Dubai Municipality is showcasing at the eighth edition of AccessAbilities Expo, running from October 19 to 21, 2026, at Dubai World Trade Centre.It appears alongside accessible beaches, sensory rooms, a workplace inclusion programme and a new partnership with the Emirates Down Syndrome Association..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..How NaviLens worksNaviLens uses digitally encoded coloured markers that can be detected through smartphone cameras, giving users immediate audio and text-based guidance.The system supports more than 35 languages, making navigation and information services accessible to a wider range of people.Dubai Municipality says the move reflects its efforts to adopt assistive technologies that address different accessibility needs and improve the experience of using public facilities..Bader Anwahi, CEO of the Public Facilities Agency at Dubai Municipality, said: "Universal accessibility is a fundamental consideration in how we plan, develop and manage Dubai's public facilities. Our responsibility extends beyond providing accessible infrastructure to ensuring that public spaces and services respond to the different needs of the people who use them. This requires an integrated approach that brings together inclusive design, assistive technologies and the continuous improvement of facilities and services."Beaches and sensory roomsBeach accessibility is another focus of the Municipality's stand. Its accessible beach infrastructure includes sea swimming platforms at Jumeirah Beach 2 and Khor Al Mamzar, along with 10 accessible entrances and pathways to the sea, dedicated parking spaces for People of Determination across all beaches and 16 accessible restrooms.Floating wheelchairs for swimming and specialised beach wheelchairs are also available, helping People of Determination enjoy Dubai's coastal destinations safely and independently.The Municipality is also showcasing its sensory rooms across Dubai's parks and beaches, including a dedicated facility at Jumeirah Beach 2.Designed to accommodate different sensory needs, these spaces offer supportive environments that enhance comfort, wellbeing and the overall visitor experience.The accessibility enhancements at Jumeirah Beach 2 have also earned the destination the Gold Classification from the World Disability Union (WDU), recognising its inclusive facilities for People of Determination..Inclusion at work and in the communityAt the expo, Dubai Municipality is marking the graduation of the first and second cohorts of its Inclusion Coordinators Programme. The programme equips participants with the knowledge and practical skills needed to support the inclusion of People of Determination in the workplace, promotes greater awareness of accessibility requirements and helps create an environment where they can participate effectively and develop professionally.Community members are being encouraged to play a part too, through the Municipality's 'Access Ambassadors' initiative. It raises awareness of universal accessibility requirements under the Dubai Building Code and guides People of Determination and building owners towards the Municipality's 'Wusool' service. It also gives residents a chance to propose ideas and practical solutions to accessibility challenges.The Municipality is further showcasing emergency evacuation and safety systems designed to accommodate the needs of People of Determination, supporting safer evacuation procedures in buildings and public facilities.New partnership and global recognitionOn the sidelines of AccessAbilities Expo 2026, Dubai Municipality signed a cooperation agreement with the Emirates Down Syndrome Association to strengthen collaboration on universal accessibility and the inclusion of People of Determination.The agreement will support efforts to enhance accessibility and inclusive design across the Municipality's facilities, services, programmes and communication channels. It will also provide a framework for joint sports, recreational, cultural and community initiatives for People of Determination and their families.A key part of the cooperation will involve drawing on the Association's specialised expertise and the experiences of People of Determination to evaluate accessibility solutions, test services and identify opportunities for improvement.Dubai Municipality's accessibility achievements also include a Guinness World Record, received in 2023, for the world's longest Braille handrail at Dubai Frame, measuring 319 metres and 11 centimetres. Its own stand at this year's expo, which features wide tactile pathways and accessible facilities, has received a Certificate of Achievement for its inclusive design.Anwahi added: "AccessAbilities Expo provides an important opportunity to exchange expertise, engage with People of Determination and strengthen collaboration with organisations working to advance universal accessibility. We recognise that developing an inclusive urban environment requires ongoing engagement, practical solutions and a clear understanding of users' experiences. Through these partnerships and initiatives, we aim to continue raising accessibility standards across Dubai's public facilities and contribute to the Emirate's position as a city friendly to People of Determination.".Watch: Dubai's Jumeirah Beach 2 turns 'Gold' with a sensory room. What's it?.Dubai Frame, Children's City and these Dubai parks are now officially special. Here is why.Dubai Municipality unveils new map of 16,000 accessible facilities for People of Determination.90% of Dubai’s beaches and 80% of public parks now fully accessible

source_snapshot.title: A new high for adventure seekers as Bungee at Yas Bay opens on Yas Island
source_snapshot.text: ABU DHABI, 19th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Adventure seekers now have a brand-new reason to visit Yas Island as Bungee at Yas Bay officially opens at Yas Bay Waterfront on Nov 1,2026. Launching from a 50-metre platform overlooking the waterfront, the new attraction delivers a thrilling experience that combines breathtaking views, adrenaline-fuelled excitement and an unforgettable challenge, adding another must-try experience to Yas Island's growing portfolio of world-class attractions.Whether guests are looking to push their limits, tick off a bucket-list experience or simply see Yas Bay Waterfront from a completely new perspective, Bungee at Yas Bay offers an exhilarating journey from start to finish. Operated by Warrior Group and designed to the highest safety standards, the attraction combines the excitement of a controlled free-fall with spectacular waterfront views, creating a memorable experience for first-time jumpers and adrenaline enthusiasts alike.Jonathan Brown, Chief Portfolio Officer, Miral, said: “The opening of Bungee at Yas Bay adds an exhilarating new dimension to Yas Island’s expanding portfolio of world-class experiences. It reflects our ongoing efforts to create joyful and unforgettable moments for our guests, while reinforcing Yas Island’s position as a leading global destination for entertainment and leisure.”“We are delighted to partner with Miral to bring this new adventure experience to Yas Bay. At Warrior Group, we are passionate about creating experiences that bring people together, inspire them to try something new and add value to the destinations we design, build and operate in. The Bungee at Yas Bay is an exciting addition to Abu Dhabi’s leisure offering. With its spectacular waterfront setting and views, this new attraction offers residents and visitors a unique opportunity to experience Yas Bay from a whole new perspective,” Troy Gillham, Founder and CEO, Warrior Group.The experience is open to guests aged 16 and above, with a permitted weight range of 40–105kg. A professional crew will prepare guests for the leap with a safety briefing and equipment checks before each jump. Participation is subject to health and eligibility requirements, with full details available at https://abu-dhabi.platinumlist.net/event-tickets/bungee-at-yas-bay.
