source_snapshot.title: UAE school photo ban: Parents and educators back children’s privacy safeguards
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Parents taking photographs or videos of children on school premises without consent could face fines of up to Dh500,000 under UAE privacy laws if a complaint is raised with the authorities and the conduct is found to constitute an offence, legal experts have said.The clarification comes after schools in Dubai and Sharjah issued circulars asking parents and visitors not to photograph or film students on campus, or share images containing other children through WhatsApp groups, social media or other digital platforms without appropriate consent.While photographs help families preserve memories of school performances, celebrations and other milestones, educators say children’s privacy and dignity must remain a priority, particularly when images can be circulated beyond their intended audience..Nevita Pandya MBE, CEO and Principal of GEMS International School – Dubai Hills, believes clear guidelines help children participate in school life without feeling pressured to have their images captured or shared.She explains, "Children should be able to participate fully in school life without their images being captured or circulated without appropriate permission." As she adds, a photograph can reveal more than we realise, including a child’s school, location or routine. "Clear guidelines establish that children’s privacy and dignity come before an adult’s wish to record or share a moment.”She adds that schools and parents should also consider children’s own preferences. “Alongside parental permission, we should listen to children’s views in an age-appropriate way and respect their discomfort. Their participation in school life should never depend on agreeing to publicity.”.Why sharing school photographs can be riskyEven when photographs are shared in familiar WhatsApp groups, parents may have little control over where the images go next.“It is essential. A familiar WhatsApp group can feel private, but images can still be saved, forwarded or shared beyond the intended audience,” Pandya says.Before sharing a photograph, she advises parents to consider whose children are visible, whether permission covers that use and whether the image reveals personal information. “Permission to take a photograph should not be assumed to include permission to publish it.”Dr Ghadeer Abu-Shamat, Principal of Al Khaleej International School, says children’s images should be treated with the same care as other personal information."Once an image is shared, especially online, it can be difficult to control who has access to it or how it may be used in the future. Being mindful helps protect children's safety, dignity, and privacy.”.She adds that knowing photographs of her child are not circulated without her knowledge gives families greater peace of mind.“It gives families greater control over their child's digital footprint and reduces the risk of images being viewed, copied, or shared beyond the intended audience. It also demonstrates respect for parental choice and children's privacy rights.”.Parents call for a balance between privacy and sharing memoriesWhile supporting safeguards around children's images, parent Suad Saleh, whose child attends GEMS International School, believes the rules should encourage responsible behaviour rather than prevent families from sharing every photograph.“If it’s a photo of your own children, with no other children visible in the background, and it’s an appropriate and respectful photo, I don’t necessarily see any harm in sharing it. I think the important thing is also to be mindful of who you are sharing it with and the privacy of your children.”For Saleh, “it’s about using good judgment rather than saying that parents should never photograph or share pictures of their children.”She believes the guidelines should focus on educating parents about responsible sharing.“I think that the rules should emphasise more to educate and encourage responsible behaviour rather than simply restrict parents completely.”Dr Abu-Shamat says the rules can encourage parents to consider the consequences before posting or forwarding images.“These rules encourage parents to pause and consider the implications before posting or forwarding images. source_snapshot.title: UAE bans use of popular antibiotic for pets and farm animals from November 1
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: The UAE is banning the use of ciprofloxacin, a popular antibiotic, in its veterinary sector from November 1, 2026, in a move aimed at tackling antimicrobial resistance.The Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) on Tuesday announced that the ban covers veterinary medicinal products and raw materials containing ciprofloxacin.It affects nine veterinary products, including eight imported products and one locally registered product.Ciprofloxacin belongs to the fluoroquinolone group of antibiotics. It is a strong antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..Why the ban?The decision is part of efforts to promote the safe use of antibiotics and preserve the effectiveness of treatments used in human medicine. It follows the classification of this group of antibiotics as Critically Important Antimicrobials (CIAs) for human medicine because of their role in treating certain bacterial infections.Inappropriate use in animals could contribute to the development of bacterial resistance, potentially reducing the effectiveness of available treatments and posing a public health challenge.The ban follows a scientific assessment of data related to antimicrobial resistance, including studies submitted by UAE University. The findings were used to support evidence-based regulatory decisions and strengthen national efforts to reduce the risks associated with antimicrobial resistance..Risk-based approachDr Ruqaya Aqeel Al Bastaki, Acting Executive Director of the Medical Products Regulation Sector at the Emirates Drug Establishment, said regulating the use of antimicrobials requires an approach based on assessing the risks associated with each substance and how those risks affect treatment priorities across different sectors.She explained that scientific evidence plays a key role in determining the appropriate level of regulatory intervention, allowing the establishment to take necessary measures when findings point to risks that require action, taking into account the nature of each substance and its uses.Al Bastaki added that the establishment is committed to keeping its decisions aligned with the latest scientific developments and responding proactively to risks linked to antimicrobial resistance. . These efforts aim to preserve the effectiveness of available treatments, strengthen pharmaceutical security, ensure the sustainability of medical products and protect public health.The decision falls within the Emirates Drug Establishment's mandate to regulate the use of medical and pharmaceutical products and monitor compliance with the relevant approved requirements.What companies must doAhead of the ban's implementation, the establishment has taken the necessary regulatory steps to identify the products and raw materials covered by the decision.It has notified the relevant establishments that they must stop manufacturing, importing and supplying these products, withdraw existing quantities from the local market before the ban takes effect, and either re-export or dispose of remaining stocks in accordance with approved procedures.Establishments must also submit supporting documents confirming that the required measures have been completed.EDE is also preparing a monitoring plan to assess compliance with the decision and verify that the relevant establishments complete the required procedures within the specified timeframe.The decision was taken as part of the Emirates Drug Establishment's efforts to strengthen oversight of veterinary medical products, promote the responsible use of antimicrobials and support national initiatives to combat antimicrobial resistance, helping protect human and animal health while strengthening the UAE's public health system, EDE said..UAE recalls two 'Goodbye All Insects' insecticide products.UAE announces new mechanism to end monopoly of medicines.FNC calls for lower drug prices, publication of banned medicines .UAE enacts law to regulate veterinary medicines and enhance food safety

source_snapshot.title: Sharjah introduces motorcycle parking for first time in Al Yarmook
source_snapshot.text: Sharjah: Sharjah has rolled out dedicated motorcycle parking in Al Yarmook for the first time, alongside 4,160 paid parking spaces, 53 roads and new recreational facilities as part of a major infrastructure upgrade.Sharjah City Municipality has completed the project to upgrade roads, pavements and parking facilities in the area in seven and a half months, ahead of the original one-year contractual deadline. The development was carried out under the directives of His Highness Sheikh Dr Sultan bin Mohammed Al Qasimi, Supreme Council Member and Ruler of Sharjah.Covering 185,000 square metres, the project aims to improve residents’ quality of life, ease movement around the neighbourhood, enhance road safety and give Al Yarmook a more organised urban appearance..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..The improvements also include a new 5,400 square metre park, 280 newly planted trees, 227 energy-efficient streetlights, 32 pedestrian benches and an integrated camera surveillance system.Dedicated motorcycle parking introducedFor the first time across Sharjah, dedicated motorcycle parking spaces have been introduced as part of the Al Yarmook development project, providing designated areas for riders and helping improve parking management across the emirate.The initiative forms part of a wider effort to organise parking, reduce random parking and make it easier for residents and visitors to find designated spaces.The project also created and prepared 4,160 paid parking spaces along roadsides and in internal open areas. The spaces are intended to improve vehicle parking arrangements and make more efficient use of available land.53 roads and improved infrastructureThe project covered a total area of 185,000 square metres and included the construction of 53 roads covering 56,876 square metres, with a combined length of approximately nine kilometres.It also involved the development and maintenance of the internal road network, as well as 41 lanes, passages and pedestrian pavements covering more than 31,320 square metres.Infrastructure works included electricity, water and gas lines, telecommunications networks, sewage systems and rainwater drainage facilities. The project also focused on organising utility routes, improving connectivity between buildings and public facilities, and making movement through the neighbourhood easier for residents and visitors.Sewage and rainwater drainage works have been completed in full, covering 14,800 linear metres.Quality control measures included reviewing detailed network plans, checking the quality of construction materials, monitoring implementation, testing the networks, verifying levels and inspecting rainwater inlets, manholes and associated structures.The municipality also cleaned and levelled 36 plots of land covering approximately 31,000 square metres. Some of these plots were earmarked for smart parking facilities, while others were designated for school buses.The work has improved the appearance of the neighbourhood while allowing better use of available land..New parks and more green spacesThe municipality has expanded recreational facilities in Al Yarmook with the development of a 5,400 square metre park featuring a shaded children's play area, a football pitch, visitor seating and an office for security and park supervision.A second, smaller park was also created, with its design incorporating an existing mature ghaf tree to preserve it. The park includes a children's play area and family seating, providing an additional community space for residents.The municipality also planted 280 sea hibiscus trees, alongside other flowering species, along the main roads to enhance Al Yarmook’s urban landscape and expand its green spaces. The project also included maintaining existing landscaped areas to preserve greenery and improve the neighbourhood’s overall appearance.Free permits for building façade improvementsImproving the appearance of buildings was another key part of the development.Engineer Faisal Al Mulla, Director of the General Services Department at Sharjah City Municipality and head of the project team, said the municipality established a specialised team to monitor building façades alongside the main construction team.The initiative covered more than 535 buildings, and maintenance permits were issued for 231 of them.All permits issued to property owners for modifying or maintaining building façades were provided free of charge, easing the process of repainting buildings and removing features that detract from the area's overall appearance.The initiative is intended to improve the urban landscape while preserving the neighbourhood's aesthetic character.Dedicated centre for municipal inspectorsUnder the directives of the Ruler of Sharjah, a plot of land was allocated for a dedicated building to serve as a base for municipal inspectors carrying out field duties in the area.The facility has been completed and fully equipped in accordance with the required specifications and standards.Inspectors will use the centre as a starting point for monitoring public cleanliness, the area's overall appearance, building façades, shop signs and other signage, as well as carrying out other duties within their responsibilities..227 streetlights and surveillance camerasThe project included the installation of 227 energy efficient streetlights and 32 benches along pedestrian pavements to improve safety and comfort for residents and visitors.An integrated camera surveillance system was also established to strengthen security and safety throughout the area.Project completed ahead of scheduleAl Mulla said the project was completed in seven and a half months through advance planning, coordinated implementation and cooperation among the government entities involved.Although the original contractual period was one year, the work was organised according to an ambitious eight months schedule to minimise disruption and complete the improvements as quickly as possible.The neighbourhood was divided into seven work zones, allowing construction to proceed in phases while keeping parts of the area accessible to residents and shop owners. This approach helped avoid a complete closure of the neighbourhood and reduced the impact of construction on daily life and business activity.The project was carried out in collaboration with the Sharjah Roads and Transport Authority, the Department of Planning and Survey, the Directorate of Public Works, Sharjah Police General Command, and the Sharjah Electricity, Water and Gas Authority.The Roads and Transport Authority was involved from the early stages, reviewing the works, monitoring implementation and overseeing quality to ensure compliance with approved technical specifications and standards.The project began with the approval of infrastructure plans and the issuance of the required certificates and permits, followed by the implementation and inspection of the works.The municipality said the improvements are intended to provide an integrated, safe and sustainable urban environment, improve access throughout Al Yarmook and enhance the daily experience of residents and visitors. Sharjah: Sharjah has rolled out dedicated motorcycle parking in Al Yarmook for the first time, alongside 4,160 paid parking spaces, 53 roads and new recreational facilities as part of a major infrastructure upgrade.Sharjah City Municipality has completed the project to upgrade roads, pavements and parking facilities in the area in seven and a half months, ahead of the original one-year contractual deadline.

The development was carried out under the directives of His Highness Sheikh Dr Sultan bin Mohammed Al Qasimi, Supreme Council Member and Ruler of Sharjah.Covering 185,000 square metres, the project aims to improve residents’ quality of life, ease movement around the neighbourhood, enhance road safety and give Al Yarmook a more organised urban appearance..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..The improvements also include a new 5,400 square metre park, 280 newly planted trees, 227 energy-efficient streetlights, 32 pedestrian benches and an integrated camera surveillance system.Dedicated motorcycle parking introducedFor the first time across Sharjah, dedicated motorcycle parking spaces have been introduced as part of the Al Yarmook development project, providing designated areas for riders and helping improve parking management across the emirate.The initiative forms part of a wider effort to organise parking, reduce random parking and make it easier for residents and visitors to find designated spaces.The project also created and prepared 4,160 paid parking spaces along roadsides and in internal open areas.

The spaces are intended to improve vehicle parking arrangements and make more efficient use of available land.53 roads and improved infrastructureThe project covered a total area of 185,000 square metres and included the construction of 53 roads covering 56,876 square metres, with a combined length of approximately nine kilometres.It also involved the development and maintenance of the internal road network, as well as 41 lanes, passages and pedestrian pavements covering more than 31,320 square metres.Infrastructure works included electricity, water and gas lines, telecommunications networks, sewage systems and rainwater drainage facilities.

The project also focused on organising utility routes, improving connectivity between buildings and public facilities, and making movement through the neighbourhood easier for residents and visitors.Sewage and rainwater drainage works have been completed in full, covering 14,800 linear metres.Quality control measures included reviewing detailed network plans, checking the quality of construction materials, monitoring implementation, testing the networks, verifying levels and inspecting rainwater inlets, manholes and associated structures.The municipality also cleaned and levelled 36 plots of land covering approximately 31,000 square metres.

Some of these plots were earmarked for smart parking facilities, while others were designated for school buses.The work has improved the appearance of the neighbourhood while allowing better use of available land..New parks and more green spacesThe municipality has expanded recreational facilities in Al Yarmook with the development of a 5,400 square metre park featuring a shaded children's play area, a football pitch, visitor seating and an office for security and park supervision.A second, smaller park was also created, with its design incorporating an existing mature ghaf tree to preserve it.

The park includes a children's play area and family seating, providing an additional community space for residents.The municipality also planted 280 sea hibiscus trees, alongside other flowering species, along the main roads to enhance Al Yarmook’s urban landscape and expand its green spaces.

The project also included maintaining existing landscaped areas to preserve greenery and improve the neighbourhood’s overall appearance.Free permits for building façade improvementsImproving the appearance of buildings was another key part of the development.Engineer Faisal Al Mulla, Director of the General Services Department at Sharjah City Municipality and head of the project team, said the municipality established a specialised team to monitor building façades alongside the main construction team.The initiative covered more than 535 buildings, and maintenance permits were issued for 231 of them.All permits issued to property owners for modifying or maintaining building façades were provided free of charge, easing the process of repainting buildings and removing features that detract from the area's overall appearance.The initiative is intended to improve the urban landscape while preserving the neighbourhood's aesthetic character.Dedicated centre for municipal inspectorsUnder the directives of the Ruler of Sharjah, a plot of land was allocated for a dedicated building to serve as a base for municipal inspectors carrying out field duties in the area.The facility has been completed and fully equipped in accordance with the required specifications and standards.Inspectors will use the centre as a starting point for monitoring public cleanliness, the area's overall appearance, building façades, shop signs and other signage, as well as carrying out other duties within their responsibilities..227 streetlights and surveillance camerasThe project included the installation of 227 energy efficient streetlights and 32 benches along pedestrian pavements to improve safety and comfort for residents and visitors.An integrated camera surveillance system was also established to strengthen security and safety throughout the area.Project completed ahead of scheduleAl Mulla said the project was completed in seven and a half months through advance planning, coordinated implementation and cooperation among the government entities involved.Although the original contractual period was one year, the work was organised according to an ambitious eight months schedule to minimise disruption and complete the improvements as quickly as possible.The neighbourhood was divided into seven work zones, allowing construction to proceed in phases while keeping parts of the area accessible to residents and shop owners.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai sets new speed limits on five roads under traffic safety drive
source_snapshot.text: Dubai's traffic authorities are reducing the speed limits on three roads and increasing them on two others, as part of the Dubai Traffic Safety Strategy. The changes have been authorised by the emirate's Roads and Transport Authority and Dubai Police. The speed limit has been raised from 60kph to 70kph on Al Mustaqbal Street, between Sheikh Rashid Street and Al Meydan Street, and on Latifa bint Hamdan Street, between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road. On Al Asayel Street, between Oud Metha Street and Al Meydan Street, the limit will be increased from 60kph to 80kph. The limit on Al Rebat Street, between Marrakech Street and Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Road, will be reduced from 100kph to 90kph, and from 80kph to 70kph on Sheikh Sabah Al Ahmad Al Jaber Al Sabah Street, between 2nd December Street and Khalid bin Al Waleed Street. The changes will come into effect from November 1 and are in line with a major drive by Dubai transport authorities to boost road safety and improve traffic flow to keep pace with the needs of a growing population.

source_snapshot.title: UAE’s new 68km E-911 highway to link Dubai-Sharjah border with Ras Al Khaimah
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: The Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure has invited engineering consultancy firms to bid for the study and design of the Fourth Federal Highway Corridor (E-911), a proposed 68-kilometre road linking the Dubai-Sharjah border to Ras Al Khaimah.The ministry said in a post on X that only Category A consultancy firms are eligible to apply for the contract, which covers engineering studies, design and optional supervision services..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..Tender No. 2026-022 was issued on October 15, with interested firms required to submit their bids by Friday, October 23.According to details published on the ministry's website, the proposed highway will extend from the Dubai-Sharjah border to Al Shuhada Road in Ras Al Khaimah.The project also includes an eight-kilometre connecting road linking the new corridor to Emirates Road (E-611) in Umm Al Quwain.The highway will feature between 12 and 16 lanes in both directions combined, with the number of lanes varying along different sections of the route.The tender represents a step towards developing the project, with consultants expected to undertake the technical studies and engineering designs required before construction.The ministry has not disclosed the project's estimated construction cost or implementation timetable.Dubai's 80km Fourth Corridor projectThe tender comes a month after Dubai announced a separate 80-kilometre Fourth Corridor project in September, aimed at strengthening the emirate's road network and improving connectivity between Sharjah, Dubai and Abu Dhabi.The first phase, estimated to cost Dh3.5 billion, will extend from Al Shanouf Road in Sharjah to Dubai-Al Ain Road. The second phase will continue from Dubai-Al Ain Road to Al Faya Road in Abu Dhabi.While the federal E-911 project will provide a new road connection between the Dubai-Sharjah border and Ras Al Khaimah, Dubai's Fourth Corridor project is designed to improve transport links towards Abu Dhabi.Both developments are intended to expand road capacity and strengthen connectivity between the emirates..Dubai’s new 80km road project explained: Route, traffic cuts and what’s being built.Dubai's Dh750 million Emirates Road project reaches 30 per cent completion, cutting journey times by 65 per cent.Dubai approves 80km Fourth Corridor to cut travel time.How a Dh6 billion highway will change travel in the UAE

source_snapshot.title: Dubai tenants warned: Read rental contracts carefully
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Signing a tenancy contract without reading the fine print could land tenants and landlords in costly legal disputes, Dubai’s Rental Disputes Center (RDC) has warned.The centre has urged residents and business owners to carefully review every clause of their rental agreements before signing, particularly those relating to rent payments, financial guarantees, contract renewal and eviction.The warning follows a number of rental disputes involving overlooked contractual conditions, undocumented agreements and verbal promises that were never formally recorded.MisunderstandingsAccording to the RDC, such misunderstandings can result in financial claims, compensation demands and even eviction proceedings.Highlighting the risks, the centre cited the case of a tenant who became involved in a legal dispute with his landlord just months after starting a commercial activity. The disagreement arose over payment arrangements and financial guarantees included in the tenancy contract.The tenant referred to separate arrangements made with the landlord. However, these had not been formally documented.As the dispute escalated, the written tenancy agreement became central to the case because it clearly outlined the obligations accepted by both parties.The RDC said the undocumented arrangements lacked sufficient supporting evidence before the relevant authority.Fine print mattersThe centre explained that many rental disputes arise not from deliberate wrongdoing but from tenants or landlords rushing to sign agreements without fully understanding their legal implications.It advised both parties to pay particular attention to payment deadlines, contractual penalties, eviction provisions and the conditions governing renewal or termination.Even a seemingly minor clause could have significant financial or legal consequences if a disagreement arises later.Ejari registrationThe RDC also reminded landlords and tenants of the importance of registering tenancy contracts through Dubai’s Ejari system.Registration provides an officially recognised record of the rental relationship and helps protect the rights of both parties.Failure to register a tenancy agreement may create procedural difficulties when seeking to enforce certain rights or obligations through official channels.The centre also advised landlords and tenants to retain copies of correspondence, notices and other documents relating to their rental arrangements.Any changes to the original agreement, including revised payment schedules or additional conditions, should be formally documented rather than left to verbal understandings.The RDC stressed that a successful rental relationship begins before a tenant receives the keys or starts occupying a property.What tenants should check before signing Rent payments: Confirm amounts, deadlines and payment arrangements.Financial guarantees: Understand deposits and other financial commitments.Renewal and termination: Check notice periods and relevant conditions.Penalties: Review any charges for breaching contractual terms.Ejari registration: Ensure the tenancy contract is officially registered.Additional agreements: Put any changes or special arrangements in writing..Dubai rental dispute process: How to file a case, fees, documents and what happens next.Dubai landlord refusing to return your security deposit? source_snapshot.title: UAEV, Dubai World Trade Centre sign agreement to expand EV charging infrastructure
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 21st October, 2026 (WAM) -- UAEV has signed an agreement with Dubai World Trade Centre (DWTC) to develop and deploy electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure across designated parking areas at the Dubai World Trade Centre and Dubai Exhibition Centre. Signed on the sidelines of WETEX, the agreement will expand access to charging at key business, exhibition and event destinations in Dubai.The planned infrastructure will serve visitors attending exhibitions, conferences and events, alongside businesses and commercial fleets operating in and around these locations. By integrating charging facilities into existing parking areas, the initiative aims to make charging more convenient and support the growing demand for electric mobility.Phase 1 of the deployment at DWTC will cover four locations, establishing the project’s initial footprint within one of Dubai’s busiest business and exhibition districts.Ali Al Darwish, Acting CEO of UAEV, said: “Access to charging is an important consideration for people and businesses choosing electric vehicles. Our agreement with DWTC will bring charging services closer to drivers at destinations they already use for work, business and events, making it easier to fit charging into their day.“As we expand our network, we are working with partners to integrate charging into locations that serve a wide range of users. This collaboration will help us meet the needs of individual drivers and commercial operators, while supporting the UAE’s transition to more sustainable mobility.”Abdulrahman Obaid Abu Al Shawareb, EVP of Protocol and Security at DWTC, said: “Dubai World Trade Centre continues to enhance its infrastructure in line with Dubai’s ambitions for a more sustainable and future-ready urban environment. Our collaboration with UAEV will enable us to progressively expand EV charging facilities across our destinations, enhancing the overall visitor experience by providing greater convenience and accessibility for our visitors, tenants, and stakeholders, while supporting the wider adoption of sustainable mobility in Dubai.”The agreement brings together UAEV’s charging expertise and DWTC’s exhibition and commercial destinations to support the continued expansion of Dubai’s public EV charging network. It reflects a shared commitment to developing infrastructure that responds to changing mobility needs and supports the UAE’s wider sustainability objectives.

source_snapshot.title: RTA Enhances Mahboub to Enable Integrated Services Using AI Assistants
source_snapshot.text: RTA Enhances Mahboub to Enable Integrated Services Using AI Assistants Upgrade Designed to Simplify Customer Journeys and Enable Easier Service Completion Through a Unified Conversational Experience Dubai. Roads and Transport Authority. 22 October 2026: Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) has upgraded Mahboub, its virtual assistant, using AI assistant technology to simplify the customer journey and facilitate the completion of RTA services through a unified conversational experience. The enhanced version is being prepared for public rollout as part of RTA’s Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2030. New Capability: Coordinating and Executing Procedures Mahboub uses AI assistants to coordinate and execute services involving interconnected steps, in addition to the information and services it currently provides. Depending on each customer’s request, the system activates specialised AI assistants to coordinate and carry out the required procedures, such as paying vehicle fines and then renewing vehicle registration, according to the customer’s needs. Simpler Customer Journeys and Targeted Impact The system enables customers to complete these procedures within a single conversation. The process includes using the UAE PASS digital identity for verification and the Dubai Sadad platform for payment. The initial scope focuses on vehicle licensing services, including vehicle registration renewal, vehicle fines payment, a clearance certificate issuance and number plate reservations renewal. Mahboub supports Arabic and English, with language models fine-tuned to suit the local context. Mahboub aims to reduce the need for customers to switch between pages and channels, as well as the number of steps required to complete transactions. It is also expected to reduce the time and effort involved in accessing services. Development is being carried out in accordance with RTA’s established governance and cybersecurity procedures. The enhancement reflects RTA’s drive to develop leading, customer-centric digital services and reinforce Dubai’s standing with the aim of establishing the emirate as a global leader in trusted, smart government services.

source_snapshot.title: Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure enhances federal road readiness for rainy season
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 22nd October, 2026 (WAM) -- The Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure continues its proactive preparations for the rainy season by enhancing the readiness of federal roads and associated facilities, conducting preventive inspections and maintenance of stormwater drainage networks, pumping stations, and culverts, and strengthening monitoring and field response capabilities.The efforts aim to ensure road user safety and maintain service continuity under various weather conditions.As part of its preparations, the Ministry is inspecting and maintaining stormwater drainage networks, clearing waterways where wadis intersect with federal roads, and ensuring the efficiency and operational readiness of 17 pumping stations and 800 stormwater drainage culverts.It is also deploying specialised field teams and providing the necessary equipment and machinery to address water accumulation and various weather conditions, enabling faster response times, safer roads, and uninterrupted traffic flow.The Ministry continues to carry out preventive inspections and maintenance, including assessing structural conditions, removing sediment, and ensuring the operational readiness of discharge gates, waterways, and monitoring systems. These measures strengthen the infrastructure's capacity to accommodate rainwater flows and mitigate the risks of flash floods and flooding.It operates a smart, around-the-clock monitoring system for dams and wadis, equipped with surveillance cameras and sensors that measure water levels and flow rates. The system includes an early flood warning mechanism connected to the control centre and relevant national authorities, helping anticipate potential risks, issue alerts, and support proactive measures to protect lives and property.In addition, the Ministry continues to coordinate with its federal and local partners to strengthen joint preparedness, review emergency plans, and enhance field response procedures. This collaboration ensures the rapid exchange of information, coordinated responsibilities, and effective management of various rainfall scenarios, while minimising their impact on lives, property, and infrastructure.The Ministry continuously monitors the federal road network through its control centre, which provides real-time oversight of road conditions and field developments.The centre supports timely decision-making and the deployment of emergency and maintenance teams to affected locations in coordination with relevant authorities. This enables a rapid response to rainwater accumulation, minimises traffic disruptions, and enhances road user safety and service continuity.Eng. Mohammed Al Mansoori, Undersecretary for Infrastructure and Transport Affairs at the Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure, said that protecting lives and property and ensuring the continuity of essential services are key priorities in the Ministry's plans. He noted that preparations for the rainy season begin well in advance, with assessments of federal roads, dams, and water infrastructure, the identification of priority locations, and enhanced field team capabilities to respond effectively to various weather conditions.He said, "We follow a proactive approach focused on enhancing infrastructure readiness and strengthening its resilience to changing weather conditions, with particular emphasis on rapid response and minimising the impact of rainfall on traffic flow. We are committed to developing an integrated operational system that combines preventive maintenance, continuous monitoring, and coordinated field response to ensure road user safety and service continuity."Al Mansoori added, "Our investments in infrastructure development go beyond improving operational efficiency. They also focus on strengthening resilience and adaptability to different climatic conditions, ensuring that our infrastructure meets future development needs while maintaining the quality of services provided to the community."

source_snapshot.title: UAE end-of-service gratuity: How much are employees entitled to and when must it be paid?
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Private sector employees in the UAE are entitled to end-of-service gratuity based on their basic salary and length of service, with employers required to settle all outstanding payments within 14 days of the termination of their employment contracts, according to the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MoHRE).In an awareness post explaining key provisions of the UAE Labour Law, the ministry outlined how gratuity is calculated, eligibility requirements and the deadlines employers must follow when settling employees' financial entitlements..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..Under the law, expatriate employees who complete at least one year of continuous service are entitled to end-of-service gratuity calculated on their last basic salary.Employees receive the equivalent of 21 days' basic salary for each year of service during their first five years of employment. For every additional year of service beyond the first five years, the entitlement increases to 30 days' basic salary.The ministry clarified that employees who have completed at least one continuous year of service are also entitled to gratuity for any additional partial year, calculated proportionately according to the period worked.However, the total gratuity payable must not exceed the equivalent of two years' wages, regardless of the employee's length of service.14-day payment deadlineMoHRE stressed that employers must pay all end-of-service entitlements and outstanding wages within 14 days from the date an employee's contract ends.The requirement is intended to ensure that workers receive their financial entitlements promptly following the termination of their employment.The ministry also highlighted its voluntary Savings Scheme, which provides an alternative mechanism for managing and growing employees' end-of-service benefits.Under the scheme, employers can participate in approved investment funds, allowing employees' end-of-service benefits to be invested and potentially generate returns over time.The ministry said the initiative provides an opportunity to strengthen employees' financial security while supporting more sustainable management of end-of-service entitlements.The clarification forms part of MoHRE's efforts to raise awareness of labour rights and obligations, helping employees understand their financial entitlements and employers comply with the UAE Labour Law..UAE gratuity calculation: What happens if your basic salary is reduced?.UAE gratuity: When can your employer legally deduct from your end-of-service benefits?.UAE gratuity guide: How to calculate your final settlement.Is UAE gratuity calculated on basic salary or gross salary?

source_snapshot.title: Google, YouTube expand online child safety drive with US$2.4 million Google.org funding, Dubai child safety Pop-up
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 23rd October, 2026 (WAM) -- Google.org is supporting INJAZ Al-Arab with US$2.4 million in funding to empower youth across the Middle East and North Africa region with digital safety and online citizenship training over four-years through Google’s Arabic-language Abtal Al Internet (Be Internet Awesome) curriculum.The initiative aims to reach over 2.3 million young people across nine countries including the United Arab Emirates, Egypt, Morocco, Tunisia and Saudi Arabia.First launched in Arabic in 2018, Abtal Al Internet is Google’s digital literacy programme for children between the ages of seven and thirteen. The grant marks Google’s latest contribution to online safety in the region.The announcement coincides with the launch of the Google Abtal Al Internet Pop-Up Playground at Alserkal Avenue in Dubai, in partnership with the UAE Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority (TDRA) and the National Media Authority (NMA).The Pop-up, which is open to the public between 24-25 October, offers families an engaging, hands-on experience of Google’s digital literacy programme Abtal Al Internet and the parental control features available on Google products, including YouTube Kid and Teen accounts and the stand-alone YouTube Kids app.Abdulla bin Mohammed bin Butti Al Hamed, Chairman of the National Media Authority, said creating a safe digital environment for youth is a strategic pillar of the UAE's vision to build a secure and sustainable knowledge-based society that protects future generations from online risks while empowering them to harness digital opportunities responsibly and consciously.He said the Authority is working to raise digital awareness and promote responsible use of online platforms, ensuring that technology serves as a tool for knowledge, creativity and progress.Speaking during a visit to Google’s “Be Internet Awesome” interactive space (Abtal Al Internet), Al Hamed stressed the importance of digital literacy in helping children distinguish reliable information from misinformation, protect their privacy and interact respectfully online.He added that preparing future generations goes beyond mastering technological tools, requiring a set of values and skills that enable children to use technology consciously and responsibly. He noted that increased digital awareness broadens opportunities for exploration and creativity, empowering youth to help build a safer and more beneficial digital environment.“Whether seeing a life-sized T-Rex with Augmented Reality on Search, exploring biology with AbdulAllah Anan on YouTube, or using Gemini’s Study Notebook to prepare for a chemistry quiz, kids use our products every day to make sense of the world. As parents and leaders, our job is to help them navigate these spaces safely, building healthy habits and becoming responsible digital citizens,” said Anthony Nakache, Managing Director, Google MENA.Google builds protections directly into its products, combining default safeguards for under-18 accounts, such as private uploads, turned-off autoplay, and disabled personalised ads, with controls like Google Family Link and the YouTube Family Centre.Across MENA, more and more families are turning to YouTube to learn real life skills. Research by Kantar found that 95% of viewers in Saudi Arabia and the UAE believe YouTube offers leading educational content, while 92% of Gen Z respondents said the platform has helped them develop new skills.Eng. Saeed Belhoul, Acting Director-General of the TDRA, said, “TDRA’s child digital safety strategy is based on an integrated approach that combines prevention, awareness, and empowerment, while reinforcing shared responsibility among families, relevant entities, and digital platforms. As technology and artificial intelligence continue to evolve rapidly, we believe that protecting children does not necessarily mean avoiding their engagement with the digital world, but rather empowering them to explore it and benefit from its opportunities with awareness, confidence, and responsibility, while building a generation equipped with the knowledge and skills to make informed and safe decisions in the digital environment.”"We want parents to feel empowered when their children open YouTube to learn and explore, whether they are building a science experiment at home or diving into the region’s rich history. By pairing strong default protections with easy-to-use parental controls, every unique family can customise their experience and make the most of YouTube's educational content," said Javid Aslanov, Head of YouTube MENA.Earlier this year, YouTube launched Kid & Teen Accounts to give parents across the Middle East and North Africa additional content controls based on their child’s stage of development, including an industry-first Shorts feed timer to manage viewing, with the option to set it to zero minutes per day. In 2021, YouTube launched its stand-alone kids app, YouTube Kids offering robust parental controls.Healthy digital habits take ongoing conversation. To help families start open discussions about screen time and online safety at home, Google and YouTube created a simple Family Online Safety Agreement that parents and kids can adapt together:● Talk openly about what we watch, play, and share online.● Keep personal details private (like passwords, addresses, and phone numbers).● Double-check facts before sharing links or stories.● Choose kindness online and report toxic behavior.● Agree on trusted adults to talk to whenever something feels uncomfortable or confusing.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Future Solutions – Prototypes for Humanity summit to showcase 100 innovative projects from leading universities worldwide
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 23rd October, 2026 (WAM) -- The annual Dubai Future Solutions – Prototypes for Humanity summit returns to Dubai from 18 to 21 November 2026. Held under the patronage and leadership of H.H. Sheikha Latifa bint Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Chairperson of Dubai Culture and Arts Authority (Dubai Culture), the summit brings together one of the world’s largest and most diverse communities of academic innovators and provides a platform for turning research into real-world impact.This year’s edition will take place on The Prototype Floor during Dubai Future Week, held under the patronage of H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence of the UAE, and Chairman of the Board of Trustees of Dubai Future Foundation. The Week will run from 18 to 21 November 2026 at Emirates Towers and the Museum of the Future, under the theme ‘For the Human of the Future’.Organised by Dubai Future Foundation, Dubai Future Week is expected to bring together more than 10,000 participants from around the world, including experts, innovators, investors, policymakers and entrepreneurs. The programme will feature talks, policy discussions, investment pitches, competitions and public experiences exploring how emerging technologies can shape the future.Held as part of the summit, the Dubai Future Solutions – Prototypes for Humanity exhibition will feature 100 innovative projects selected from thousands of submissions by academics representing around 1,000 universities across more than 120 countries. Five outstanding projects, one in each of the initiative's five main categories, will be honoured during the event.Organised annually by Art Dubai Group in partnership with Dubai Future Foundation, Dubai International Financial Centre and the Hussain Sajwani – DAMAC Foundation, the initiative brings together leading innovators, researchers, professors, students and graduates from universities worldwide. It provides a platform to exchange knowledge and expertise, showcase academic research and explore how innovative ideas can be transformed into practical solutions to some of humanity's most pressing social, economic and environmental challenges.Dubai Future Solutions – Prototypes for Humanity aims to support university innovators from around the world in developing their ideas into practical applications. The exhibition also gives the public an opportunity to explore a wide range of research-driven solutions across healthcare, agriculture, water, energy, transport, the environment and civil society.This year's cohort includes teams from more than 70 universities across 33 countries, representing some of the world's leading academic institutions. These include Harvard University, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), the University of Oxford, the University of Cambridge, ETH Zurich, Imperial College London, Cornell University, the National University of Singapore and Delft University of Technology.The exhibition will also feature teams from universities in emerging economies, including Ghana, Peru, Morocco and Chile, alongside academic institutions from the UAE, including New York University Abu Dhabi, Khalifa University of Science and Technology and the American University of Sharjah.Khalfan Juma Belhoul, CEO of Dubai Future Foundation, said: “Dubai Future Solutions – Prototypes for Humanity reflects Dubai's vision of supporting creative minds and empowering future generations to develop innovative solutions to global challenges.”He added: “The initiative's objectives also align with Dubai Future Week and its theme, ‘For the Human of the Future’. It has become a global platform that brings together leading researchers and innovators from universities and academic institutions worldwide, enabling them to showcase their ideas and transform their research into practical projects that make a positive difference to communities.”Hussain Sajwani, Founder of DAMAC Group, said: “Dubai embodies an extraordinary vision for the future, driven by the ambition of its wise leadership and its proactive approach to transforming bold visions into tangible achievements. This is achieved through investments in innovation and technology, and the adoption of solutions that place people at the heart of development, with the aim of building a more competitive and sustainable economy.”He added: "Dubai Future Solutions - Prototypes for Humanity" reflects this vision, reaffirming that shaping the future is not about waiting for it to unfold, but about anticipating it and taking proactive steps to plan for it. At DAMAC, we believe our responsibility lies in translating this vision into transformative projects and strategic investments that contribute to urban development, enhance quality of life, and harness innovation for the benefit of humanity. Through these efforts, we aim to further strengthen Dubai’s position as a global hub for shaping the future, while creating a positive and lasting impact for generations to come.”This year's projects reflect a world adapting to rapid change, as innovators respond to rising temperatures, growing pressure on natural resources and the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence in everyday life.Beyond software, algorithms and data systems, teams are developing physical devices and robotic systems, biotechnology and bio-based solutions, advanced materials and chemical formulations. They are also redesigning industrial and environmental processes and exploring new ways to generate, store and convert energy.In healthcare, innovators are developing solutions to enable earlier diagnosis, improve the delivery of care and make healthcare more accessible.Among the featured projects, HEURIS helps emergency department clinicians consider the full range of possible diagnoses as test results become available. Age Resist uses a wearable device to analyse sweat composition and assess the body's ability to withstand and recover from physical stress associated with surgery. ChronoVasc, meanwhile, estimates the biological age of a person's arteries through a single blood test.Projects focused on climate and natural resources are developing innovative ways to use energy and materials more efficiently while transforming waste into valuable resources.SolarSkin enables solar panels to switch automatically between generating electricity and heating indoor spaces. MetCycle dissolves materials from spent batteries in less than 15 minutes at room temperature, while AlgaePalm produces an alternative to palm oil using UAE microalgae cultivated in saltwater.Other projects demonstrate how data and artificial intelligence can support smarter cities and strengthen public trust.Greenery Scanner monitors the health of street trees and maps their condition using cameras installed on vehicles travelling through city streets. Coco: Heat Minimizer helps people identify cooler walking routes during heatwaves, while Litmus independently assesses whether companies are fulfilling their commitments to protecting user privacy.Dubai Future Solutions – Prototypes for Humanity also supports academic entrepreneurs through a dedicated venture-building programme that provides funding, business expertise and specialised support, alongside opportunities for direct collaboration with industry partners. The programme helps participating teams transform scientific research into practical solutions that address real industry needs.The programme begins by testing the feasibility of selected technologies in real-world environments, before supporting participants in establishing companies, developing their businesses and expanding their operations.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Police warn of Dh400 jaywalking fine as part of road safety campaign
source_snapshot.text: Dubai Police have warned pedestrians of crossing roads unsafely, reminding them of a fine of Dh400. According to Article 89 of the Federal Traffic Law, pedestrians who disregard traffic signals or cross roads at undesignated locations can be fined Dh400. Brigadier Majid Sultan Al Suwaidi, Director of the General Department of Police Stations, urged pedestrians to use designated crossings, check that the road is clear of approaching vehicles and obey pedestrian traffic signals at intersections. “Road safety is a shared responsibility. Everyone has a role to play in following traffic regulations and helping create safer roads for all,” he said. The reminder comes as the authority launched an awareness campaign to promote pedestrian safety, encourage responsible road behaviour and reduce traffic accidents. The campaign also targets motorists, reminding them to remain vigilant, reduce speed and give way to pedestrians at designated crossings, particularly in busy and densely populated areas.

source_snapshot.title: Pakistani expats in UAE: E-Passports start, fees from Dh145
source_snapshot.text: The Embassy of Pakistan in Abu Dhabi and the Consulate General of Pakistan in Dubai have begun processing all passport applications as e-Passports from Friday, October 23, 2026, according to a public notice issued by the missions. The notice said the e-Passport issuance process “has started and will continue”, covering all new applications submitted at both offices. Pakistani nationals holding valid Machine Readable Passports (MRPs) do not need to replace them immediately. The missions said all valid MRPs remain valid until their date of expiry. Applicants have been advised to apply for renewal only when the remaining validity of their passport is less than six months. The notice also said that both a first name and a last name are mandatory for the e-Passport. Applicants whose current passports carry only a single name should be prepared for this requirement when applying. Over two million Pakistanis live in the UAE, making them the country’s second-largest expatriate community in the country. The community includes professionals, entrepreneurs and workers across various industries, with many considering the Emirates a second home after years or generations of residence. Beyond contributing to the UAE’s development, Pakistanis play a vital role in supporting their home country through remittances. Fees vary by the number of pages, validity period, processing type and whether the passport is being replaced after loss. All fees are in UAE dirhams.For a standard renewal, the lowest fee is Dh145 for a 36-page, five-year passport under normal processing, while the same document with a 10-year validity costs Dh215. A 72-page passport costs Dh260 for five years and Dh390 for 10 years under normal processing. Urgent processing adds a premium across all categories. source_snapshot.title: St. Regis Dubai, The Palm to reopen on November 1 after 6 months of refurbishment
source_snapshot.text: The St. Regis Dubai, The Palm will reopen its doors on November 1, 2026. The announcement by St. Regis Hotels & Resorts on Friday, marks the return of one of Palm Jumeirah's most well-recognised hotels. The hotel was temporarily closed for a major refurbishment in the middle of April this year. At the time, an operator had told Khaleej Times that the luxury property had closed off guest rooms, spas and other key services since April 12. Only their lobby lounge and and the St Regis Bar remained functional. The reopening comes as hotels across the country prepare for an influx of residents and tourists after a quieter summer due to the regional conflict. Refurbished and reimagined According to the hotel, St. Regis Bar has been reimagined and is at the heart of the reopening. Drawing on the brand's New York heritage, a series of photographic frames pays tribute to the cultural energy of Manhattan — connecting the Dubai property to the original St. Regis in Manhattan. The cocktail collection now features signature serves and original creations and for four evenings a week, a live pianist will provide the soundtrack. The St. Regis Spa will returns as will the hotel’s dining destinations, including all-day dining at Cordelia, Turkish-inspired cuisine at RÜYA and the vibrant KYMA Beach Club. At St. Regis Gardens, a collection of acclaimed restaurants — including Michelin-starred concepts and celebrated chef-led venues — offers exceptional dining in an open-air rooftop setting.

source_snapshot.text: Ras Al Khaimah closed all its beaches "until further notice", according to a notice by the emirate's Public Services Department. Earlier, the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment confirmed an oil spill off Umm Al Quwain to be the source of the 'fuel-like' smell that residents reported across multiple emirates. All beaches and coastal areas in Umm Al Quwain have been temporarily closed until teams complete assessments, and identify safety and marine protection measures, the ministry said. The odours "pose no health risk" to residents, the ministry confirmed. After the spill was detected, teams immediately began containment, cordoning, cleanup and remediation to limit environmental impact, Moccae said.

source_snapshot.title: Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial begins second edition in Al Ain
source_snapshot.text: AL AIN, 24th October, 2026 (WAM) -- The second edition of the Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial, organised by the Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi (DCT Abu Dhabi), opened yesterday in Al Ain. Presented under the theme Home: A Glossary for a Communal Sense of Place, the Al Ain chapter brings four newly commissioned works to Al Qattara Oasis, part of the UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape of Al Ain, and to Al Towayya Roundabout, placing contemporary art within working farms, historic irrigation networks and the everyday routes of the city. The Al Ain works remain on view until 15 February 2027, with the Biennial opening across Abu Dhabi on 15 November 2026.Under the artistic direction of Elvira Dyangani Ose, Artistic Director of Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa (MOCAA), the second edition approaches the concept of ‘home’ as an evolving, collective and plural condition rather than a static geographic site. Through distributed commissions, research-led practices and public encounters, the Biennial prioritises sustained engagement, inviting audiences to interact with art in their everyday spaces. The title proposes that what communities share in relation to Abu Dhabi is not the place itself, but the capacity to construct meaning in relation to it, through the diverse vocabularies, practices and forms of knowledge that the glossary is designed to hold.At Al Qattara Oasis, Moroccan artist M'barek Bouhchichi presents ‘I am not the stone thrown into the water, but the seed sown in the field’ (2026), a stainless-steel work that reimagines the pigeon tower, a vernacular architecture found from North Africa to the Emirates, as a space of refuge and passage. Taking its title from Tayeb Salih’s Season of Migration to the North, the work carries a poem from Al Nahma, the traditional Emirati sea shanties sung by sailors, rendered in Braille across its structures. Nearby, Indian artist Reena Saini Kallat’s Thresholds: Requiem (The Last Call) (2026) reimagines twentieth-century acoustic locators, once designed to detect distant aircraft, as vessels for the calls of extinct and critically endangered bird species, several of which are native to, or migrate through, the UAE and the Arabian Peninsula. Spanish artist Asunción Molinos Gordo’s Bil Hana wa Al Afia (2026) centres on Al Aflaj, the traditional irrigation systems that originated during the Iron Age and continue to support shared water distribution among farmers in the Emirates. Built from rammed-earth walls arranged in a root-like form, its seven stratigraphic layers incorporate pottery, artefacts and other material traces from different historical periods, set among the working farms of the oasis.At Al Towayya Roundabout, Emirati artist Roudhah Al Mazrouei, born in Al Ain, presents Tassa (2026), an 80-metre-diameter sculpture that reimagines the traditional Emirati gold headpiece as a monumental public landscape. Drawing on heirloom jewellery passed down through generations, the work transforms its cascading chains, curved forms and ornamental details into an immersive environment. Developed through conversations and workshops with children, Tassa proposes heritage as something lived, shared and continually reimagined.Elvira Dyangani Ose, Artistic Director, Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial 2026–27, said: “What do we mean when we say home? It is one of the most used terms in any language, and yet many aspects of it often go unexamined. Home is not only a location. It is a condition: felt before it is understood, carried in the body before it is articulated in language. Al Ain is where this edition begins, in an oasis landscape shaped over millennia by cooperation, shared water and collective care. We offer this Biennial as a glossary, not as a guide to correct interpretations but as a set of terms to think with. The definitions are partial by design, and yours to complete.”The Al Ain chapter inaugurates the Biennial’s second edition, which continues across Abu Dhabi from 15 November 2026 with further commissions, research-led projects and a public programme, details of which will be announced in the coming weeks. The second edition builds on the inaugural Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial, Public Matter (2024–25), which presented site-specific commissions by artists from the UAE and around the world. Several works from the first edition have since been acquired or retained as long-term installations, contributing to the emirate’s growing public art collection.The Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial is on view in Al Ain from 23 October 2026 to 15 February 2027 and in Abu Dhabi from 15 November 2026 to 15 February 2027.

source_snapshot.title: Dh60,000, 4.4kg and built like a camera: Rare Batman comic on display in Sharjah
source_snapshot.text: A Batman comic book that weighs 4.4kg, comes with a detachable lens and is designed to resemble a camera is on display at the Sharjah Animation and Comics Conference (SACC), with a price tag of Dh60,000. Only 47 copies of Batman: The Killing Joke Avant-Garde Edition are being produced worldwide. The handcrafted collector’s edition is being exhibited at the Argent Comics booth at the event, which runs until Sunday at Aljada. The book is inspired by the camera featured on the famous cover of Batman: The Killing Joke, originally published in 1988. Its aluminium boards are lined with goatskin, while the edition also features a detachable lens and a viewfinder. It is kept in a carrying case covered in calf leather and lined with suede. Croatian publishing imprint Argent Comics developed the edition under the direction of its creative director Marko Matijašević. According to the publisher, it is the world’s first giclée-printed comic book. The pages are printed on specially made Hahnemühle metallic paper using a patent-pending process. Vibor Kreća, a Croatian exhibitor representing Argent Comics at SACC, said making the book involves painstaking manual work. “You have to print on each side and then fuse them together by hand,” he said. The 47-copy run is also deliberate. Kreća said the number reflects silver’s atomic number, linking it to the Argent brand, whose name is associated with the metal. The edition contains two versions of the artwork from the acclaimed Batman story, written by Alan Moore and illustrated by Brian Bolland. Readers can see John Higgins’ original colouring as well as Bolland’s 2008 recolouring. Kreća said Bolland had been unhappy with the earlier coloured version of the book and later revisited it. “This is like a director’s cut,” he said. source_snapshot.title: 40 million students, Dh11m in prizes: Arab Reading Challenge to crown winner on Oct 29
source_snapshot.text: The Arab Reading Challenge will crown the winners of its tenth edition on October 29, 2026, at a closing ceremony at the Dubai World Trade Centre. Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai, said the country remains committed to serving the Arabic language and nurturing new generations who believe that progress begins with reading and knowledge. "The future of a nation begins with nurturing its young minds. Our investment in the Reading Challenge is an investment in a better future for all," he said. "For centuries, the Arabic language served as the driving force for human and social progress. It will restore its former glory once again with the dedication and brilliant minds of its youth." Record participation Organised by the Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Initiatives, this year's edition drew over 40 million students from 60 countries, including 74,062 in the People of Determination category. This massive participation marks a 24 per cent increase over the challenge’s ninth edition and represents 48 per cent of all school students across the Arab World. The challenge also involved 138,426 schools and 161,507 supervisors. Mohammad Al Gergawi, Secretary-General of the Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Initiatives (MBRGI), which organises the challenge, described this year’s edition as a landmark: "The tenth edition is a major milestone for the Arab Reading Challenge, drawing a record-breaking participation of over 40 million students and expanding across 60 countries for the first time," he said. "This remarkable reach reflects the deep appreciation and support the initiative commands across the Arab world and beyond." The closing ceremony will crown: Arab Reading Challenge Champion: Dh500,000 (second: Dh100,000; third: Dh70,000) People of Determination Champion: Dh200,000 (second: Dh100,000; third: Dh50,000) Best School: Dh1 million (second: Dh500,000; third: Dh300,000) Outstanding Supervisor: Dh300,000 (second: Dh100,000; third: Dh50,000) Community Champion: Dh200,000 total (first: Dh100,000; second: Dh70,000; third: Dh30,000) — open to students outside the Arab world, non-native Arabic speakers and those learning Arabic as a second language Total prizes awarded since the challenge launched now stand at Dh110 million, with Dh11 million given to winners each year. A growing challenge Launched in 2015 by Sheikh Mohammed as the largest-ever Arab literacy initiative, the Arab Reading Challenge has grown dramatically. Participation in the tenth edition is up 1,019 per cent compared with the first, which drew 3.6 million students. Last year, the ninth edition brought together 32.231 million students from 50 countries. The main title went to Tunisian twins Bisan and Baylasan Kouka, while Maria Hassan Ajil from Iraq won the People of Determination category. The challenge aims to promote reading among students across the Arab world and beyond, strengthen language skills, and nurture a lasting love of knowledge and the Arabic language.

source_snapshot.title: RTA completes World Trade Centre Roundabout Development Project, to open final bridge October 30
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 25th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) will open the final bridge of the World Trade Centre Roundabout Development Project this Friday, 30th October 2026. The 1,000-metre, two-lane bridge will accommodate approximately 3,000 vehicles per hour, serving traffic from Al Majlis Street towards 2nd December Street.The bridge will improve traffic flow at one of Dubai’s key intersections, cutting journey time from Al Majlis Street to 2nd December Street from six minutes to one minute.With its opening, RTA will have completed all major works under the World Trade Centre Roundabout Development Project, which include five bridges with a combined length of 5,000 metres, at a cost exceeding AED696 million.Mattar Al Tayer, Director-General, Chairman of the Board of Executive Directors of RTA, said the project involves converting the former roundabout into an at-grade intersection, improving traffic flow on Sheikh Zayed Road and enhancing connectivity between the emirate’s leading economic and commercial centres. It will also reduce average delay at the intersection from 12 minutes to 90 seconds, benefiting more than 500,000 residents and visitors.Al Tayer explained that the World Trade Centre Roundabout Development Project complements Al Mustaqbal Street Development Project, scheduled for completion in 2027. The project includes bridges and tunnels spanning a total of 1,500 metres and expansion of the street to four lanes in each direction, increasing its capacity by 33 percent.The World Trade Centre Roundabout Development Project includes a bridge at the second level towards Deira, two bridges linking Sheikh Rashid Street with 2nd December Street, and another two bridges connecting Al Majlis Street with 2nd December Street, providing free-flowing traffic in multiple directions.The integrated project serves key areas, including Dubai World Trade Centre, Dubai International Financial Centre, Zaa’beel, Al Satwa, Al Karama, Al Jafiliya and Al Mankhool.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Municipality awards AED3 billion worth of contracts for four projects under Phase 3 of ‘Tasreef’ Programme
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 25th October, 2026 (WAM) -- In line with the directives of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister and Ruler of Dubai, to develop advanced, resilient and world-leading infrastructure and enhance the efficiency of the stormwater drainage system to meet the emirate’s future growth requirements, Dubai Municipality has awarded contracts for four new projects under Phase 3 of the ‘Tasreef’ Programme to develop Dubai’s stormwater drainage network. With a total value of AED3 billion, the projects will involve the construction and extension of approximately 100 kilometres of main stormwater drainage lines, with diameters of up to 3 metres, further enhancing the resilience of the city’s drainage network.The new projects are distributed across vital areas representing key economic, commercial, industrial and tourism corridors across the emirate, covering nearly 100 square kilometres. They include the development of stormwater drainage systems and networks in Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim, Al Safa, Al Manara, Al Quoz, Al Barsha, Al Wasl, Za’abeel, Al Bada’a, Al Satwa and Al Marmoom, connecting these areas to Dubai Municipality’s main stormwater drainage network. The projects will increase the network’s water-flow capacity, enhance operational resilience and support sustainable urban growth.The third package of projects represents an integrated extension of the Tasreef Programme, one of the UAE’s largest strategic and transformational infrastructure projects. The programme is classified as the largest integrated stormwater collection programme in a single system in the region and one of the most operationally efficient. Implemented by Dubai Municipality at a total cost of AED30 billion, it will provide a highly resilient and advanced drainage system capable of meeting Dubai’s future requirements.The programme will enhance the city’s readiness and preparedness to address climate-related changes, increase stormwater drainage capacity by 700 percent, and reduce costs associated with the construction of pumping stations and operations and maintenance by 20 percent. It will also extend the lifespan of the network and support the objectives of the Dubai 2040 Urban Master Plan and the UAE’s Net Zero 2050 Strategy.Eng. Marwan Ahmed bin Ghalita, Director-General of Dubai Municipality, said, “Dubai Municipality continues to implement the phases of the ‘Tasreef’ Programme, one of Dubai’s largest strategic infrastructure projects, enhancing its efficiency and resilience, making it more sustainable and strengthening its ability to address both future climate change and accommodate population and urban growth.Our objective is to build a comprehensive and integrated model for a leading future city, characterised by a sustainable urban system and advanced infrastructure that serve people, enhance their quality of life and well-being, and strengthen their safety and security. At the same time, it provides a stable and enabling environment for the growth of businesses and economic, commercial and tourism activities, reinforcing Dubai’s position as the world’s best city to live, work, invest and visit.”Eng. Adel Mohammed Al Marzouqi, CEO of the Waste and Sewerage Agency at Dubai Municipality, said, “The third phase of the Tasreef Programme’s projects will serve areas that represent vital arteries across the emirate, marking another pivotal step in developing Dubai’s stormwater drainage system as well as making it more resilient and efficient in managing rainfall under different conditions and future climate changes. We are committed to ensuring that these projects advance the broader objectives of the Tasreef Programme by reducing water accumulation, protecting residents and assets, improving the quality of services, enhancing the city’s readiness and traffic flow, and safeguarding the sustainability of its resources.”The Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim Stormwater Drainage Network Development Project is one of the largest projects under the third phase of Tasreef. It aims to enhance infrastructure readiness along key strategic corridors across the two areas, serving communities extending from Umm Suqeim 1, 2 and 3, and Umm Al Sheif to Jumeirah 3, Al Safa 1 and 2, and Al Manara along the Dubai Water Canal.The project includes the construction of approximately 42 kilometres of main stormwater drainage lines, enhancing the resilience, efficiency and capacity of the drainage system.The Stormwater Drainage Network Development and Capacity Enhancement Project between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road focuses on developing resilient and sustainable infrastructure capable of accommodating residential and urban growth and enhancing the city’s readiness and resilience.The project includes the construction of 14 kilometres of main stormwater drainage lines in accordance with the highest international standards.It will serve several of Dubai’s key strategic corridors and vital areas, including the Al Khail Road interchange towards Umm Suqeim, Umm Suqeim Road and Sheikh Zayed Road, in addition to First Al Khail Street, Al Marabea Street, Al Waha Street, Al Zumurrud Street and the connecting secondary roads.The project will cover Al Quoz Industrial Areas 1, 3 and 4, as well as Al Barsha 1.The Development of Main Stormwater Drainage Lines along Al Wasl Road Project aims to serve areas east of the Dubai Water Canal, including Za’abeel 2, Al Wasl, Jumeirah 1 and 2, Al Bada’a, Al Satwa, and Dubai World Trade Centre 1 and 2, covering an area of up to 25 square kilometres.The project includes an integrated stormwater drainage network comprising main and secondary conveyance lines and associated infrastructure, with a total length of 21 kilometres. This will enable the drainage and management of large volumes of water flow with operational flexibility, helping to prevent water accumulation.As part of the third phase of the Tasreef Programme, Dubai Municipality will develop an integrated and sustainable stormwater drainage network in Al Marmoom, serving vital areas by implementing 23 kilometres of stormwater drainage infrastructure. This will ensure continuity of services and enhance the quality of the area’s urban infrastructure.Dubai Municipality continues to implement strategic projects in accordance with approved timelines and operational plans, reaffirming its commitment to developing an integrated and resilient drainage system that contributes to reducing the risks associated with water accumulation, enhancing the efficiency and sustainability of infrastructure, and strengthening Dubai’s readiness to respond effectively to climate change.These efforts further support Dubai’s ambition to be recognised globally for the quality of its infrastructure and public services.
