source_snapshot.title: Dubai to close some E611 lanes, Al Maktoum airport tunnel amid autonomous taxi testing
source_snapshot.text: Dubai's transport authority announced the closures of a major road and tunnel on Sunday, October 25, amid autonomous taxi companies' testing operations. Three lanes of the Emirates Road (E611), opposite Al Maktoum International Airport, are set to be closed during the highway testing, the RTA revealed in its statement. Additionally, the entire Al Maktoum International Airport Tunnel will also be closed in both directions. The closures are set to take place from October 26 to 31, between 9am and 4pm. Motorists have been urged to plan their journeys in advance and follow directional signs to ensure smooth travel. Earlier this month, a senior UAE official said the country would have more than 10,000 autonomous taxis and delivery vans operating next year, with orders already placed for the vehicles as the country prepares to sharply scale up driverless transport. Both Abu Dhabi and Dubai have already begun commercial autonomous taxi operations. Abu Dhabi expanded Level 4 autonomous taxi services on Yas Island earlier this year, while Dubai launched commercial autonomous taxi services in areas including Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah. Abu Dhabi had previously become the first city in the Middle East and North Africa to begin commercial operations of fully driverless Level 4 vehicles, according to Abu Dhabi Mobility.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Police deploy 904 HP JETOUR G700 to strengthen desert tourism safety
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 25th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Police have introduced a new JETOUR G700 patrol vehicle to strengthen security, improve emergency response and provide assistance to visitors at desert tourism destinations ahead of the winter season.The four-wheel drive vehicle, designed to operate across sandy terrain and challenging desert conditions, was unveiled at Al Marmoom Oasis as part of a collaboration between the Tourist Police Department at Dubai Police’s General Department of Criminal Investigation and JETOUR.The initiative comes as Dubai prepares for increased visitor activity at desert attractions during the cooler months, particularly on weekends and public holidays.The unveiling ceremony was attended by Colonel Mohammad Abdulrahman, Director of the Tourist Police Department; Abdullah bin Khadeya, Chief Executive Officer for Strategy, Partnerships and Government Relations; and Major Saeed bin Ghadeer, Head of the Tourist Trip Programmes Monitoring Section at the Tourist Police Department.Col Mohammed Abdulrahman said the collaboration with JETOUR supports Dubai Police’s commitment to maintaining a strong presence at tourist destinations and providing visitors with a safe and enjoyable experience.He explained that the new patrol will help officers respond more efficiently to emergency calls, assist tourists and answer enquiries, particularly as desert attractions experience increased demand during the winter tourism season.“The collaboration supports our efforts to strengthen police presence in tourist areas, improve emergency response and ensure visitors have access to the assistance and services they need,” he said.Col Abdulrahman noted that vehicles suited to desert conditions are essential for maintaining effective police operations in remote tourist locations.He explained that the JETOUR G700’s off road capabilities will allow officers to access sandy tracks and desert attractions more easily, especially during periods of increased visitor activity.He also praised the cooperation with JETOUR, highlighting the importance of partnerships in supporting field operations and improving public safety.The JETOUR G700 features a 2.0 litre turbocharged engine paired with two electric motors and a 34.13 kWh battery, delivering a combined output of approximately 904 horsepower and 1,135 Nm of torque. Equipped with a four-wheel drive system, the vehicle can accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h in approximately 4.6 to 4.8 seconds, combining powerful performance with the off-road capabilities needed to navigate challenging desert terrain.

source_snapshot.title: New Indian passport collection points announced after 4 consular centres in UAE shut
source_snapshot.text: After four Indian Consular Application Centres (ICACs) in the UAE shut permanently, applicants awaiting passport collections are required to visit alternative locations to receive their documents. Alhind, the outsourced service provider for the Indian Embassy in Abu Dhabi and the Indian Consulate in Dubai, has issued a fresh advisory on its website detailing the revised arrangements, effective Sunday, October 25, 2026. The move follows an announcement by the Embassy on Wednesday that the four centres would cease operations from October 22. Consular, passport, visa and attestation services will remain available at the other 12 centres across the UAE. The affected centres are: Musaffah, Abu Dhabi Al Reem, Abu Dhabi Dubai Investment Park-I, Dubai Al Majaz, Sharjah Where to collect pending passports The latest announcement brings the interim arrangement following the closures to an end. In an earlier advisory, Alhind had said passport delivery counters would remain open at three of the affected centres — DIP, Al Majaz and Musaffah — while submission counters at all four locations would remain closed. Applicants who had chosen to collect their passports from the Dubai Investment Park (DIP) centre in Dubai or the Al Majaz centre in Sharjah must now go to UW Mall in Bur Dubai. Those awaiting passport collection at the Musaffah or Al Reem centres in Abu Dhabi have been directed to the Al Danah Centre. Alhind has urged applicants with passports pending collection at any of the four closed centres to visit their designated alternative location to collect their documents. The closures have reduced the number of operational Indian Consular Application Centres (ICACs) in the UAE from 16 to 12. The 12 remaining centres, operated by Alhind Tours & Travels, continue to function as usual. These include the large Bur Dubai facility, which has 45 counters to help reduce waiting times, and centres at the Indian Association Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah, Kalba, Khor Fakkan, Al Danah, Al Ain, Madinat Zayed and Ghayathi. For urgent requirements, the embassy has confirmed that Tatkal passport applications, newborn applications, Emergency Certificate requests and applications from people aged 60 and above will be accepted without appointments on a walk-in, first-come, first-served basis at all 12 centres. All centres operate from 8am to 6pm. Applicants are allowed to enter only 15 minutes before their scheduled appointment, so arriving much earlier will not offer any advantage. Appointments can be booked through the official portal, consularsevainuae.com, with new slots released daily at 9am and 9pm.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Municipality launches refreshed Al Ruwayyah winter camping season
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 26th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Municipality has opened registration for the 2026–2027 winter camping season in Al Ruwayyah, introducing an enhanced experience with expanded facilities, recreational activities and greater flexibility for UAE nationals. Running from 1st November 2026 to 30th April 2027, the new season will accommodate 600 camps, representing an increase of approximately 120% compared with previous seasons.The expanded offering includes the return of double-sized camping plots of up to 800 square metres, alongside standard plots measuring 400 square metres. For the first time, Dubai Municipality has also introduced 50 dedicated caravan plots and 10 fully equipped camps available for daily rental, providing additional options for visitors seeking a camping experience without having to establish and equip their own camps.These enhancements mark a new phase in the development of Al Ruwayyah as a seasonal destination, reflecting Dubai Municipality's approach to expanding the functions and experiences offered across public spaces. The Municipality aims to progressively enhance the destination in future seasons, introducing facilities and activities that respond to community needs while encouraging outdoor recreation, family engagement and wellbeing.As part of the new season, Dubai Municipality has designated 10 spaces for winter events and gatherings, providing dedicated areas for family activities, community programmes, recreational experiences and seasonal markets.These additions will expand the range of activities available at Al Ruwayyah, creating more opportunities for families and community members to enjoy the winter season in an organised desert environment.The Municipality has also allocated dedicated investment opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in food and beverage services, desert activities and recreational experiences.These opportunities will enable local entrepreneurs and businesses to introduce additional products, services and activities for campers and visitors. By integrating commercial offerings into the destination, Dubai Municipality aims to support local economic activity while enhancing the overall camping experience.The developments form part of a longer-term approach to enhancing Al Ruwayyah's recreational and community offering, with the current season establishing a foundation for further improvements to facilities, services and visitor experiences in the years ahead.Bader Anwahi, CEO of the Public Facilities Agency at Dubai Municipality, said, “The 2026–2027 season marks an important step in our approach to developing Al Ruwayyah as an integrated winter destination that responds to the evolving needs of Dubai's community. By significantly increasing capacity and introducing new camping options, recreational facilities and spaces for community activities, we are expanding opportunities for UAE nationals and their families to enjoy the winter season in a safe, well-organised environment.“Our ambition extends beyond the enhancements introduced this season. We are establishing a foundation for the continued development of Al Ruwayyah, with a focus on providing more diverse experiences, strengthening community connections and ensuring that our public destinations continue to contribute to quality of life and wellbeing.”He added, “An important part of this approach is creating opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises to participate in the destination's development. By encouraging local businesses to introduce new services and recreational experiences, we aim to support entrepreneurship while expanding the range of activities available to visitors. This reflects our wider commitment to developing public facilities that deliver lasting community and economic value.”Dubai Municipality allows seasonal permit holders to design and equip their camps according to their individual requirements, following the issuance of the necessary permits and the demarcation of camping plot boundaries.Campers must comply with the approved regulations, including the installation of temporary fencing and the use of camps exclusively for family purposes and camping activities.The Municipality has also allocated dedicated spaces for participating government entities, enabling them to establish and equip camps according to their requirements.UAE nationals can register and reserve camping plots through Dubai Municipality's official digital channels, including wintercamp.dm.gov.ae and the DubaiNow app.Seasonal camping reservations are available for periods ranging from three to six months, while separate booking options are offered for caravan plots and fully equipped daily rental camps, subject to the applicable requirements.Through the continued development of Al Ruwayyah's winter camping facilities, Dubai Municipality aims to expand opportunities for outdoor recreation, strengthen family and community connections, and enhance the quality of seasonal public destinations across Dubai.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai's Museum of the Future reopens in 2027: What visitors can expect
source_snapshot.text: When Dubai’s Museum of the Future reopens in the first quarter of 2027, the building may look familiar from the outside, but the experience within will be entirely new. Fresh exhibitions, immersive environments and new laboratories will replace the experiences that have defined the museum since it opened in 2022, with visitors promised a more hands-on role in exploring science, research and the possibilities of what comes next. The renewed museum experience will have its “own focus and direction” rather than simply updating its existing galleries, Azza Al Nuaimi, Chief Operating Officer of the Museum of the Future, told Khaleej Times. According to FAQs published on the museum’s website, none of the current exhibitions and experiences will return in their previous form. They will be replaced by entirely new ones, brought together through a new narrative and a different visitor journey. “The aim is to make the future something visitors can do more than simply imagine,” Al Nuaimi said. Visitors will have opportunities to explore new possibilities, engage with work taking place inside the laboratories and consider how decisions being made today could shape the world of tomorrow. Even the people bringing the experience to life are changing. The museum said its new “ Future Perfects ” recruitment drive for the Visitor Experience team drew more than 20,000 completed applications in its first 48 hours. The roles prioritise qualities including curiosity, imagination, emotional intelligence and adaptability rather than previous museum or customer-service experience. source_snapshot.title: Nakheel awards over AED950 million main construction contract for 617 homes at Bay Grove Residences on Dubai Islands
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 26th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Nakheel, a member of Dubai Holding Real Estate, has awarded Parkway International Contracting LLC a construction contract valued at more than AED 950 million for Phases 2 and 4 of Bay Grove Residences on Dubai Islands.The contract covers 617 homes ranging from one to four-bedroom across eight residential buildings, together with basement works, associated infrastructure and amenities including swimming pools, sports courts and fitness centres. Phase 2 comprises 360 homes across four buildings, with main construction works expected to be completed by late 2028. Phase 4 comprises 257 homes across four buildings, with completion anticipated in the second quarter of 2029.The award builds on Nakheel’s earlier contract of more than AED 800 million for 537 homes across seven buildings in Phases 1 and 3. Together, the two contracts represent more than AED 1.75 billion in main construction awards and cover all 1,154 planned homes across Bay Grove Residences’ 15 buildings.Khalid Al Malik, Chief Executive Officer of Dubai Holding Real Estate, said: “This award marks another important step in the delivery of Bay Grove Residences, establishing a clear construction pathway for a further 617 homes. Together with the contract already awarded for Phases 1 and 3, it represents a substantial investment in the community and the long-term development of Dubai Islands. Our focus remains on delivering high-quality homes, amenities and public spaces that will create a distinctive waterfront community for residents.”Tarek Zoabi, Managing Partner of Parkway International Contracting LLC, said: “We are pleased to partner with Nakheel on the next stages of Bay Grove Residences. Our team is focused on safe, disciplined delivery across both phases, with close attention to build quality, coordination and the agreed programme.”Bay Grove Residences is planned as a waterfront community with landscaped communal spaces, walking and cycling routes and access to Crystal Beach.Located off the coast of Deira, Dubai Islands is a five-island waterfront destination spanning 18.6 square kilometres. Its master plan includes residential neighbourhoods, hospitality, parks, leisure and cultural destinations as part of Dubai’s longer-term urban development.

source_snapshot.title: Emirates Dubai 7s adds HSBC SVNS 3, featuring 28 teams, 70 matches
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 26th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Emirates Dubai 7s will host the world’s biggest international sevens tournament with the addition of HSBC SVNS 3 to the schedule, while in the HSBC SVNS, New Zealand will begin the defence of the titles they won in Dubai last year against Fiji (men’s) and Japan (women’s) following the announcement of the fixtures and pools for next month’s event.The Middle East’s largest sports and entertainment festival returns to The Sevens Stadium on November 27-29, ahead of the UAE National Day holiday, with tickets for the event on sale now.For the first time, HSBC SVNS 3 will take place at the event alongside HSBC SVNS Series, bringing together 28 international men's and women's teams across both competitions, with 70 matches being played throughout the weekend, giving fans the opportunity to enjoy more world class rugby and watch some of the sport’s rising stars in action.As the third tier of the international rugby sevens competition, HSBC SVNS 3 gives those nations who are fast becoming established as genuine contenders in global sevens the opportunity to compete and progress to HSBC SVNS 2, HSBC SVNS and, ultimately, secure a pathway to Olympic qualification.In addition to HSBC SVNS and HSBC SVNS 3, this year’s Emirates Dubai 7s features amateur competitions for men and women across rugby, netball presented by Dubai Holdings Community Management, cricket presented by Dulsco Group, Rebound Padel, WODON3 fitness and Gaelic football, which makes its debut at this year’s festival.Additionally, the International Invitational rugby tournaments have been enhanced with representation from international teams including Argentina, Brazil, China, South Africa and Spain.Away from the sporting action, hugely popular DJs Melanie C and Jax Jones have been confirmed as the main acts at Beats on 2 across the weekend, with further headline artist announcements to follow in the coming weeks.As ever, the event marks the opening leg of the HSBC SVNS 2026/2027 Series, with tournaments to follow in Cape Town, Singapore, Perth, Vancouver and New York. The HSBC SVNS World Championship 2027 then takes place, during April and May, in Hong Kong, Valladolid and Bordeaux.With the HSBC SVNS 3 tournament set to begin on Friday November 27, on Pitch 1, international SVNS rugby will be played on the opening day of Emirates Dubai 7s for the first time. Pitch 1 will also host the HSBC SVNS 3 finals on Saturday November 28.Once again, all HSBC SVNS fixtures across the weekend will take place on Pitch 1 with the men’s and women’s competitions made up of the best eight teams in the world.In the men’s tournament, South Africa, last season’s Series winners, are joined in Pool A by Australia, beaten finalists in Dubai last year, along with Argentina and USA. Pool B, meanwhile, sees Emirates Dubai 7s defending champions, New Zealand, drawn alongside Fiji, Spain and France.The pick of the opening fixtures sees New Zealand begin the defence of their title against Fiji at 12.36pm, while the two most recent Series champions – South Africa and Argentina – go head-to-head at 11.52am in what promises to be a fascinating encounter.Other highlights include South Africa versus Australia, scheduled for 2.55pm, and New Zealand versus France, which brings the group-stage matches to a close at 8.22pm.New Zealand, last season’s Series champions and Emirates Dubai 7s winners, are undoubtedly the team to beat, with the All Blacks drawn alongside Fiji, Japan and Canada in Pool B, while Pool A features Australia, France, Spain and USA.The women’s competition kicks off with USA taking on Spain at 10am, while New Zealand open their campaign against Japan at 11.06am.France face Spain at 1pm, immediately followed by Australia’s match against USA at 1.22pm, while the standout match of the group stage – New Zealand versus Fiji – brings the curtain down on the women’s pool fixtures at 6.52pm.The tournament features six men's and six women's teams, who secure qualification through regional competitions around the world. Like HSBC SVNS, teams compete in pool stages before progressing to knockout matches, with the top two men's and women's teams securing promotion to HSBC SVNS 2, which takes place across three rounds in Nairobi, Sao Paolo and Montevideo early in 2027.The men’s HSBC SVNS 3 competition will be contested by Hong Kong China, Canada, Chile, Italy, Samoa and Zimbabwe, while China, Mexico, Poland, Samoa and Colombia have secured their spot in the women’s competition, with one more team set to qualify.Mathew Tait, Festival Director of Emirates Dubai 7s, said: “The addition of HSBC SVNS 3 to this year’s Emirates Dubai 7s for the first time is a particularly significant milestone for the event and its overall evolution.“This will be the world’s biggest international sevens tournament, with 28 teams from around the world competing across HSBC SVNS and HSBC SVNS 3, and 70 matches taking place over the course of the weekend.“This gives us a sense of enormous pride and firmly reinforces our commitment to growing the game. We can’t wait for fans to experience what promises to be a truly special weekend.”World Rugby Sevens World Series General Manager, Sam Pinder, said: "The return of HSBC SVNS 3 to Dubai is another important moment for the development of international rugby sevens and our ambition to create meaningful opportunities for more nations to compete on the global stage."Bringing HSBC SVNS 3 together with HSBC SVNS provides a fantastic platform to showcase the depth of talent across the game, from teams looking to take the next step to the world's best competing at the highest level."With promotion to HSBC SVNS 2 at stake, there is plenty to play for, and we're looking forward to an exciting weekend of rugby sevens in Dubai."Mohammed Alzaabi, Secretary General of the UAE Rugby Federation, said: “We are proud to be part of Emirates Dubai 7s, an iconic event that continues to strengthen Dubai’s position as a leading global destination for rugby. The addition of HSBC SVNS 3 marks an exciting milestone, creating more opportunities for emerging rugby nations to compete on the international stage.“At the UAE Rugby Federation, we are committed to supporting the growth and development of rugby at all levels, and our participation in this prestigious event reflects our ambition to showcase UAE rugby talent, inspire the next generation of players, and contribute to the continued success of rugby in the region.“We look forward to another exceptional edition of Emirates Dubai 7s and to welcoming teams and fans from around the world.”Tickets are on sale via emiratesdubai7s.com and the Emirates Dubai 7s app, with General Admission 3-Day Passes starting from AED595 per person, while a 3-Day Family Pass, securing entry for two adults and two children, is priced AED1,136. Day Passes for Saturday or Sunday are priced AED455, while Friday entry is AED 75, with children under 15 admitted free of charge. Tickets for People of Determination, including a carer, are AED375.

source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 26th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dr. Abdulrahman Abdulmannan Al Awar, Minister of Human Resources and Emiratisation and Acting Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research, inaugurated Najah Dubai 2026 today at Za’abeel Hall 5, Dubai World Trade Centre.The sixth edition, running until 27 October, brings together more than 100 universities from 20 countries, with the UAE Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research serving as Strategic Partner.The Ministry’s strategic partnership reflects the importance of helping students make informed academic choices and preparing them for an evolving labour market. As technology reshapes industries and new skills gain importance, Najah brings international higher education options, practical guidance and direct access to admissions teams together under one roof.The exhibition welcomed visitors on Sunday, 25th October, ahead of Monday’s official inauguration. Students, parents, teachers and academic counsellors can explore programmes, compare admission requirements and seek first-hand information about scholarships, student life and possible career pathways.Participating universities represent major study destinations, including the UAE, United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Germany, Spain, Hungary, Malaysia and more. Their diverse programmes span fields such as AI, engineering, health sciences, business, technology and communications, giving students an opportunity to consider both established disciplines and emerging areas of study.The event also features more than 30 expert-led seminar sessions covering university admissions, scholarship opportunities, studying abroad and career planning. Through direct conversations with universities and education specialists, visitors can better understand how programme choices connect with their interests, academic strengths and future ambitions.Beyond the university prospectus, students can use the exhibition to ask practical questions about choosing a programme. Families may want to understand how qualifications are recognised, whether a degree includes work placements, what support is available to international students, or how graduates progress into employment. By giving visitors access to the people who can answer those questions, the exhibition brings academic planning closer to the realities of university life and the workplace.The significance of this guidance is reinforced by growth across the UAE’s higher-education sector. According to the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research, 218,241 students were enrolled at universities during the previous academic year, including 64,859 new students. The country’s 103 higher-education institutions collectively offer approximately 2,500 academic programmes.Commenting on the exhibition, Dima Al Sadi, Portfolio Manager, Najah Expo, said, “More choice is a good thing, but it also means students have more to work through before they make a decision. They may be comparing a university in the UAE with an overseas campus, looking at several different programmes, or trying to understand which option gives them the best fit academically and professionally. Speaking to universities directly helps make that process much clearer.”She added, “What we hear from students is that they want to go beyond the brochure. They want to ask about scholarships, recognition, student life, internships, employability and what graduates actually go on to do. Those are much easier conversations to have face to face.”

source_snapshot.title: Etihad Rail, Citymapper partner to make end-to-end journey planning easier across UAE
source_snapshot.text: ABU DHABI, 27th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Etihad Rail has partnered with Citymapper; its parent company Via; and United Trans to make it easier for customers to plan end-to-end journeys across the UAE through the Citymapper app.The announcement comes following the official launch of the national passenger network on 30 September, with services now operating across Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Al Dhaid, and Fujairah. As the network expands to serve more people and communities, making it easier for customers to plan their journeys to and from Etihad Rail stations will become increasingly important.The Citymapper app enables customers to view and compare journeys that combine Etihad Rail services with metro, bus, on-demand transport and other mobility options, simplifying end-to-end journey planning across the country. The integration complements Etihad Rail's existing digital channels, with customers continuing to book and manage their rail journeys through the Etihad Rail website and app, while using Citymapper to plan connections across the wider transport network in the UAE. As Etihad Rail passenger services continue to expand, the partnership supports a shared vision for connected mobility with a focus on making the full customer journey easier; from planning a trip to reaching the final destination. Etihad Rail passenger services form part of the UAE's wider vision to enhance connectivity, create new travel opportunities and encourage greater use of public transport. Adhraa Al Mansoori, Executive Director of Commercial and Support at Etihad Rail Mobility, said: " Giving customers greater choice and confidence is key to how we are shaping the passenger rail experience. As our network expands, we want customers to feel that planning a train journey is simple, clear and fits naturally to the way they already move across the UAE.""By working with partners such as Citymapper, we are supporting that experience beyond the rail journey itself, helping customers make more informed decisions before they travel and making it easier for them to choose public transport as part of their journeys."By combining Etihad Rail services with a broader range of transport options through the Citymapper app, the partnership aims to reduce journey complexity, improve accessibility and encourage greater use of shared and public transport across the UAE.Lionel Joseph, Head of Operations, United Trans, said: "Integrated mobility depends on strong collaboration between transport providers, operators and technology partners. We are proud to support an initiative that helps make public transport more connected, accessible and convenient for customers across the UAE."Chris Snyder, Chief Operating Officer at Via, said: "Passengers increasingly expect transport networks to work together as a single experience. By integrating Etihad Rail services within Citymapper and combining them with other transport modes, we are helping create a more connected and intuitive way for people to move around the UAE."United Trans and Via have a proven track record of supporting innovative mobility solutions across the UAE, including on-demand public transport services in Abu Dhabi, Dubai and Ajman. The integration of Etihad Rail services into Citymapper builds on that experience while supporting a more convenient journey-planning experience for customers as passenger rail services continue to expand.

source_snapshot.title: Hamdan bin Mohammed affirms public wellbeing remains top priority for every investment in Dubai’s future
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 27th October, 2026 (WAM) -- H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence of the UAE, and Chairman of The Executive Council of Dubai, affirmed that, guided by the vision of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai, Dubai is advancing plans that balance economic growth with population expansion, enhance infrastructure readiness and service efficiency, and ensure that development translates into the wellbeing of citizens and residents alike.Chairing a meeting of The Executive Council of Dubai, held today at Emirates Towers, H.H. said: "Under the vision of Mohammed bin Rashid, Dubai has become an exceptional, inspiring, people-centric model. To sustain this model, we are investing in urban centres to develop integrated communities that meet people's aspirations and support sustainable growth. The Urban Centres Development Plan, with a budget exceeding AED2 billion by 2040, will contribute to an increase in the real estate value of the targeted centres by AED20 billion, making them more vibrant places to live, work and invest."Sheikh Hamdan added: "This plan is an investment in Dubai's future and the sustainability of its growth, strengthening its leadership across different domains and its position as a city that places people's wellbeing at the heart of development."H.H. said: "Dubai is a preferred city to live, work and invest, welcoming investors, entrepreneurs and talent, and home to a community of more than 200 nationalities. Today, we approved the Sustainable Population Planning Policy, which links population growth forecasts with our economic and urban plans and guides the development of services and infrastructure in line with residents' needs. Our goal is for Dubai's economic growth to keep pace with the aspirations of its citizens and residents, expand opportunities for individuals and families, and reinforce the emirate's leadership in attracting and investing in talent and skills."Sheikh Hamdan noted: "Ranking second globally in the 2026 Smart City Index, Dubai is among the world's leading cities for digital services, and our ambition is to set a global benchmark for digital government services in ease of access, efficiency and integration. Today, we approved the Digital Authorisation System for individuals and companies to deliver a unified and trusted government experience that serves society and business, and reinforces Dubai's position at the forefront of digital government."H.H. Sheikh Maktoum bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, First Deputy Ruler of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance of the UAE; and H.H. Sheikh Ahmed bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Second Deputy Ruler of Dubai, attended the meeting.The Executive Council approved the Urban Centres Development Plan, which is being overseen by the Supreme Committee for Urban Planning and Dubai Municipality in collaboration with relevant entities. The plan covers six main urban centres and 42 supporting sub-centres across the emirate, accounting for 12% of Dubai's urban area.With a budget exceeding AED2 billion, the plan willcontribute to an increase in the real estate value of the targeted centres by AED20 billion by 2040. It focuses on three pillars; namely: quality of life, economic returns, and infrastructure efficiency and cost, by concentrating population and jobs around mass transit stations, diversifying land use, and bringing homes closer to workplaces.The plan aims to increase the percentage of residents living around metro stations from 52% to 74%, and raise public services coverage from 74% to 85%, improving access to services and public transport and strengthening integration between urban centres.The Council also approved the Sustainable Population Planning Policy, an integrated framework that responds to demographic shifts and links them to economic and urban development. The policy balances the requirements of growth with the efficiency and sustainability of infrastructure, while safeguarding quality of life in line with global best practices.The policy harnesses data and population growth forecasts to determine future needs for services and facilities, and to guide infrastructure development plans across Dubai. It also supports maximising the use of existing infrastructure and services, enhancing their efficiency and ensuring their sustainability.The policy further supports job growth in high-productivity sectors in line with the targets of the Dubai Economic Agenda, D33. It will help attract talent and skills, raise average income for individuals and families, strengthen their purchasing power, and reinforce Dubai's economic competitiveness.To advance government digital services, the Council approved the Digital Authorisation System for individuals and companies. Delivered through a digital platform developed and operated by Digital Dubai, the system enables customers to authorise others to complete transactions on their behalf, within the scope of low-risk services that do not require notary public or legal attestation procedures.The system aims to deliver a 100% digital experience through a unified platform, achieve 100% effectiveness in combating fraud, disputes and operational risks, and achieve a 90% score on the Customer Effort Index, enabling proactive services while reducing effort and simplifying procedures for customers.The system provides a secure, trusted, real-time and paperless mechanism to create, manage and activate authorisations. It uses the UAE PASS digital identity for verification and integrates with digital applications and services to provide a unified experience across all service channels.

source_snapshot.title: UAE driving tests: Why scoring 75% may still not be enough to pass
source_snapshot.text: Learner drivers in the UAE could score at least 75 per cent in their practical driving test and still fail if they make a dangerous mistake, under new regulations that are set to take effect on January 1, 2027, a judicial official told Khaleej Times. The rules, published in the official gazette on October 21, require UAE residents applying for a driving licence to achieve a minimum score of 75 per cent in both theory and practical tests. However, meeting that threshold does not guarantee a pass, as certain dangerous errors can result in automatic failure regardless of the overall score. Judicial counsellor Hesham Elrafei explained that the regulations distinguish between serious mistakes that can trigger automatic failure and smaller errors that are dealt with through the marking system, where points can be deducted. However, the law does not establish one identical marking system for every driving school across the UAE. Detailed assessment criteria are determined by the relevant licensing authorities. When can a learner automatically fail? Under Article 68, dangerous mistakes can result in failure even when a candidate has achieved the required overall score. Examples include losing control of the car, hitting a kerb or barrier, ignoring traffic signs or signals, and making dangerous errors when changing gears. If an examiner has to speak to or physically intervene with a learner to prevent a dangerous situation, the candidate can automatically fail the test. The regulation does not, however, explicitly require the examination to end immediately following such an incident. It also does not specify how feedback must be provided to candidates who fail, leaving these procedures to the relevant licensing authorities. What happens if a learner fails? Under Article 69, applicants who fail the practical driving test will be given another test date by the relevant licensing authority. The regulation does not prescribe a fixed waiting period before a learner can retake the test, nor does it require additional driving lessons as a condition for taking it again. It also does not specify whether candidates must pay another test fee following failure. These details depend on the procedures of the relevant licensing authority. Will the rules affect learners already taking lessons? The new regulations do not exempt applicants who began driving lessons or booked their tests before that date. Learners taking their tests from January 1 should therefore expect to be assessed under the new requirements, even if they began their training months earlier. Driving schools and licensing authorities will need to update their testing procedures, although the regulation does not set out specific preparations they must complete ahead of implementation.

If an examiner has to speak to or physically intervene with a learner to prevent a dangerous situation, the candidate can automatically fail the test.
The regulation does not, however, explicitly require the examination to end immediately following such an incident.
It also does not specify how feedback must be provided to candidates who fail, leaving these procedures to the relevant licensing authorities.
What happens if a learner fails?
Under Article 69, applicants who fail the practical driving test will be given another test date by the relevant licensing authority.
The regulation does not prescribe a fixed waiting period before a learner can retake the test, nor does it require additional driving lessons as a condition for taking it again.
It also does not specify whether candidates must pay another test fee following failure.
These details depend on the procedures of the relevant licensing authority.
Will the rules affect learners already taking lessons?
The new regulations do not exempt applicants who began driving lessons or booked their tests before that date.
Learners taking their tests from January 1 should therefore expect to be assessed under the new requirements, even if they began their training months earlier.
Driving schools and licensing authorities will need to update their testing procedures, although the regulation does not set out specific preparations they must complete ahead of implementation.

source_snapshot.title: Indians travelling to UAE urged to secure adequate medical insurance
source_snapshot.text: The Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi and the Consulate General of India in Dubai and the Northern Emirates have urged Indian residents or tourists in the UAE to ensure they have adequate medical insurance, warning that unforeseen illnesses and medical emergencies can leave patients and their families facing substantial bills. In an advisory shared on X on Tuesday, the Indian missions said they had been receiving several instances of citizens encountering medical emergencies that resulted in huge medical bills beyond the capacity of patients or their family members to bear, with inadequate insurance cover. “All Indian nationals who are travelling to UAE for visit or tourism purposes are hereby advised to take adequate and appropriate medical insurance, prior to commencement of their journey, which also covers cashless facilities including the cost of medical repatriation to India in the event of unforeseen medical emergency,” the advisory stated. The missions have also called on Indians already living in the UAE on employment visas or as dependents to check whether their existing insurance policies provide sufficient coverage. “Indians residing in UAE on employment visa or as dependents are advised to verify that their medical insurance is adequate to cover all medical expenses in UAE and medical repatriation to India,” the advisory added. The advisory highlights the importance of checking the scope of insurance coverage before travelling to the UAE or relying on an existing policy while living in the country. For visitors, this includes confirming that the policy covers medical emergencies, offers cashless facilities where applicable and provides for repatriation to India if required. Residents and dependents have been urged to review their existing coverage to ensure it is adequate for medical expenses in the UAE and medical repatriation.

source_snapshot.title: Department of Municipalities and Transport announces project linking Ramhan and Jubail Islands to Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Highway
source_snapshot.text: ABU DHABI, 27th October, 2026 (WAM) -- The Department of Municipalities and Transport (DMT) has announced plans to open the Ramhan Island bridge network in the second quarter of 2027, as part of a major strategic project involving the construction of a seven-bridge development connecting Ramhan and Jubail Islands to Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed highway (E12). The project is part of DMT’s efforts to enhance mobility links in line with urban and economic development across Abu Dhabi.Upon completion, the development will cover more than 166,000 square metres, at an estimated cost of AED 872 million. It also includes three tunnels and a network of ramps, roads, and utility corridors to improve road accessibility and capacity, and support smoother traffic flow within the vicinity.Eng Eisa Mubarak Almazrouei, Director General of Infrastructure Development at the DMT, said: “This sophisticated construction project represents an important part of Abu Dhabi's evolving transportation network, facilitating access to Ramhan and Jubail Islands while unlocking new development zones and economic opportunities. The initiative exemplifies DMT's strategic approach to creating integrated, liveable communities that enhance quality of life and support the emirate's rapid expansion.”The project also incorporates environmentally conscious design elements, such as the widespread use of energy efficient LED lighting to reduce energy consumption and light pollution. In addition, approximately 90% of the project’s waste, equivalent to over 2,200 tonnes, will be recycled during implementation, in line with the department’s commitment to environmental responsibility and best practices in infrastructure delivery.

source_snapshot.title: Sharjah temporarily closes all its beaches after oil spill off UAE shores
source_snapshot.text: Sharjah has announced the closure of all its beaches after an oil spill from a tanker near UAE's shores was first reported last week. The government announced the closures as a precautionary measure to prevent marine pollution from reaching the shore. Specialised teams and relevant authorities in the emirate are taking necessary measures to ensure the safety of the beaches and prevent the pollution from reaching them, according to the statement. Teams have urged the public and beachgoers to follow issued instructions in order to ensure public safety. The public has also been advised to obtain information from official channels and avoid circulating rumours. The full closure across the emirate's coastline comes after Al Hamriyah Beach was first closed on October 23 as a precaution to prevent pollution from reaching the coast. At the time, fishermen and sea-goers had been urged to adhere to instructions to protect public safety. The reports of an oil spill came after residents across several emirates reported a 'fuel-like' smell for almost three days. The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment confirmed an oil spill off Umm Al Quwain to be the source of the pungent smell. All beaches and coastal areas in Umm Al Quwain have been temporarily closed until teams complete assessments, and identify safety and marine protection measure, the ministry said in its statement. The next day, Ras Al Khaimah announced that it had closed all its beaches "until further notice", although the authority did not immediately disclose the reason. In an interview with Khaleej Times, vendors at Umm Al Quwain's Fish Market confirmed fresh supplies remain available despite a temporary halt in local fishing. Vendors at the market said fresh stock was arriving every day from Oman, with nearly all common varieties available. Meanwhile, local fishing has come to a halt because fishermen are not allowed to go to sea during the restrictions. The closures will remain until technical teams finish assessments. The ministry has said it will release further updates on the incident and response efforts.

source_snapshot.title: Upgraded Wage Protection System enables instant services, digital salary payments
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 28th October, 2026 (WAM) -- The UAE's upgraded Wage Protection System (WPS) enables employers to manage salary payments digitally, eliminating paperwork and the need to visit financial institutions for registration while providing instant access to services.Launched in December 2025 by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MoHRE), in collaboration with the Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE) and Al Etihad Payments, the upgraded system uses secure application programming interfaces (APIs) to enable real-time data exchange, improving the speed, accuracy and reliability of wage payments.Al Etihad Payments, the national payments entity owned by the CBUAE, develops and operates the system's central platform, providing direct connectivity between MoHRE and participating financial institutions.The system is being rolled out progressively through partnerships with seven additional institutions: First Abu Dhabi Bank, Emirates NBD, Dubai Islamic Bank, Mashreq Bank, Ajman Bank, Lari Exchange and First Gulf Exchange Centre.This brings the total number of partners to 17, including Al Ansari Exchange, Lulu Exchange, GCC Exchange, Al Fardan Exchange, Wio Bank, Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank, Al Maryah Community Bank, Habib Bank AG Zurich, e& Group and Botim, extending access to digital wage payment services.The WPS covers more than 99% of private-sector workers, with average monthly wage transfers of AED37 billion, supporting transparency and stability in the UAE labour market.Dalal Al Shehhi, Assistant Undersecretary for Labour Protection at MoHRE, said the upgraded system has evolved from a wage payment compliance mechanism into an integrated digital financial platform that provides reliable labour market data.She said the initiative strengthens social and insurance protection, advances financial inclusion and reduces bureaucracy through artificial intelligence and digital financial governance, supporting the objectives of We the UAE 2031.Dr. Tareq Al Hawi, Chief Operating Officer of Al Etihad Payments, said the platform reflects continued progress in the UAE's digital financial infrastructure and the importance of integrating government entities and financial institutions within a unified, secure operational framework.He highlighted its role in accelerating salary processing, improving data integration and accurately tracking wage transfers to ensure workers receive their salaries on time, in accordance with the highest standards of transparency and protection.Futoon Hamdan Al Mazrouei, Group Head of Personal, Business, Wealth and Privileged Client Banking at First Abu Dhabi Bank, said the upgraded system improves employers' experience and wage management efficiency through closer integration between government entities and financial institutions.Ahmed Al Qassim, Group Head of Wholesale Banking at Emirates NBD, said direct digital connectivity simplifies procedures and enhances the efficiency and reliability of salary payments.Dr. Adnan Chilwan, Group Chief Executive Officer of Dubai Islamic Bank, said the bank's participation reflects its responsibility as a banking partner whose role extends beyond processing transactions to providing practical solutions for businesses and workers, consistent with Islamic banking principles of transparency, fairness and responsibility.He added that continued collaboration would simplify procedures, accelerate payments and provide a smoother experience, supporting labour market stability and a more resilient and sustainable economy.Fernando Morillo, Group Head of Retail Banking at Mashreq, said secure digital payment channels streamline wage administration, advance financial inclusion and improve transparency and operational efficiency, supporting We the UAE 2031 and the country's position as a global centre for innovation and digital services.Mustafa Al Khalfawi, Chief Executive Officer of Ajman Bank, said the bank's participation supports digital transformation and financial inclusion through more efficient and reliable banking solutions, helping employers process salaries efficiently and ensuring workers receive their wages on time.Fouad Abbas Darwish Lari, Chief Executive Officer of Lari Exchange, said direct integration with the central platform improves salary processing and data management while extending reliable digital wage services to more employers and workers.Mohammed Al Otaibi of First Gulf Exchange Centre said employers can register through a secure digital link, create confidential login credentials and establish individual profiles. The exchange centre then reviews, verifies and approves the submitted information in accordance with established procedures.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Future Foundation launches AI Sandbox to accelerate deployment of emerging AI technologies
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 28th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Future Foundation (DFF), through Sandbox Dubai, has launched the AI Sandbox to help local and international technology companies overcome regulatory and policy barriers that can prevent promising artificial intelligence (AI) solutions from moving beyond experimentation into real-world deployment.The initiative will bring together startups, SMEs, established technology companies and relevant government entities, including the Dubai Centre for Artificial Intelligence (DCAI), to test AI-native solutions in real-world environments. Participating companies will benefit from technical, policy and commercial expertise, alongside tailored regulatory guidance to address challenges that may limit deployment.Depending on the use case and applicable requirements, this may include exploring regulatory exemptions, subject to approval by the relevant authorities.The launch addresses a persistent challenge in AI development. Despite growing investment and adoption, 74 percent of companies have yet to move their AI initiatives beyond experimentation, according to research cited by the World Economic Forum. Beyond technological readiness, companies face challenges relating to regulatory requirements, data access and the application of existing policies to emerging technologies.The AI Sandbox will allow innovators and regulators to work together to address these challenges. Through practical testing, regulators will be able to assess emerging applications, identify potential risks and gather evidence to inform future policies. source_snapshot.title: RTA commences construction of two pedestrian bridges at Dubai's Palm Jumeirah
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 29th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Construction has begun on two pedestrian bridges on Palm Jumeirah in a project designed to improve pedestrian safety and ease traffic across the landmark destination. It is a joint project by Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) and Dubai Holding Community Management.The first bridge will be built near Shoreline, at the entrance to Palm Jumeirah, with completion scheduled for June 2027. The second, at Golden Mile adjacent to the retail frontages, is due in October 2027. Together they will have a combined capacity of 2,700 pedestrians per hour — exceeding current demand and allowing for future growth — and are expected to benefit approximately 16,000 residents.Hussain Al Banna, Chief Executive Officer of RTA's Traffic and Roads Agency, said the project reflected the strategic partnership between the RTA and Dubai Holding to integrate infrastructure and road network projects with major developments. He said it built on ongoing cooperation to deliver "integrated traffic solutions that respond to current and future growth requirements, improve connectivity between areas and key facilities, enhance safety and accessibility, and support sustainable urban development across the emirate."Francis Gianni, Chief Executive Officer of Dubai Holding Community Management, said the new bridges would "enhance accessibility and connectivity across Palm Jumeirah, while supporting safer pedestrian movement and smoother traffic flow," adding that the investment reflected a commitment to "creating future-ready communities that put people and their everyday experience at the centre."

source_snapshot.title: Sheikh Zayed Festival opens tomorrow in Al Wathba
source_snapshot.text: ABU DHABI,29th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Under the patronage of President His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, and the follow-up of His Highness Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Vice President, Deputy Prime Minister and Chairman of the Presidential Court, the Sheikh Zayed Festival will open its new 2026/2027 season in Al Wathba, Abu Dhabi, on Friday, 30 October. The festival launches a packed 135-day programme combining cultural, artistic, entertainment, sports and community events, with the participation of dozens of countries and a line-up of leading Arab and Emirati artists, alongside public shows, family activities and interactive experiences that make it a comprehensive destination for visitors from within the UAE and abroad.The new season builds on the journey of a festival that has established its place among the major events in the UAE and the region. Guided by a vision that combines pride in Emirati national identity with openness to world cultures, it offers an integrated experience that goes beyond traditional entertainment into a broader space where art meets culture, sport meets community engagement, and local creativity meets international participation.The festival's Higher Organising Committee confirmed that the festival is ready to welcome visitors from across the UAE, presenting an edition with numerous updates and additions designed to enrich the visitor experience and offer diverse options to suit all groups and interests, reinforcing the festival's position as a leading destination for family and cultural entertainment in the country.The festival's opening will feature a series of celebratory events, including giant installations and artistic performances by participants from around the world, as well as shows at the Fountain Theatre, traditional and military music performances, folkloric heritage competitions and lively entertainment activities, in addition to the fireworks displays that consistently draw wide interest from all visitors.Events will continue throughout the season with a diverse range of shows and interactive experiences, including laser shows, the Al Wathba Floating Market, the Rare Species Reserve and other destinations and activities that offer visitors varied experiences combining entertainment, exploration and interaction.Emirati identity has a strong presence throughout the festival, through the UAE Civilisation pavilions, the Heritage Village and the Popular Souq, as well as handicrafts and live performances that evoke authentic Emirati life. Visitors can learn about aspects of the country's history, culture and traditions in an experience that combines knowledge and enjoyment and connects new generations with their national heritage.Meanwhile, the pavilions of participating countries present diverse programmes and activities reflecting their cultures, customs and arts, allowing the public to discover the experiences, products and traditional cuisines of different peoples in a space where cultures meet and experiences multiply, promoting the values of communication, mutual understanding and cultural openness.A number of government entities and institutions are also taking part in the festival to showcase their activities and programmes through pavilions and programmes that highlight their services, initiatives and areas of work. These include the National Library and Archives, the Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi, the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority, the Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Agricultural Excellence Award, the Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan Foundation, Abu Dhabi Majlis, Presidential Camels, Abu Dhabi Police, the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department, the Zayed Higher Organisation for People of Determination, the Arabian Saluki Centre and falconry, along with other official and community entities and institutions.This season, the festival's amusement park adds an atmosphere of fun and excitement through a variety of new rides and experiences enhanced by virtual reality technology, as well as adventures and activities suitable for all ages.These experiences combine entertainment and innovation, offering children, young people and families a wide range of options to spend enjoyable time within an integrated entertainment environment that caters to visitors' diverse interests and gives them opportunities to discover something new with every visit.The festival also offers a diverse artistic programme featuring art and music performances and specialised festivals, alongside national celebrations and sports and entertainment activities that enrich the events calendar throughout the season.Food experiences occupy a prominent place among the festival's activities, through a food court featuring a variety of traditional restaurants serving Emirati and Gulf cuisine, as well as international restaurants and food trucks offering a wide choice of dishes and flavours to suit all tastes, giving visitors the chance to enjoy a complete journey that combines entertainment with diverse culinary experiences.This space reflects part of the cultural diversity that distinguishes the festival, where local cuisine meets flavours from around the world in a family atmosphere that adds further variety and enjoyment to the visit.Throughout the festival, Al Wathba is transformed into a vibrant destination of events and activities, with experiences spread across the festival's grounds and pavilions. This offers visitors a varied programme of experiences and strengthens the bond between families and friends and the festival as an annual occasion that brings them together in a festive atmosphere.Through the diversity of its programmes and the breadth of its participation, the Sheikh Zayed Festival continues to consolidate its position as a platform bringing together culture, the arts, entertainment and sports, offering an integrated interactive experience that reflects the vibrancy of Abu Dhabi's cultural and entertainment scene and attracts visitors from across the UAE and beyond.The festival welcomes visitors daily from 4 pm until midnight on weekdays, and until 1 am on weekends and public holidays. Events will continue until 13 March next year.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Municipality opens registration for sixth Farmers’ Market season
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 30th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Municipality has opened registration for the sixth season of the Farmers’ Market, offering Emirati farmers and local businesses opportunities to showcase their products and sell directly to consumers.The market will run from 28th November 2026 to 31st January 2027 at Quranic Park in Al Khawaneej, operating every Saturday and Sunday.The new season will feature 52 Emirati farmers and local businesses, representing an approximately 24 percent increase in participation compared with the previous season, which attracted 393,467 visitors.For the first time, the market will also introduce 10 dedicated spaces for children under the "Young Farmers and Entrepreneurs" initiative, allowing them to display and sell products while developing practical skills in agriculture and entrepreneurship.Mohammed Abdulrahman Ahli, Director of the Public Parks and Recreational Facilities Department at Dubai Municipality, said, "The Farmers’ Market has established itself as an important community platform for supporting Emirati farmers and connecting local agricultural producers directly with consumers. Building on the success of previous seasons, we are expanding opportunities for participation and introducing new experiences that strengthen the market's role in promoting locally grown produce and supporting the development of the agricultural sector." “Our focus is on providing farmers with the facilities, resources and guidance they need to develop their businesses, improve production practices and expand their market reach. Through these efforts, we aim to strengthen the competitiveness of local agricultural products and encourage sustainable production while contributing to Dubai's wider food sustainability objectives," he added. Dubai Municipality will provide participating farmers with dedicated market stalls, logistical support, agricultural supplies, training courses, technical consultations and workshops to improve agricultural practices and production efficiency.The market will also feature recreational and educational activities for families and visitors, including opportunities to learn about local agriculture and interact with participating producers.Emirati farmers, eligible home-based businesses and agricultural product vendors can register through the Dubai Municipality registration portal.Applications will be assessed according to the initiative's participation criteria, quality standards and sustainable local production requirements.

source_snapshot.title: ROX delivers first 100 Made in the Emirates vehicles, boosting UAE advanced manufacturing
source_snapshot.text: ABU DHABI, 30th October, 2026 (WAM) -- ROX has announced the delivery of its first batch of 100 UAE-manufactured vehicles bearing the “Made in the Emirates” mark as part of its UAE Signature Edition.The milestone supports the UAE’s efforts to diversify its national industrial base and develop advanced manufacturing capabilities in high-value sectors.The 100 vehicles are the result of collaboration between the Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology (MoIAT), the Abu Dhabi Investment Office (ADIO) and ROX. They were produced at the company’s AI Manufacturing Centre in Khalifa Economic Zones Abu Dhabi (KEZAD), as part of ROX’s efforts to localise its manufacturing operations and expand its presence in Abu Dhabi, while advancing the UAE’s automotive manufacturing capabilities.The project demonstrates the UAE’s industrial and investment ecosystem’s ability to attract international companies and provide the foundations needed to establish and develop local production operations, drawing on advanced infrastructure, logistics services, advanced technology and supportive institutional partnerships.The partnership between ADIO and ROX has supported the company’s establishment and expansion in the emirate, as part of a broader effort to develop the automotive industry in line with the Abu Dhabi Industrial Strategy. This includes building an integrated ecosystem spanning manufacturing, design, advanced technology, and research and development.The industrial project is supported by MoIAT under the Make it in the Emirates initiative, in line with the objectives of the National Strategy for Industry and Advanced Technology (Operation 300bn), which aims to strengthen national industrial capabilities, resilience and competitiveness, accelerate advanced technology adoption, and increase the industrial sector’s contribution to the national economy.Hasan Jasem Al Nowais, Undersecretary of the Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology, said, “The UAE continues to develop an integrated industrial and investment ecosystem that attracts investment. We are focused on expanding the country’s advanced manufacturing base and accelerating the adoption of advanced technology and artificial intelligence, strengthening industry’s contribution to economic diversification and competitiveness, in line with the National Strategy for Industry and Advanced Technology and the Make it in the Emirates initiative.”He added, “ROX’s operations in Abu Dhabi bring together government enablers, investment, advanced manufacturing, technology and industrial infrastructure. The delivery of 100 vehicles bearing the Made in the Emirates mark carries strategic value, creating an opportunity to attract further high-quality investment, develop national capabilities, localise knowledge and build partnerships that drive growth, competitiveness and industrial resilience in the UAE, particularly amid global supply chain challenges.”Al Nowais emphasised, “Together with our partners, we continue to strengthen industrial resilience, develop local supply chains and attract high-quality industrial investment. Our aim is to build a more diverse and resilient industrial base that harnesses modern technology and competes in local, regional and international markets. Built on best-practice production standards, the Made in the Emirates mark has earned credibility in global markets.”Mohammad Ali Al Kamali, Chief Trade and Industry Officer at the Abu Dhabi Investment Office (ADIO), said, “ROX’s journey in Abu Dhabi demonstrates how investment can translate into tangible industrial capabilities and opportunities for global growth. The delivery of the first batch of 100 vehicles reflects the company’s commitment to strengthening its manufacturing operations and associated value chains in the emirate, contributing to the development of an automotive ecosystem that supports the localization of industrial activities and strengthens supply chains.”He added, “As ROX enters the next phase of its growth, Abu Dhabi continues to offer manufacturers competitive advantages through advanced infrastructure, connectivity and partnerships that enable companies to establish and expand their operations and strengthen their ability to compete globally from a single base.”Jarvis, Founder and CEO of ROX, said, “The delivery of our first UAE-manufactured vehicles is an important milestone in ROX’s long-term commitment to Abu Dhabi and the UAE. In a short period, we have established advanced manufacturing, AI and design capabilities that allow us to produce vehicles locally and serve customers across the region.”He added, “We will continue working with our partners to expand our manufacturing operations, develop local capabilities and strengthen the supply chains supporting production. We look forward to establishing the UAE as a base for vehicle manufacturing and contributing to the continued development of an advanced automotive industry ecosystem.”ROX developed its Abu Dhabi facility in six months, bringing manufacturing, design and AI capabilities together. The delivery of the first 100 vehicles bearing the Made in the Emirates mark represents another step towards strengthening the presence of locally manufactured products in the market.The facility includes a Manufacturing Centre, an AI Lab and a Design Studio, supporting ROX’s plans to expand its manufacturing operations in the UAE and meet the needs of regional markets.The commencement of vehicle deliveries reflects efforts to develop local manufacturing capabilities and demonstrates the UAE’s ability to translate investment into the domestic production of value-added products. It also creates opportunities to develop industrial expertise and strengthen integration between manufacturing, design and advanced technology, in line with the national drive to increase value added in the industrial sector.Bringing AI, manufacturing and design capabilities together in a single facility supports the UAE’s industrial ambitions and reinforces efforts to accelerate advanced technology adoption across the industrial sector.The first 100 vehicles carry the Made in the Emirates mark on their bodywork, reflecting the UAE Signature Edition’s connection to its place of manufacture. Each vehicle in this edition is a luxury SUV produced through a precise and numbered production process designed to meet regional market needs.The delivery of the first batch of 100 vehicles establishes a foundation for the next phase of ROX’s manufacturing operations in Abu Dhabi. Continued production at ICAD/KEZAD is expected to support the company’s plans to expand into regional markets while contributing to the growth of the UAE’s advanced manufacturing base.The project’s progress also reflects the ongoing efforts of ADIO and MoIAT to support industrial investment, develop local manufacturing capabilities and provide an enabling environment for companies to expand from Abu Dhabi into regional and international markets.

source_snapshot.title: Hamdan bin Mohammed announces new initiatives to further enhance competitiveness of Dubai’s tourism sector
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 1st November, 2026 (WAM) -- H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, and Chairman of The Executive Council of Dubai, has announced two new initiatives to further enhance the competitiveness of Dubai’s tourism sector.Aimed at facilitating access for visitors, strengthening visitors’ connection with the city and providing a seamless travel experience, the initiatives support the goals of the Dubai Economic Agenda, D33, to position Dubai among the world’s top three global destinations for business and leisure.The measures include the launch of the world’s first city-led, invitation-only tourism membership programme, and a new option to apply for tourist visas through Visit Dubai, the city’s official tourism website. Both initiatives, which will be implemented during November 2026, have been developed through a collaboration between the General Directorate of Identity and Foreigners Affairs – Dubai (GDRFA Dubai), the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism (DET) and Digital Dubai under the Shared Digital Channels Initiative, which brings government services together through unified digital platforms.Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid said, “Under the wise leadership of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister and Ruler of Dubai, the emirate continues to enhance its appeal as a leading global tourism hub through innovation, outstanding services and memorable experiences.We are committed to positioning Dubai among the world’s top three tourism destinations through initiatives that enrich every stage of the visitor journey and set new standards for hospitality and service excellence. Our goal is to make the city the preferred choice for travellers worldwide and a global benchmark for quality and convenience.”Sheikh Hamdan added, “Tourism is a key pillar of Dubai’s economy. By harnessing technology, fostering innovation and strengthening public-private partnerships, we aim to attract more investment, open up new opportunities and strengthen the sector’s contribution to long-term growth, in line with the Dubai Economic Agenda, D33.”Dubai Access Club, a membership programme for repeat visitors, will provide invited members with exclusive experiences, services and benefits. Designed to encourage repeat visitation, the programme will make returning to Dubai easier and more rewarding.Dubai Access Club will bring together exclusive offers and benefits that enrich the visitor experience and give travellers more reasons to come back to the city. Its launch builds on Dubai’s long-term approach to deepening visitors’ connection with the destination, fostering lasting relationships that encourage recommendations, repeat visits and engagement with the city’s economy and business community.Under the Shared Digital Channels Initiative, more government services, including tourist visa applications, are being integrated into Visit Dubai, the city’s official tourism website. The platform is bringing these services together with the information and tools that support every stage of the visitor journey, from discovering attractions and experiences to booking tickets, exploring events and planning itineraries. Visitors will be able to access the services they need through a single channel, without navigating multiple websites, applications, or entities.As part of this, Visit Dubai will offer applications for single-entry and multiple-entry tourist visas, with plans to introduce further visa categories in the future. GDRFA Dubai remains responsible for assessing visa applications and issuing visas, with further service details to be announced in due course.The initiatives reflect Dubai’s continued efforts to advance its tourism ecosystem, enhance the visitor experience, and further strengthen the city’s global appeal, driving the sector’s growth and its contribution to the goals of the Dubai Economic Agenda, D33.Helal Saeed Almarri, Director-General of the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism, said, “Guided by the vision of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum and the directives of H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Dubai continues to focus on creating new opportunities for growth, strengthening its global connectivity and making it easier for people to visit, do business and invest in the city.Tourism plays a critical role in this ambition, generating economic value well beyond the sector itself. These initiatives are about removing barriers, creating greater value for visitors and giving people more reasons to return to Dubai. Equally important is the collaboration between government and the private sector to translate these opportunities into tangible economic impact, supporting businesses, stimulating demand and contributing to the wider objectives of the Dubai Economic Agenda, D33.”Lieutenant General Mohammed Ahmed Al Marri, Director-General of the General Directorate of Identity and Foreigners Affairs – Dubai, said the initiatives launched by Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum reflect Dubai’s vision to provide visitors with an exceptional, seamless experience from the moment they plan their journey until their departure.He said, “At GDRFA Dubai, we work closely with our strategic partners to simplify procedures, improve access to government services and harness advanced digital solutions. Enabling visitors to apply for tourist visas through the Visit Dubai platform is an important step towards integrating services into a single digital journey while maintaining the highest standards of security and efficiency.”He added, “Excellence in government services is measured not only by speed and technology, but also by the ease and confidence visitors experience. Through stronger government integration and public-private partnerships, we aim to deliver a seamless journey that reflects Dubai’s hospitality and innovation, encourages repeat visits and supports the objectives of the Dubai Economic Agenda, D33.Hamad Obaid Al Mansoori, Director-General of Digital Dubai, said, “These initiatives reflect the vision of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum to build a government that anticipates people’s needs, and the directives of Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum to develop a more integrated and efficient digital government ecosystem. The Shared Digital Channels Initiative brings services together through connected platforms, enabling people to access what they need through a seamless experience, regardless of the entity providing the service.”He added, “Enabling visitors to apply for tourist visas through the Visit Dubai platform, in collaboration with the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism and GDRFA Dubai, is a practical example of this approach. By harnessing data and AI, we aim to make services more personalised and proactive, enhancing the visitor experience, strengthening Dubai’s global competitiveness and supporting the Dubai Economic Agenda D33 and the emirate’s ambition to rank among the world’s top three tourist destinations.”In February 2025, Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum approved the Shared Digital Channels Initiative, led by Digital Dubai, to establish a more integrated, user-centric model for delivering government services. The initiative brings together public and private sector services across seven unified platforms and harnesses advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence, to personalise services and proactively meet users’ needs, reinforcing Dubai’s global leadership in digital government and innovation.
