source_snapshot.title: Mohammed bin Rashid witnesses announcement of Nad Zabeel, Dubai’s Future RDI Campus
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 1st November, 2026 (WAM) -- His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President, Prime Minister and Ruler of Dubai, witnessed the announcement of Nad Zabeel, Dubai’s Future RDI Campus.The new architectural and knowledge landmark will serve as a major centre within Dubai’s research, development and innovation ecosystem, and an incubator for global partnerships, initiatives and ambitious research projects. It will further reinforce Dubai’s position as a trusted regional and global centre for knowledge creation and advanced technology development.The project was launched by H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence of the UAE, and Chairman of the Board of Trustees of Dubai Future Foundation.H.H. Sheikh Mansoor bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Chairman of the UAE Olympic Committee, and Her Highness Sheikha Latifa bint Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Chairperson of Dubai Culture and Arts Authority, attended the event along with several senior officials.H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum said: “Guided by the vision of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Dubai became the first city in the world to institutionalise an integrated government framework centred on anticipating and shaping the future. This transformed future thinking from a series of standalone initiatives and projects into a sustainable institutional approach.“This journey began years ago, turning Mohammed bin Rashid’s vision into an integrated ecosystem of institutions, initiatives and projects that design the future and prepare for its transformations.”H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed added: “Today, this ecosystem includes the Museum of the Future, Dubai Future Foundation, Dubai Future Accelerators, Dubai Future Labs and Dubai Future Academy. Together, these institutions and initiatives anticipate transformations, develop talent, test solutions and translate ideas into practical applications.“We continue this journey today with the launch of Nad Zabeel, a major addition to Dubai’s future-shaping ecosystem and a global centre bringing scientific research, development and innovation together to transform knowledge into new economic and development opportunities.”H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed noted: “Shaping the future in Dubai is not a slogan or a temporary project, but an integrated institutional system established by Mohammed bin Rashid that we continue to develop and build upon.“Our goal is to keep Dubai ahead in anticipating global transformations, developing solutions to future challenges, attracting the world’s leading minds and expertise, and reinforcing its position as a global centre for knowledge creation and shaping the future.”Mohammad Abdullah Al Gergawi, Minister of Cabinet Affairs, Vice Chairman of the Board of Trustees and Managing Director of Dubai Future Foundation, said: “Nad Zabeel translates the vision of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum into action by establishing research and development as a key driver of progress and economic opportunity.“The campus will provide a global institutional platform bringing researchers, universities, technology companies, investors and government entities together within one environment. This will strengthen Dubai’s position as a trusted destination for scientific talent and knowledge investment, and an influential centre in the future economy.”Nad Zabeel will become a major centre for designing and developing the future of vital sectors central to human life, including artificial intelligence, robotics, advanced technology, urban technologies, and health and environmental technologies.It will add new institutional and research capacity to Dubai’s efforts to develop future sectors and increase their contribution to the economy.The campus builds upon Dubai’s integrated ecosystem spanning foresight, research, development, innovation and future skills, which has been progressively institutionalised since 2016. This ecosystem includes Dubai Future Foundation, Dubai Future Accelerators, the Museum of the Future, Dubai Future Labs, and Dubai Future Academy, alongside economic districts and specialised centres serving vital sectors.Nad Zabeel will add dedicated research infrastructure that brings partners together to accelerate the development and application of new solutions.Located in Zabeel Park, Nad Zabeel will house laboratories, scientific and research centres, and creative and innovation incubators. It will bring together leading scientists, researchers, engineers, innovators and future pioneers, alongside specialised talent and expertise from the UAE, the region and around the world.Construction and associated operations are expected to be completed within five years under the supervision of Dubai Future Foundation.Situated in central Dubai, the campus will be within one kilometre of several of the city’s most prominent landmarks and business centres, including Burj Khalifa, Dubai International Financial Centre, the Museum of the Future, Emirates Towers, and Dubai Frame. It will become a global destination for innovators, researchers and future shapers.Nad Zabeel will host leading global technology companies, academic institutions, universities, renowned institutes and government entities, alongside leading experts, scientists, engineers, innovators and future pioneers from multiple fields.The campus will also provide a base for entities developing future legislation, in addition to promising start-ups, and local and international investment companies. It will include leisure facilities and dedicated spaces for scientific and professional events and gatherings.Nad Zabeel will strengthen collaboration between government, investors, researchers and start-ups through accelerator and incubator programmes that support promising companies and help them access the investment required to grow and scale.More than 30,000 scientists, researchers and entrepreneurs are expected to participate in its programmes and events annually.Aligned with D33 goalsThe launch of Nad Zabeel supports the objectives of the Dubai Economic Agenda (D33), launched by His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum. D33 comprises 100 transformative projects and aims to double the size of Dubai’s economy by 2033 while consolidating its position among the world’s top three cities for business.The campus will support these objectives by strengthening the knowledge economy, attracting specialised investment and talent, accelerating the growth of technology companies and start-ups, and creating an environment that connects scientific research with commercial development and future legislation. This will strengthen Dubai’s competitiveness and its ability to lead new high-value sectors.Nad Zabeel will serve as an incubator for the efforts and initiatives of the Dubai Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Ecosystem, established under the directives of His Highness Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum in December 2025.Overseen by Dubai Future Foundation, the ecosystem provides an umbrella for current and future projects and initiatives across research, development and innovation.It supports government and private sector entities in Dubai and across the UAE in developing high-impact ideas based on emerging technologies and advanced applications. It also provides a framework that integrates research efforts and connects them with economic, social and development priorities.The name Nad Zabeel draws on the Emirati word ‘nad,’ meaning elevated ground. It reflects the campus’s distinctive architectural character and embodies Dubai’s ambition to reach new heights in research, knowledge and innovation.

This ecosystem includes Dubai Future Foundation, Dubai Future Accelerators, the Museum of the Future, Dubai Future Labs, and Dubai Future Academy, alongside economic districts and specialised centres serving vital sectors.Nad Zabeel will add dedicated research infrastructure that brings partners together to accelerate the development and application of new solutions.Located in Zabeel Park, Nad Zabeel will house laboratories, scientific and research centres, and creative and innovation incubators.

It will bring together leading scientists, researchers, engineers, innovators and future pioneers, alongside specialised talent and expertise from the UAE, the region and around the world.Construction and associated operations are expected to be completed within five years under the supervision of Dubai Future Foundation.Situated in central Dubai, the campus will be within one kilometre of several of the city’s most prominent landmarks and business centres, including Burj Khalifa, Dubai International Financial Centre, the Museum of the Future, Emirates Towers, and Dubai Frame.

It will become a global destination for innovators, researchers and future shapers.Nad Zabeel will host leading global technology companies, academic institutions, universities, renowned institutes and government entities, alongside leading experts, scientists, engineers, innovators and future pioneers from multiple fields.The campus will also provide a base for entities developing future legislation, in addition to promising start-ups, and local and international investment companies.

It will include leisure facilities and dedicated spaces for scientific and professional events and gatherings.Nad Zabeel will strengthen collaboration between government, investors, researchers and start-ups through accelerator and incubator programmes that support promising companies and help them access the investment required to grow and scale.More than 30,000 scientists, researchers and entrepreneurs are expected to participate in its programmes and events annually.Aligned with D33 goalsThe launch of Nad Zabeel supports the objectives of the Dubai Economic Agenda (D33), launched by His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum.

D33 comprises 100 transformative projects and aims to double the size of Dubai’s economy by 2033 while consolidating its position among the world’s top three cities for business.The campus will support these objectives by strengthening the knowledge economy, attracting specialised investment and talent, accelerating the growth of technology companies and start-ups, and creating an environment that connects scientific research with commercial development and future legislation.

This will strengthen Dubai’s competitiveness and its ability to lead new high-value sectors.Nad Zabeel will serve as an incubator for the efforts and initiatives of the Dubai Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Ecosystem, established under the directives of His Highness Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum in December 2025.Overseen by Dubai Future Foundation, the ecosystem provides an umbrella for current and future projects and initiatives across research, development and innovation.It supports government and private sector entities in Dubai and across the UAE in developing high-impact ideas based on emerging technologies and advanced applications.

It also provides a framework that integrates research efforts and connects them with economic, social and development priorities.The name Nad Zabeel draws on the Emirati word ‘nad,’ meaning elevated ground.
It reflects the campus’s distinctive architectural character and embodies Dubai’s ambition to reach new heights in research, knowledge and innovation.

source_snapshot.title: RTA to launch first integrated smart monitoring system for delivery motorcycles
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 3rd November, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) is set to launch the first integrated smart monitoring system for delivery motorcycles. The initiative reflects RTA’s leading role in leveraging advanced technologies and smart data to develop its monitoring and regulatory system, strengthen road safety, and improve compliance with approved regulations and requirements.The system is also designed to support delivery companies in managing their fleets more efficiently, using real-time operational data to lead decision-making and enhance the quality of their services.Saeed Al Ramsi, Director of Licensing Activities Monitoring at RTA, said: “The new system marks a step-change in monitoring of delivery activity. It covers a smart digital platform, IoT-enabled monitoring devices, and advanced cameras fitted to delivery motorcycles.“The system will gather and analyse data on driving indicators and on-road behaviour, including speed, sudden acceleration, harsh braking, driving patterns, location and route. This will allow operational performance to be tracked and unsafe practices detected with greater accuracy and efficiency.”Al Ramsi added: “The system reflects RTA’s shift from conventional monitoring to proactive, data-driven oversight underpinned by smart analytics. It is also the result of ongoing cooperation with Dubai Police General Command and relevant entities in developing an integrated system that balances operational efficiency with safety and compliance requirements.“By giving companies practical tools to monitor the performance of their fleets and riders in real time, the system will enable them to take early corrective and awareness measures, thereby improving delivery service quality and raising safety and security standards across this vital sector.”He explained that the platform will provide advanced operational indicators to help delivery companies upgrade their fleet management systems, analyse driving patterns, and leverage real data and precise performance indicators to guide training and awareness programmes.These capabilities will contribute to fostering a culture of safe riding and reinforcing compliance with traffic regulations and guidelines. Al Ramsi stressed that the system’s success depends on regulatory authorities, operating companies and riders each fulfilling their part in ensuring a safer and more sustainable operating environment for all road users.Al Ramsi noted that installing the monitoring devices and connecting to the platform will be optional from the system’s launch until the end of the first half of 2027. This will allow companies to complete their technical and operational readiness and benefit from the system’s features. Implementation will become mandatory once the transitional period ends. Throughout this phase, RTA will step up coordination with delivery companies and relevant entities, providing the support needed to ensure readiness for the new requirements and achieve a smooth and effective rollout.The system will bolster RTA’s efforts to strengthen governance of the delivery sector, where demand and the number of motorcycles on the emirate’s streets are growing rapidly. By establishing an integrated operational database, it will help develop regulatory and oversight policies and procedures, improve field monitoring efficiency, and encourage companies to adopt safer, more sustainable operating practices.The launch forms part of RTA’s strategy to harness smart technologies and advanced data to strengthen oversight and compliance. It also complements ongoing regulatory efforts to raise safety and security standards in delivery operations, improve service quality, and reinforce Dubai’s position as a leading global city for smart, safe and sustainable mobility.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Land Department launches enhanced Ejari service through DubaiNow app
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 2nd November, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Land Department (DLD) has launched an enhanced Ejari service through the DubaiNow app, simplifying the customer journey and making real estate services more accessible, efficient, secure and transparent. The enhanced service brings key tenancy procedures together within a unified government platform.The enhanced digital journey lets customers create and register tenancy contracts through a single process, with the Ejari certificate issued immediately after contract approval. Customers can also renew and cancel contracts through a digital process connecting landlords and tenants through UAE PASS, supporting faster completion and greater security and transparency throughout the tenancy lifecycle.The upgraded Ejari service also lets customers pay their DEWA security deposit directly within the same digital journey, enabling them to activate electricity and water services for the property.This enhancement is part of the ongoing cooperation and digital integration between the Dubai Electricity and Water Authority and the Dubai Land Department, reinforcing the ‘One Government’ concept and elevating the customer experience.The enhancement supports DLD’s implementation of the Dubai Government’s ‘Services 360’ policy, which focuses on delivering seamless, proactive and integrated services centred on customer needs. The approach brings related services together within efficient digital journeys.The enhanced Ejari journey through ‘DubaiNow’ puts this approach into practice by enabling customers to complete multiple procedures through a clear and connected process, supporting quality of life and easier access to digital government services.The enhanced service also supports the objectives of the Dubai Economic Agenda D33 and the Dubai Digital Strategy by advancing government service integration, improving the efficiency of digital services and reinforcing Dubai’s position as a global leader in seamless and intelligent government services.Mohammed Ali Al Badwawi, CEO of the Real Estate Registration Sector at Dubai Land Department, said: “The launch of the enhanced Ejari service through DubaiNow represents another milestone in the evolution of Dubai’s digital real estate services. In cooperation with our strategic partners, we continue to simplify procedures and create a more integrated, seamless experience for customers by bringing the tenancy journey together through a trusted government platform. This approach accelerates service delivery, enhances transparency and provides a secure and interactive digital experience that meets the expectations of Dubai’s community.”Dr Moza Suwaidan, Executive Director of the Digital Applications and Platforms Sector at the Digital Dubai Government Establishment, said: “In collaboration with our government partners, we are translating the directives of His Highness Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence of the UAE, and Chairman of the Executive Council of Dubai, into practical steps that strengthen shared digital channels and advance the concept of a unified government, where entities, services and systems work together to deliver a connected customer experience. Integrating the Ejari service into DubaiNow reflects this approach by bringing services and procedures associated with the housing journey into a single digital experience, creating a more connected and convenient journey for customers.”She added: “The customer remains at the heart of Dubai’s digital services ecosystem. We measure the success of digital transformation through its impact on people’s lives: fewer steps, greater time savings and a smoother overall experience.”Marwan Bin Haidar, Executive Vice President of Innovation and the Future at DEWA, said: “Guided by the directives of His Highness Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence of the UAE, and Chairman of the Executive Council of Dubai, we continue to strengthen Dubai’s digital leadership and deliver proactive, customer-focused government services. Integrating DEWA’s services with Ejari through the DubaiNow app supports our efforts to accelerate digital transformation and improve the customer experience through closer government cooperation. This integration enables customers to pay the security deposit and activate electricity and water services through a unified, seamless digital journey, streamlining procedures, saving time and effort, and enhancing quality of life. It also supports the objectives of the Dubai Economic Agenda D33 and reinforces Dubai’s position as a leading digital city globally.”

Al-Futtaim also confirms hospitality concepts that M&S has not used before.M&S food halls built their name on premium own-brand ready meals, bakery and chilled food. British staples such as crumpets, scones and Colin the Caterpillar sweets drive the loyalty. The Dubai format adds counters and cooked-to-order food beyond that packaged core.By combining greater choice, fresh food, convenience, meal solutions and hospitality, the Foodhall is designed to make the quality and value associated with M&S Food relevant across more everyday shopping occasions..Setting a new benchmarkWassim Arabi, President of Retail at Al-Futtaim, says the store will set a new benchmark for food retail in the UAE."The launch of this new Foodhall is an important milestone in that journey, bringing an exciting, elevated food shopping experience to our customers. source_snapshot.title: Sharjah desert gatherings allowed, police clarify rules
source_snapshot.text: Sharjah: Residents are free to visit and gather in open desert areas across Sharjah and will not be fined simply for sitting with friends or family, a senior police official has clarified in response to complaints about violations issued to motorists in the desert.Brigadier Khalid Al Kay, Director of the Traffic and Patrols Department at Sharjah Police, addressed the issue during the direct line programme, broadcast on Sharjah TV and Radio, after a resident called in to complain that five vehicles had received violations while their occupants were spending time together in an open desert area.Al Kay stressed that there was no blanket ban on entering open desert areas and that residents were free to take their vehicles into such locations, provided they complied with traffic regulations and respected restrictions in designated zones."There is no general ban on entering open areas. We have not prevented people from going into desert areas. Entry is permitted to everyone, and we do not restrict people's freedom to take their vehicles into these areas," Al Kay said. .Five vehicles receive violations. During the programme, the caller said the group had been sitting in the desert when authorities issued violations against all five vehicles. The offence was reportedly recorded as (gathering violation), leaving the motorists confused about whether gathering in desert areas was permitted.The caller said the group had wondered whether the fines were related to playing loud music, causing a disturbance, driving close to residential neighbourhoods, entering a restricted military area or shining lights towards the sand.The violations had left the group worried about whether they could continue visiting the desert without risking further penalties.Responding to the complaint, Al Kay stressed that simply being present in an open area with friends or family did not constitute an offence. .Restrictions apply in designated areas. Al Kay clarified that residents are free to drive into open desert areas, but must observe restrictions at specific locations where entry, stopping or parking is prohibited. Such areas are clearly marked with signs alerting motorists to the restrictions.He stressed that simply gathering with friends or family in open areas does not constitute a violation, adding that police would look into the complaint involving the five vehicles to establish why the fines were issued."We will follow up on this matter and verify the exact reasons for issuing these violations," he said.Al Kay reiterated that access to open desert areas was permitted and that the authorities had not imposed a general restriction on residents visiting these locations. However, motorists must comply with traffic regulations and respect signs prohibiting entry or parking in restricted areas. .Police patrols monitor roads and open areas.Al Kay also highlighted the role of police patrols in monitoring vehicle movement, maintaining road safety and assisting members of the public across the emirate.He said patrols were deployed along highway roads and in different areas to oversee traffic movement, guide motorists and provide assistance whenever required. .Sharjah Police to confiscate noisy vehicles.Sharjah rolls out residential parking permits in three neighbourhoods.Sharjah bans car shades outside private property, warns of fines and removal.Sharjah Police seize 8 cars after reckless rain stunts

source_snapshot.title: UAE allows authorised doctors, essential workers to exceed speed limits by 40km/h
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Doctors authorised to respond to medical emergencies and drivers of certain essential service vehicles in the UAE may exceed speed limits by up to 40km/h on roads outside built-up areas under a ministerial decision setting out the circumstances in which they can be granted priority on roads.The decision provides exemptions from three types of traffic violations when authorised drivers exercise road priority.According to Arabic daily Al Khaleej newspaper, these include exceeding the speed limit by no more than 40km/h on roads outside built-up areas, using road shoulders and lanes designated for emergency vehicles when traffic is stationary or congested, and using designated bus lanes.However, drivers must comply with traffic regulations, exercise caution around other road users and refrain from crossing red traffic lights. They must also observe posted speed limits near schools, hospitals and residential areas.The decision identifies four categories of essential services eligible for road priority and sets out six obligations for authorised drivers, along with four conditions doctors must meet to qualify for emergency response permits.Who qualifies for priority on UAE roads?The decision covers vehicles providing emergency medical response services for doctors, public road services operated by government entities or their contractors, vehicle recovery services travelling to the scene of an accident or breakdown, and traffic accident scene mapping services.These vehicles may be granted priority in four circumstances: partial or general restrictions, traffic congestion or obstruction, emergencies and adverse weather conditions, and traffic accidents.For doctors, priority applies to emergency medical response services at hospitals or healthcare facilities approved to receive patients when a rapid response is required.These include medical emergencies and cases in which a doctor is called from one emirate to another.Three traffic exemptionsUnder the decision, authorised drivers exercising road priority are exempt from three categories of traffic violations.The first concerns exceeding the legal speed limit by no more than 40km/h on roads outside built-up areas.The second permits the use of road shoulders and lanes reserved for emergency vehicles when traffic is stationary or congested.The third allows authorised drivers to use designated bus lanes.These exemptions apply only when the conditions for exercising road priority are met.Six obligations for driversThe decision sets out six requirements for drivers of vehicles authorised to use road priority.Drivers must complete a training course approved by the traffic enforcement or licensing authority before obtaining a road priority permit.They must not use warning signs approved in the UAE unless they have obtained the required permit in accordance with the applicable provisions.They must also comply with all traffic rules and exercise caution around other road users, particularly by not crossing red traffic lights because of the risk of serious accidents.Authorised drivers must give way to fire emergency vehicles, vehicles transporting patients and injured people, police, civil defence and ambulances, as well as official motorcades travelling to carry out their duties.They must also observe posted speed limits near schools, hospitals and residential areas.Four conditions for doctorsDoctors seeking authorisation to use the emergency response service must meet four requirements.They must belong to one of the essential medical specialties included in the service and approved by the committee established for that purpose.They must also complete a training course approved by the traffic enforcement or licensing authority, obtain approval to use the service and hold a valid medical licence in the UAE.Operations room must be notifiedThe decision requires drivers of authorised essential service vehicles to notify the relevant operations room when providing the service.Road priority must also be obtained through the traffic enforcement authority.The requirements govern how essential service vehicles can exercise priority on UAE roads while complying with the safety obligations specified in the decision.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai court upholds student's dismissal over AI-written thesis
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: A master's student has lost the legal battle to overturn his dismissal from university over academic misconduct in his thesis, after Dubai's Court of Cassation rejected his appeal and Dh100,000 compensation claim.The court upheld the university's decision to dismiss the student and ordered him to pay legal costs and Dh2,000 in lawyers' fees. It also ruled that he would lose his appeal security deposit.The Court of Cassation issued its ruling on October 29.The student had enrolled in a master’s programme in international dispute resolution law, completed his coursework and examinations, and reached the thesis stage before the university initiated disciplinary proceedings.On December 7, 2023, the university's academic integrity officer emailed the student, alleging that his thesis was not his own work..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..An investigation report dated February 8, 2024, submitted by an investigator from Birmingham Law School to the Faculty Conduct Committee, concluded that the student had used artificial intelligence to generate parts of his thesis and had copied and pasted material without properly acknowledging the sources.The committee subsequently dismissed him from the programme. His internal appeal against the decision was also rejected.The student then filed a lawsuit seeking to overturn the university's decision and its academic consequences. He asked to be reinstated, allowed to complete and submit his thesis, and awarded his master's degree. He also sought Dh100,000 in compensation for material and moral damages.The Court of First Instance dismissed his case on February 10, 2025. The Court of Appeal later appointed an expert and upheld the dismissal on July 30, 2026.In his final appeal, the student argued that AI-detection software was unreliable and could not provide conclusive evidence of misconduct. He also challenged the expert's findings, arguing that the expert had gone beyond the scope of the assignment by examining the thesis content and its legal references.He further argued that the university's decision was excessive and that a lesser disciplinary measure should have been imposed.However, the Court of Cassation found that concerns over the reliability of AI-detection tools did not invalidate the other evidence of academic misconduct..The expert had identified problems beyond the alleged use of AI, including fabricated or inaccurate legal references and judicial rulings that did not exist or had been incorrectly presented. The court considered these findings sufficient to support the conclusion that academic misconduct had occurred.It also rejected the argument that the expert had exceeded the scope of the assignment, ruling that examining the thesis content and verifying its legal references were relevant to assessing the work's integrity.The court further explained that a claim for compensation requires proof of wrongdoing, actual damage and a direct causal link between them. As the university's disciplinary decision was lawful, the student had not established the wrongdoing required to justify compensation.The Court of Cassation therefore rejected the appeal and upheld the previous judgments..AI use in academic research is not misconduct, UAE expert explainsUsing artificial intelligence in academic research is not academic misconduct, but submitting unverified AI-generated information, including fabricated references and fictitious court judgments, can undermine academic integrity, a UAE legal expert has warned.Dr Ammar Ali, a legal consultant specialising in AI governance , said the key issue was not whether researchers used AI, but whether they took responsibility for checking the accuracy of its output.Researchers who rely on AI-generated material without verification risk compromising the credibility of their work, particularly when it contains non-existent academic sources or inaccurate legal references.Universities must establish clear AI policiesUnder Article 16, Clause 9, of Federal Decree-Law No. 31 of 2025 on Higher Education and Scientific Research, higher education institutions in the UAE are required to uphold institutional governance, transparency and disclosure.These obligations include managing risks, protecting academic integrity and ensuring the quality of decision-making.Dr Ali said universities' responsibilities extend beyond identifying academic violations and imposing disciplinary penalties. They must also introduce clear, proactive policies governing the responsible use of AI in research and education.These policies should specify students' and researchers' obligations and establish procedures for checking the accuracy and reliability of AI-generated content.The aim, he said, should be to encourage technological innovation without compromising academic standards, while ensuring that disciplinary procedures are fair and penalties proportionate to the seriousness of any violation.UNESCO calls for human oversightThe need for human supervision is also highlighted in UNESCO's 2023 guidance on generative AI in education and research.Dr Ali pointed to sections 4.2 and 4.3, which address the protection of human agency and the monitoring and validation of generative AI systems. The guidance stresses the importance of verifying the reliability and suitability of AI tools for educational and research purposes.The European commission's 2022 ethical guidelines on the use of artificial intelligence and data in teaching and learning identify four fundamental principles: human agency, fairness, humanity and justified choice.Human agency is particularly important because it ensures that people retain control over decisions and remain accountable when using AI systems.Researchers remain responsible for their workDr Ali said researchers must not treat AI-generated information as automatically reliable or allow technology to replace independent thinking and human judgement.This is particularly important when preparing scientific research, assessing academic work and making decisions that could affect academic outcomes.The principles also reinforce the importance of transparency, accountability, human oversight and data protection.He stressed that responsibility must be shared between researchers and educational institutions. Researchers must verify the accuracy of information and references, while universities must establish clear rules for AI use and ensure fair investigations when academic violations are suspected.Any disciplinary action must also be proportionate to the nature and seriousness of the violation."AI governance in education does not mean restricting innovation. It means ensuring that AI is used in a way that protects academic integrity and reinforces human responsibility for scientific outputs," Dr Ali said..Sharjah launches ethical framework for AI use in schools.Emirati researcher develops AI platform to detect deepfakes and fake content.UAE explores how AI can reshape higher education.UAE accelerates efforts to integrate artificial intelligence into higher education

source_snapshot.title: Dubai International retains world's busiest international airport title with 8.94 million seats in November
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Dubai International Airport has retained its position as the world's busiest airport for scheduled international seat capacity in November, with airlines offering 4.47 million departing seats, equivalent to approximately 8.94 million seats in both directions, according to aviation data provider OAG.The airport maintained a lead of nearly 680,000 seats over London's Heathrow Airport, which ranked second with 3.79 million international seats, the latest figures showed..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..Dubai International remained at the top of the global rankings for international flights despite a 16 per cent decline in scheduled seat capacity compared with November 2025, OAG reported. Seoul's Incheon International Airport ranked third with 3.7 million seats, followed by Singapore's Changi Airport with 3.58 million and Amsterdam's Schiphol Airport with 3.25 million.Hong Kong International Airport placed sixth with 3.19 million seats, ahead of Istanbul Airport with 3.16 million and Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport with 3.08 million.Bangkok's Suvarnabhumi Airport ranked ninth with 2.82 million seats, while Frankfurt Airport completed the top 10 with 2.65 million.The figures are based on the number of seats airlines have scheduled on international flights, rather than actual passenger numbers. source_snapshot.title: UAE to allow two-year car registration from January 2027: Who qualifies?
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Motorists in the UAE will be able to apply for two-year registration for eligible light vehicles under new federal traffic regulations taking effect on January 1, 2027, replacing the standard annual renewal requirement for vehicles that meet three conditions.The change is outlined in Article 98 of Cabinet Decision No. 174 of 2026, which approves the Executive Regulation of Federal Decree-Law No. 14 of 2024 on the Regulation of Traffic..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..Under the new rules, vehicle registration will generally remain valid for one year and renewable for the same period. However, licensing authorities may approve a two-year registration for light vehicles at the owner's request, provided they meet specific requirements.Who qualifies for two-year vehicle registration?Article 98 sets out three conditions for obtaining the extended registration period.First, the vehicle must have been newly manufactured when it was first registered.Second, it must be no more than six years old from its date of manufacture.Third, the vehicle must be owned by an individual rather than a company or other legal entity.All three conditions must be met for the licensing authority to consider an application for two-year registration.The provision gives authorities discretion to approve the longer validity period, meaning qualifying vehicles will not automatically receive two-year registration.The regulations do not specify whether additional fees or other requirements will apply to motorists seeking the extended registration period.Right-hand-drive vehicles prohibitedThe new regulations also prohibit the registration of right-hand-drive vehicles for road use in the UAE, although such vehicles may be permitted for display purposes.Vehicles that fail to meet the prescribed road safety requirements will not be eligible for registration.Owners seeking to register vehicles, or their legally authorised representatives, must submit applications through the channels or digital platforms approved by the relevant licensing authority and follow its procedures.Vehicles with registrations expired for more than five yearsArticle 117 gives licensing authorities the power to remove vehicles from traffic records if their registration has remained expired for more than five years.The measure is not automatic. Authorities may exercise this power in accordance with their approved procedures and requirements.The same article permits the suspension of vehicle registration if an owner changes the vehicle's body, engine or colour without prior authorisation, or if a court orders the suspension.Registration may also be cancelled if the chassis or body is damaged beyond repair, or if a serious traffic accident leaves the vehicle unfit for use, as determined by the licensing authority.Other grounds for cancellation include a court order or a decision to sell the vehicle at public auction under the applicable procedures.Authorities may refuse renewal when a vehicle fails to meet registration conditions, does not comply with safety requirements or is found to be unroadworthy during an approved technical inspection.Registration fee exemption for people with disabilitiesArticle 104 provides an exemption from the prescribed registration fees for one vehicle owned by a person with a disability.The exemption applies to one vehicle and is separate from the conditions governing the two-year registration option.Minimum driving ages and licence validityThe regulations also establish minimum ages for different vehicle categories under Article 54.Motorists must be at least 18 to obtain a light vehicle driving licence and 20 to qualify for a heavy vehicle licence.The minimum age for a Category 1 motorcycle licence is 17, rising to 21 for Category 2 motorcycles.Applicants for light and heavy bus licences must be at least 21, while those seeking licences to operate light or heavy mechanical equipment must be at least 20.Article 55 also specifies how long driving licences remain valid.Licences issued to applicants under 21 are temporary and generally valid for one year, renewable for the same period. Drivers aged 21 and above who obtain their first licence will receive one valid for two years.Upon subsequent renewal, UAE and Gulf Cooperation Council nationals qualify for licences valid for 10 years, while expatriate residents receive five-year licences, with both categories eligible for renewal for equivalent periods.The new executive regulations will come into force on January 1, 2027, introducing revised standards for vehicle registration, roadworthiness and driving licences across the UAE. .New UAE driving licence rules 2027: Who gets one, two, five or ten years’ validity?.UAE sets five-vehicle registration limit for individual residents under 2027 traffic rules.UAE to limit driving to nine hours in 24-hour period under new traffic rules.UAE new traffic law 2027: Ignored car recalls could restrict transactions

During an interview on the Live Broadcast programme on Noor Dubai Radio, he explained that the new system will allow traffic signal timings to be changed more dynamically than they are currently, so that they are controlled according to vehicle movement and traffic conditions. He pointed out that these systems are expected to contribute to reducing traffic congestion by no less than 10%, in addition to other projects that will also contribute to improving traffic flow in the emirate. He added that the RTA aims, within two and a half years, to radically introduce AI to support its 41 areas of work, explaining that the implementation is distributed over six phases. source_snapshot.title: New UAE sick leave certificate rule: What has changed and who benefits
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Getting a sick leave certificate attested in the UAE is about to get a lot less tiring for patients in many emirates.The Ministry of Health and Prevention (MoHAP) on Wednesday announced an enhanced system to streamline sick leave attestation and approval process in healthcare facilities under the ministry in multiple emirates.Here is an explainer on what has changed and who benefits.What is the new ruleUnder the enhanced system, hospitals and healthcare facilities, not patients, will now submit attestation applications directly to the ministry.Until now, the process started with the individual. Under the new arrangement, the facility that issued the sick leave sends the attestation request on behalf of the patient or the patient’s companion.Requests that meet the required conditions move automatically on to the approval service, with no need to file a fresh application.What has changedThe key shift is where the process begins. MoHAP says the service journey now starts with the issuing healthcare facility rather than the individual, which reduces the effort required from customers.This follows approved procedures and controls.The changes cover two services: the Attestation of Sick Leaves and Medical Reports Service, and the Approval of Sick Leaves and the Leave of the Patient’s Companion Service.The two are now linked, so a request that qualifies passes from attestation to approval automatically.Who benefitsPatients seeking sick leave certificate attestation from facilities under MoHAP in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah will benefit.The automatic link between attestation and approval applies to employees of the Federal Government and the local governments of Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah, in line with approved controls. For them, the second application is gone.Patient companions are covered too. Healthcare facilities can now submit attestation requests for companion leave alongside the patient’s own sick leave.MoHAP says this addresses the needs of companions and makes it easier to complete sick leave procedures.Why the changeThe ministry links the move to the UAE Government’s Zero Bureaucracy objectives. It says the enhancements simplify the customer journey, reduce procedures and speed up service completion, supporting the government’s leadership and global competitiveness in delivering easier, faster and more efficient services.Abdullah Ahli, Acting Assistant Undersecretary for the Support Services Sector at MoHAP, said the changes reflect the ministry’s commitment to turning the government’s vision into a fundamental transformation of service delivery. He said the focus is on redesigning procedures, simplifying the customer journey and strengthening integration between entities.Ahli added that the ministry wants a more flexible and sustainable service model, where transactions are completed through interconnected processes and data is exchanged effectively between entities. He stressed that Zero Bureaucracy is measured by real improvements in customer experience and government efficiency and said the ministry will keep working to improve service quality..UAE announces new sick leave attestation rule, makes approval process easier.Do you need a sick leave certificate in the UAE? source_snapshot.title: UAE sets 15 criteria for practical driving test, 75% minimum pass mark
source_snapshot.text: The new Executive Regulations of the Federal Traffic Law have approved a mechanism for assessing applicants for a driving licence in the UAE. The regulations specify 15 key criteria for evaluating practical driving skills, either through on-road testing or smart technical systems approved by the licensing authority. Anyone who scores less than 75% is considered to have failed the test and will be assigned a later date to retake it. The regulations state that applicants who successfully pass the theoretical examination will undergo a practical driving test conducted and supervised by the licensing authority or an accredited driving education facility. The 15 assessment criteria are designed to cover all key driving skills, including vehicle control, parking, manoeuvring on slopes and in emergency situations, maintaining safe distances, the correct use of mirrors and indicators, and proper interaction at roundabouts, intersections and in response to examiner instructions. These criteria include: Starting the engine. Driving the vehicle forwards and backwards in normal and emergency situations and on slopes. Using the transmission correctly when starting and while driving. Performing normal and emergency stops, including on slopes. Parking along a kerb, between vehicles, on slopes, and within designated signs or lines. Changing from one lane to another and turning right and left. Using the required signals at the appropriate time when changing direction or traffic position. Complying with traffic rules, signs and road markings, and responding appropriately to signals from other drivers and instructions from the examiner. Crossing intersections, squares and roundabouts. Turning the vehicle within a limited road space. Overtaking another vehicle and passing oncoming vehicles safely. Leaving and parking the vehicle on elevated areas. Using the parking brake correctly. Using side and rear-view mirrors correctly. Maintaining a sufficient safety distance from the vehicle ahead. The licensing authority may adopt any additional assessment criteria it considers necessary. Failure criteria The Executive Regulations stipulate that the licensing authority will allocate specific marks to each test criterion in line with the applicant's level of competence. Any applicant who fails to achieve at least 75% of the total score will be considered to have failed the test. An applicant may also fail even after achieving the required pass mark if they create an actual or potential danger to themselves or others during the test, or if the risk is avoided only because of the examiner's verbal or physical intervention. The regulations also identify the following actions as potential hazards: The vehicle's body or wheels coming into contact with designated boundaries or barriers. The vehicle moving unintentionally when starting due to lack of control. Errors when changing gears. Failure to park the vehicle in the designated location. Violating traffic signs and road markings. A motorised bicycle licence applicant touching the ground with their foot while riding. Theoretical testing The regulations state that the theoretical examination on traffic rules and road ethics will be conducted using methods approved by the licensing authority, which is responsible for supervising the tests and allocating marks out of a total score of 100. Any applicant who scores less than 75% of the total marks will be considered to have failed the theoretical test.

source_snapshot.text: Dubai: If one trip to Global Village is never enough for you, there is a weekend offer at the popular family destination – a limited number of visitors who buy entry tickets on November 6 will be able to enjoy free entry on November 7! Here’s how you can take advantage of the offer. How to get free entry to Global Village According to Global Village, those who visit the venue on November 6 (Friday) simply need to hold on to their ticket for the next day. On November 7 (Saturday), they would then need to present their ticket from the previous day at the Information Booth at the Gate of the World, to claim their complimentary ticket. It is important to note that the complimentary ticket is available for November 7 only, with only 3,100 complimentary tickets available, on a first-come, first-served basis.

deliveries on motorcycles licensed for delivery services.Approved vehicle systems: Drivers must log into the system installed in their vehicles and approved by the relevant authority when operating them, and use it in accordance with the applicable instructions.Uniform requirements: Delivery drivers must wear the prescribed uniform and maintain a presentable appearance.Professional permits: Drivers must carry their professional driving permits and present them to the relevant authorities upon request.Prohibited materials: Drivers must not transport or deliver prohibited or banned materials or items that violate public order.Valid permits: Drivers must not carry out professional activities without a valid professional permit or under an expired permit.Additional requirements: Drivers must comply with any other conditions imposed by the licensing authority or traffic enforcement authority, as applicable.Rules for motorcycle ridersThe regulations also prohibit motorcycle riders from operating their vehicles without holding the handlebars or while holding them with only one hand, except when giving a hand signal.Riders are not permitted to weave along roads, travel at dangerous speeds or operate their motorcycles in any other manner that could endanger the public.Motorcycle riders must wear protective helmets and travel in single file, one behind another, unless source_snapshot.title: UAE links health records to driving licences in new traffic law, to keep unfit drivers off the road
source_snapshot.text: Abu Dhabi: The new executive regulations of the Federal Traffic Law , which will come into effect on January 1, have approved legal controls and provisions that grant the licensing authority in the country the right to suspend, cancel, or refuse to renew driving licenses and permits in 12 cases, with the aim of raising the levels of safety and security on the roads. The regulations also introduced a clause obligating the competent health authorities in the country to coordinate with the licensing authority to provide it with data on people who suffer from diseases or health conditions that may affect their ability to drive vehicles safely. Specifically, the regulations classified the procedures related to driving licenses and permits into three main categories, including suspending their use, canceling them, and refusing to renew them, based on the driver’s record, health condition, and court rulings issued against him. The first category includes suspending the license in three cases: a court ruling to suspend it, reaching the cumulative limit of black points, or proving that the driver has lost the eligibility or health fitness necessary to drive. The second category relates to the cancellation of the licence, and includes five cases: the issuance of a court ruling to cancel, reaching the cumulative limit of traffic points, the applicant submitting a request to cancel it, the death of the licence holder, or proof of his loss of eligibility or the necessary health fitness to drive. The third category includes refusal to renew the licence in four cases: proof of loss of eligibility or health/fitness necessary for driving, issuance of a court ruling refusing renewal, the existence of unsettled traffic violations recorded on the driver’s traffic code, or reaching the cumulative limit of traffic points. In a related context, the regulation introduced a clause obligating the competent health authorities in the country to coordinate with the licensing authority to provide it with data on people who suffer from diseases or health conditions that may affect their ability to drive vehicles safely. Driver training Article (76) of the regulations, regarding the reassessment and qualification of drivers, stipulates that the holder of an expired driving license, when he wishes to renew it after more than 10 years have passed since its expiry without renewal, shall be subject to the theoretical and practical tests determined by the licensing authority, while fulfilling the other renewal conditions stipulated in the decision. The regulation granted the Federal Traffic Council the authority to determine the minimum theoretical and practical tests required to implement the provisions of this article. Licence renewal Article (73) stipulates that a request to renew a driver’s license must be submitted within 30 days of its expiry date, provided that the renewal is done after payment of the prescribed fees, and in accordance with the procedures approved by the licensing authority. Before renewing a driver's license, the individual is required to pay the fines resulting from violations committed, or to provide proof of payment of the fines imposed on him, if any, for violating the provisions of the decree-law, the regulations, and the decisions issued in implementation thereof. Eye exam Article (62) of the new executive regulations of the Federal Traffic Law approved the medical requirements for eye examinations for different driving categories, and set graduated standards starting with a minimum visual acuity of (6/18) for each eye separately for light vehicle drivers, taking into account cases of visual variance or loss of one eye, in which it is required that the visual acuity of the healthy eye not be less than (6/6). The regulations require drivers of buses and heavy and light equipment to have visual acuity of no less than (6/6) in both eyes. To make things easier for customers, the regulations granted the licensing authority the power to accept eye examination reports issued from outside the country, to enable holders of expired driving licenses to renew them.

source_snapshot.title: RTA boosts marine transport network with four new fourth-generation traditional abras
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 6th November, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) has expanded its marine transport network with the addition of four new fourth-generation traditional abras to its fleet, developed to the latest approved technical specifications and designs for this model.Through this step, RTA reaffirms its ongoing commitment to advancing public transport services, enriching customer experience and enhancing integration across the emirate’s transport modes.Khalaf Belghuzooz Al Zarooni, Director of Marine Transport at RTA’s Public Transport Agency, said that the addition forms part of RTA’s efforts to advance marine transport as a key component of Dubai’s sustainable mobility network. Such efforts reinforce the emirate’s position as a leading global city for quality of life, tourism and business, while enhancing its ability to offer residents and visitors diverse, safe and comfortable mobility options.Al Zarooni said, “The introduction of the new abras builds on RTA’s ongoing efforts to develop marine transport services and improve their operational efficiency, offering an integrated, more comfortable, and safer passengers travel experience. This aligns with RTA’s strategy to deliver innovative and sustainable mobility solutions that keep pace with Dubai’s rapid growth.”He added, “Each new abra accommodates 24 passengers and has been designed to the highest approved engineering and technical standards, in full compliance with the health and safety requirements of the Dubai Universal Design Code. This ensures a safe and comfortable travel environment that caters to the needs of all segments of society.”This significant addition will enhance the appeal of marine transport and drive greater use, reinforcing its vital role in Dubai’s public transport network. The new abras were designed to the highest standards of security, safety and environmental sustainability, and have secured certificates of conformity with applicable regulations and safety requirements under the relevant Gulf Standard Specifications.RTA has also rolled out a comprehensive package of operational and service improvements that elevate the service provided to passengers, including upgraded seating and flooring designs, more efficient use of interior space, and suitably designated areas for People of Determination to facilitate movement and use while achieving the highest levels of inclusivity and accessibility.The new abras have been equipped with smart systems and modern technologies that enhance the journey experience and raise service quality. These include digital screens displaying real-time information and safety and awareness content, alongside electronic destination boards, a first for the fourth-generation model. The systems enable passengers to access operational information clearly and easily, while boosting operating efficiency and customer satisfaction.Upgrading the marine transport fleet forms part of RTA’s vision to deliver an integrated and sustainable transport network that supports Dubai’s future smart mobility objectives, enhances service quality for residents and visitors, and reinforces the emirate’s position as a leading global model for modern, integrated transport systems.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Municipality opens registration for fifth Souk Al Freej season with 50 free stalls
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Dubai Municipality has opened registration for the fifth season of Souk Al Freej, its annual community initiative supporting entrepreneurs, small business owners and productive families, with 50 free stalls available to showcase and market local products. The fifth season will take place across three public parks during Dubai’s winter season, beginning at Nad Al Sheba Rose Garden from 11th to 20th December 2026. It will then move to Al Barsha Pond Park from 25th December 2026 to 3rd January 2027, before concluding at Al Warqa Park from 8th to 17th January 2027. The market will welcome visitors daily from 16:30 to 22:00. Of the 50 free stalls, 10 will be dedicated to supporting activities, including food and beverage kiosks. Participating entrepreneurs and productive families will showcase locally made products including homemade food, handicrafts, fashion and sustainable products. Dubai Municipality said Souk Al Freej forms part of its efforts to activate public parks and expand their role as community destinations offering shopping, entertainment and cultural experiences alongside traditional recreational activities. The initiative provides Emirati entrepreneurs and productive families with opportunities to introduce their products to wider audiences, develop their businesses, test products and build direct relationships with customers. The fifth season will introduce new cultural and entertainment experiences, including the "Asian Village Experience”, featuring Asian-inspired designs, food and cultural activities. It will also feature a dedicated Gen Z zone, free-play areas for children and creative and interactive workshops for different age groups. Other attractions will include a zipline and an interactive treasure hunt designed to encourage visitors to explore the market and engage with participating entrepreneurs through challenges and competitions. Mohammed Abdulrahman Ahli, Director of the Public Parks and Recreational Facilities Department at Dubai Municipality, said Souk Al Freej continues to strengthen its position as a community platform and comprehensive destination offering experiences beyond traditional shopping. He said the initiative provides entrepreneurs, small businesses and productive families with organised spaces to showcase their products, communicate directly with the public and expand their customer base. Ahli added that Dubai Municipality continues to develop the market each season with programmes and experiences catering to families, children and young people, combining shopping, entertainment and cultural activities while enhancing the vibrancy of public spaces and quality of life in Dubai. Dubai Municipality invited local entrepreneurs, small business owners and productive families to register for the fifth season and take advantage of the opportunity to showcase their products to a broad audience.

source_snapshot.title: UAE child car safety rules for 2027: When can your child sit in the front seat?
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Can your child sit in the front passenger seat, or do they need to travel in the back? Under the UAE's new traffic regulations, which come into effect on January 1, 2027, there are specific rules on where children can sit in a vehicle, when child safety seats are mandatory and the circumstances in which exceptions are allowed. Here is what parents need to know about keeping their children safe while travelling by car. Child safety in vehicles As per Article 11 (1) of Cabinet Resolution No. 174 of 2026, children up to four years old should be provided child safety seats. The seats should be suitable for their age and weight, as per the approved UAE safety standards, and must be placed in the rear seats. However, the Resolution lists out certain cases that are exempt from this requirement: A child with a medical condition that prevents them for using child seats. This requires a medical certificate issued by the relevant medica authority, and the child should be accompanied by an adult in the back seat. Vehicles without rear seats. In such cases, the child seat can be fitted in the front seat, provided that it is facing backwards and the airbag deactivated. When can children sit in the passenger seat? As a general rule, children should be seated in the rear seats, with seatbelts or child safety seats. However, if a child is 10 years old, or older, or at least 145 centimetres tall, he or she may be allowed to sit in the front passenger seat. The Resolution, which was issued last month, comes into effect from January 1, 2026, and lays down regulations for traffic management and road use.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Police launch traffic safety awareness competition
source_snapshot.text: Dubai Police, represented by the General Department of Traffic and the Esaad Card Centre, announced the launch of an awareness competition through the Traffic Safety Platform. The initiative aims to educate the public about the leading causes of accidents and raise awareness of safe road behaviours, helping to strengthen shared responsibility among road users to protect lives and property. The competition forms part of Dubai Police's ongoing efforts to expand community participation in traffic awareness, encourage the public to improve their knowledge of traffic rules, and turn that knowledge into daily practices that help prevent accidents. The competition will run for five weeks and features 10 questions on the leading causes of traffic accidents, including failing to leave a sufficient safe distance between vehicles, speeding, and unsafe roadside stopping. The topics are based on traffic studies. At the end of the competition, an electronic draw will be held to select five winners. Each winner will receive an Esaad card and enjoy the privileges and discounts it offers across 10 sectors. Brigadier Salah Mohammad Al Marzouqi, Director of the Esaad Card Centre at the General Department of Logistics Support, affirmed that the centre's participation reflects its commitment to community responsibility and supporting initiatives that enhance safety and quality of life. He explained that Esaad uses its partnerships and benefits to encourage participation in meaningful initiatives, strengthen collaboration with partners, and contribute to achieving shared goals in serving the community and promoting positive behaviour. Colonel Talal Abdullah Al Mansouri, Director of the Traffic Education Department at the General Department of Traffic, said that preventing accidents begins with road users recognising dangerous behaviours and adhering to rules that protect everyone. He added that the competition gives participants an opportunity to test their knowledge and correct traffic misconceptions through an interactive format. This helps them better understand road safety messages, apply them while driving, and become active partners in improving road safety. The public can participate by registering on the Traffic Safety Platform at https://amanroads.gov.ae/trsp/en. The platform provides awareness messages through videos and text content, offering tips and guidance to all segments of the community. It aims to enhance understanding of traffic safety measures, driving rules, compliance with traffic regulations, and pedestrian laws. Users can also view awareness campaigns and take part in competitions. Those wishing to participate in the awareness competition can answer the 10 questions to qualify for the final electronic draw and have a chance to win an Esaad card.

source_snapshot.title: UAE job experience certificate 2026: What it must say, who must give it and how MOHRE can help
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: If you’ve been terminated from your job, or are leaving for better opportunities elsewhere, there’s a document you shouldn’t walk out without acquiring – a job experience certificate. This vital document gives your next employer insight into your employment history, while mentioning details that may be useful, when you need to show government entities proof of previous employment for immigration, visa or legal purposes – details like your duration of work, job title and salary information. Here’s everything you need to know about experience certificates, and how to acquire them. Can the employer refuse to give me an experience certificate? It is illegal for an employer to withhold the experience certificate, according to Musa Dayani, a Dubai-based public relations officer. In the UAE, Article 13(11) of the UAE Labour Law requires employers to provide an experience certificate upon the expiration or termination of a contract – even if you were fired . The certificate is typically stamped by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE), and must be provided to you free of cost by your current employer. The law also offers protection to employees by clearly stating that the certificate must not contain any information that could damage their reputation or limit their chances of acquiring another job. What information should the certificate have? According to Article 13(11) of the UAE Labour Law, the following information must be mentioned in the experience certificate: The date the employment began. The date the employment ended. The total period or duration of service. The job title or the kind of work the employee was performing. The last wage received. The reason for the termination of the employment contract. Does MOHRE also provide an experience certificate? Another way to acquire your experience certificate is via MOHRE. The entity has simplified the process of acquiring an employment history certificate online, through its website and app. Follow these steps: Visit MOHRE’s website – mohre.gov.ae – or download the MOHRE app on the Apple App Store or Google Play Store. Log in with your UAE PASS. Click on ‘View All Services’. In the search bar, search for ‘Employment History Certificate’. Select ‘Start Service’. You will immediately receive a stamped and approved certificate by MOHRE, which can be downloaded right from the website or app. The certificate is valid for 30 days, and employers will be able to verify its authenticity through the ‘Employee Certificate Verification’ service on the MOHRE website.

source_snapshot.title: How to get a Golden Visa as an international graduate: Eligibility, nomination and what happens after 10 years
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Even if you have studied overseas, and don’t have a UAE-based degree, you may be able to apply for a Golden Visa, as an international student. The visa is available to graduates from some of the world’s most prestigious universities, as long as they meet specific requirements set out by the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP). These requirements relate to the university’s global ranking, the student’s academic performance, and when they graduated. Here’s everything you need to know about Golden Visa rules for international graduates. Which international graduates are eligible for a Golden Visa? Not everyone who has studied or graduated from a university abroad qualifies for a Golden Visa in the UAE. You can check if you are eligible through the ICP’s ‘Check Your Eligibility’ tool , to see if you qualify. The ICP also outlines the following eligibility criteria for graduates of international universities: The university from which the applicant graduated must be ranked among the top 100 universities in the world, according to the international ranking recognised by the Ministry of Education. The applicant must have achieved a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5, or its equivalent, for their bachelor’s degree. No more than two years must have elapsed since the applicant’s graduation date at the time of application. The academic qualification must be attested by the Ministry of Education. How can students or graduates check if their university is on the approved list? It’s important not to assume your university is among the global top 100 listed by the authorities – there’s a quick way to find out. Applicants can check if their university is among approved institutions, on the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ website. Visit www.mofa.gov.ae/en/top-universities. You can also check this information via the Abu Dhabi Residents Office (ADRO), at adro.gov.ae/-/media/Project/Expat-Bureau/International-Universities.pdf. How can students or graduates apply for the Golden Visa? Before applying for a Golden Visa, the applicant must first submit a Golden Visa nomination request. This can be done through the General Directorate of Residency or Foreigners Affairs (GDRFA) if you are based in Dubai, or via the ICP if you are in other emirates. Follow the nomination steps here. A nomination means that the government body has checked your credentials and has decided you are eligible for the category. Only once your nomination is approved can you proceed with other steps and complete your Golden Visa application. Learn how to apply for a Golden Visa here. What do international graduates need to know about the UAE Golden Visa? The Golden Visa provides eligible top-performing students and graduates a 10-year visa without the need for a local sponsor. Under the Golden Visa, university graduates are permitted to sponsor family members, including their spouse and children, upon proof of an employment contract, a steady monthly income and housing, in accordance with the regulations that govern family sponsorship . However, according to the ICP, unlike most other Golden Visa categories, the residency permit for students cannot be renewed after expiration. If the student or graduate wishes to remain in the UAE after their Golden Visa expires, they must apply for a new residency status under a different eligible category, such as an employment visa, investor visa, freelance work visa, Golden Visa – Content Creator category and so on, depending on their specific profession or situation. Learn about all the benefits of a UAE Golden Visa here .

source_snapshot.title: RTA opens 1,650-metre Al Khaleej Street Tunnel
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 8th November, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) opened Al Khaleej Street Tunnel today. The 1,650-metre tunnel extends from the end of the Infinity Bridge ramp in Deira to the intersection of Al Khaleej Street and Al Wuheida Street. It features three lanes in each direction, with a combined capacity of 12,000 vehicles per hour, as part of Al Shindagha Corridor Development Project.Mattar Al Tayer, Director-General and Chairman of the Board of Executive Directors of RTA, said the tunnel represents a significant addition to Deira’s road network, providing free-flowing traffic for motorists travelling from Infinity Bridge towards Deira and Al Mamzar and vice versa. It will also strengthen connectivity between residential areas, commercial centres and tourist destinations, while keeping pace with the emirate’s urban development.Al Tayer explained that Al Khaleej Street Tunnel is an integral component of Al Shindagha Corridor Development Project, which extends 13 km and is estimated to serve approximately one million people across major developments, including Dubai Islands, Dubai Maritime City and Port Rashid. He noted that completing the corridor improvements will reduce journey time from 1 hour 44 minutes to 16 minutes by 2030.The project has achieved a significant milestone, recording nearly 11 million work hours with no injuries reported. A total of 2,200 engineers, technicians and workers have contributed to the project, supported by 350 pieces of equipment and machinery. In addition, 77 percent of the materials excavated during tunnel construction, estimated at approximately 522,000 cubic metres, have been reused in other projects. The works also include developing signal-controlled intersections on Cairo Street and Al Wuheida Street.Under the Dubai Tunnels initiative, Al Khaleej Street Tunnel has been transformed into an artistic mural reflecting Dubai’s urban character. Designed by Emirati artist Maryam Al Hathboor, the artwork depicts Dubai’s skyline in a style inspired by banknote illustrations, using 35 million mosaic pieces.RTA completed Al Shindagha Corridor development works in Bur Dubai in 2025 and is currently constructing a 1,425-metre bridge connecting Dubai Islands with Bur Dubai. The bridge will have a combined capacity of 16,000 vehicles per hour, allow vessels to pass through Dubai Creek and feature a dedicated pedestrian and cycling track.
