source_snapshot.title: Dubai Municipality introduces first fully electric waste collection vehicle to enhance city cleaning operations
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 8th November, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Municipality has introduced its first fully electric vehicle dedicated to the collection and transport of general waste, marking a significant step in enhancing the efficiency of city cleaning operations and adopting innovative technologies across municipal services. The initiative reflects the Municipality's commitment to protecting the urban environment, advancing sustainability and enhancing quality of life across Dubai.The introduction of the vehicle supports Dubai Municipality's strategic objectives to advance integrated waste management, enhance the operational efficiency of public cleaning services and modernise its vehicle fleet. It also contributes to preserving Dubai's urban and aesthetic appearance while supporting climate neutrality targets, environmental sustainability and the adoption of clean energy and innovative technologies.The initiative also aligns with the Dubai Integrated Waste Management Strategy 2041, which aims to reduce waste generation by 18% and divert 100% of waste from landfills by 2041. These efforts support operational sustainability and reinforce Dubai's commitment to becoming a global model for smart and environmentally friendly cities.The vehicle operates entirely on electrical energy stored in three high-efficiency lithium-ion batteries with a combined weight of approximately 2.2 tonnes. It can travel between 100 and 150 kilometres on a single charge, meeting the daily operational requirements of waste collection and transport services across different areas of Dubai.To support the continuity of municipal services, the vehicle is equipped with fast-charging technology that allows its battery charge to increase from 20% to 80% in just one hour and 45 minutes using a 160 kW charger. This enhances operational readiness and supports the efficient delivery of daily cleaning services.The vehicle has a total waste storage capacity of 19 cubic metres and can carry up to 11 tonnes of compressed waste. It is compatible with different waste container sizes, including 1.1 cubic metres, 360 litres, 240 litres and 120 litres.The vehicle is also equipped with an advanced electric compactor that supports multiple waste collection and transport systems, including the collection and emptying of community waste containers and door-to-door waste collection services. It also incorporates source-based weighing systems that measure waste during container emptying.The vehicle features smart cameras designed to enhance occupational safety by enabling continuous monitoring of different operational stages, as well as the vehicle's movement and surrounding environment. These systems improve driver visibility and support safer driving and manoeuvring, helping to reduce risks to workers and other road users.Saeed Safar, Director of the Waste Operations Department at Dubai Municipality, said the introduction of the new electric vehicle represents a significant step in modernising the Municipality's fleet. He explained that its operation forms part of efforts to test the actual performance of heavy electric vehicles under local climatic conditions and assess their suitability for Dubai's operational requirements. The findings will help establish a scientific basis for potentially expanding their use across municipal operations in the future.Safar said: “Dubai Municipality is committed to developing an integrated and sustainable waste management ecosystem that supports the transition towards a circular economy, reduces reliance on conventional vehicles, improves energy efficiency and lowers emissions. The introduction of electric vehicles into waste collection and transport operations represents a practical step towards adopting clean and innovative technologies in daily operations, further strengthening Dubai's position as a leading global city in sustainability, innovation and quality of life.”Dubai Municipality has also trained a specialised operational team comprising a smart vehicle technician and cleaning engineers to support the vehicle's efficient operation and maintenance. The electric compactor is scheduled to operate across two shifts, totalling 16 hours per day.Dubai Municipality remains committed to strengthening Dubai's global leadership, attractiveness and sustainability by advancing smart city management operations. Through its role in planning, managing and ensuring the city's sustainability, the Municipality continues to deliver innovative municipal services that enhance residents' wellbeing, happiness and quality of life.

source_snapshot.title: UAE officially launches first innovative oral treatment for Vitiligo
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 8th November, 2026 (WAM) -- In the presence of Sheikha Dr. Noura Al Qasimi, Consultant Ophthalmologist and President of the Emirates Medical Association, and Dr. Ayman Alnaeem, President of the Dermatology Division, the Division officially celebrated yesterday, on the sidelines of the 10th Annual Dermatology Conference, the launch of the first innovative oral treatment for vitiligo, making the United Arab Emirates the first country in the world to approve the therapy. Vitiligo affects between 1% and 2% of the global population. Research indicates that the disease begins before the age of 20 in 50% of cases, while in one-third of all cases, more than one member of the same family is affected. The celebration was held last night at the InterContinental Dubai – Festival City, as the company secured a Guinness World Records title for the world’s largest interactive art installation featuring projection mapping — a three-dimensional structure onto which images, colors, and light animations are projected, with effects that change in response to visitor interaction. Vitiligo is a chronic skin condition associated with an autoimmune disorder that causes patches of skin to lose their natural color in different areas of the body, as the body mistakenly attacks and destroys its own pigment-producing cells. Genetics play a pivotal role, with the likelihood of developing the condition increasing significantly in the presence of a family history of the disorder. Scientific research confirms that the disease generally does not cause physical pain, but it is associated with a substantial psychological and social burden, in addition to its impact on self-confidence and daily quality of life. The UAE’s approval opens the door to a new treatment option for patients with non-segmental vitiligo, a step that reinforces the country’s position in adopting modern pharmaceutical therapies and accelerating patient access to medical innovations. The dosage and duration of treatment are determined by a specialist in immunological diseases, and the medication is available only on prescription. Speaking at the launch ceremony, Sheikha Dr. Noura Al Qasimi said the successive achievements and qualitative leaps made by the country’s health sector are a reflection of the vision of its wise leadership, which seeks to strengthen the UAE’s standing among advanced nations worldwide across all sectors, including healthcare, which receives the highest levels of attention and support. “Our leadership places community health at the top of national priorities and has embedded it within the state’s strategy, based on its vision that the health of the population and improving their quality of life represent the core of the UAE’s development plans, and that health is one of the key sectors prioritized to achieve comprehensive prosperity and well-being for society,” she said. Meanwhile, the 10th Dermatology Conference concluded yesterday after three days of discussions featuring a rich and diverse scientific programme, including advanced scientific lectures, hands-on workshops, live demonstrations, and interactive sessions discussing clinical cases, helping participants keep pace with the latest scientific developments and modern technologies in dermatology. Dr. Ayman Alnaeem, President of the Dermatology Division and President of the Conference, said the discussions highlighted the latest global developments in dermatology, laser, and aesthetic medicine, with the aim of improving quality of healthcare and equipping participating physicians with advanced skills and knowledge to apply in their daily practice, thereby promoting the highest standards of care for dermatology patients.The conference agenda covered a wide range of topics, including skin aging, eczema — one of the most common conditions — acne, skin cancer, infectious skin diseases, and inflammatory skin diseases. It also highlighted innovations in dermatology, including artificial intelligence applications, clinical imaging, and innovative therapeutic approaches. Dr. Alnaeem emphasised that the conference has become a landmark event in the region for strengthening collaboration among specialists, exchanging findings from leading scientific research, and providing a sustainable platform for continuing professional development.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai RTA to open 110-metre pedestrian bridge linking Metro station to Coca-Cola Arena
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) will open a 110-metre pedestrian bridge tomorrow, Tuesday. Developed by Meraas, a subsidiary of Dubai Holding Properties, the bridge connects Burj Khalifa/Dubai Mall Metro Station with Coca-Cola Arena in City Walk. The project enhances pedestrian infrastructure and safety while improving access for residents and visitors to key recreational destinations. It supports RTA’s vision of improving quality of life and providing safe and sustainable mobility for all. It also reflects Meraas’ commitment to creating interconnected destinations that encourage walking and strengthen people’s connection to their surroundings. The pedestrian bridge is part of traffic improvement projects implemented by RTA in cooperation with Dubai Holding. These projects aim to develop infrastructure and strengthen connectivity between key areas and tourist and entertainment destinations, particularly City Walk and Coca-Cola Arena. They are designed to improve mobility and traffic safety in line with Dubai’s urban and economic growth, while reinforcing the emirate’s position as a pedestrian- and bicycle-friendly city. The expansion of pedestrian bridges and tunnels supports the objectives of the Dubai Traffic Safety Strategy, which aims to achieve zero road fatalities and make Dubai one of the world’s leading cities for traffic safety. The provision of safe crossings separates pedestrians from vehicles, particularly in areas with high levels of road and pedestrian traffic and near public transport stations, shopping centres, tourist destinations and entertainment venues. The new bridge has a capacity of approximately 10,000 people per hour, equivalent to 59% of the crowd capacity for a single event. This improves pedestrian traffic management during major events, reduces the need to cross surface roads and limits interaction between pedestrians and vehicles. It also encourages the public to use the Dubai Metro to reach the area, reducing reliance on private vehicles and contributing to smoother traffic flow around Coca-Cola Arena and City Walk. The bridge is particularly important for visitors to Coca-Cola Arena, which hosts a range of live entertainment and sporting events throughout the year. It provides a safe, direct pedestrian route and helps crowds arrive at and leave the venue, particularly during peak periods when large numbers of visitors are travelling within a short period. RTA is continuing to implement its five-year plan for 2026–2030, which includes the construction of 31 pedestrian bridges and tunnels at key locations across Dubai. The locations are selected based on technical and field studies that consider population density, pedestrian traffic and proximity to public transport stations and tourist and economic attractions. The plan aims to enhance road-user safety and encourage sustainable mobility and first- and last-mile journeys. RTA’s development of pedestrian infrastructure has contributed to improvements in traffic safety. The number of pedestrian bridges and tunnels in Dubai increased from 26 in 2006 to 178 by the end of 2025, while the pedestrian death rate fell from 9.5 deaths per 100,000 people in 2007 to 0.22 in 2025, reflecting the Authority’s efforts to provide a safe and sustainable mobility environment.

source_snapshot.title: New UAE traffic regulations require tracking devices on all rental vehicles
source_snapshot.text: Abu Dhabi: The new executive regulations for the UAE Traffic Law, which will come into effect at the beginning of January, 2027, set out a series of conditions and obligations for vehicle rental activities in the country, including a requirement to install tracking devices on all vehicles designated for rental. Under Article 123, companies must obtain prior authorisation from the licensing authority before engaging in vehicle rental activities. The authorisation is valid for one calendar year and is renewable. To obtain authorisation, companies must meet several requirements, including holding a valid commercial licence, installing approved tracking devices on all vehicles designated for rental, and registering with and linking to the unified electronic platform approved by the Ministry and licensing authority. Companies must also meet any additional requirements imposed by the competent authorities or traffic control authority. Article 124 sets out five key obligations for licensed rental offices. These include verifying the validity of the renter’s driving licence, using a unified rental agreement for transactions and electronically registering the agreement with the licensing authority. Rental offices may only rent vehicles registered in their name and licensed for that purpose. The article also prohibits vehicles from being loaned between rental offices except under a notarised contract. Employees of the same office may use its vehicles, subject to approved regulations. Under Article 126, the relevant ministry will establish and design an electronic system to register rental office vehicles, record their data and information relating to vehicle rentals, and track the geographical scope of their movements. Article 127 prohibits the rental or leasing of private vehicles that are not licensed for rental purposes. It also prohibits the use of such vehicles to transport passengers or goods in return for any form of material compensation.

Under Article 123, companies must obtain prior authorisation from the licensing authority before engaging in vehicle rental activities.
The authorisation is valid for one calendar year and is renewable.

To obtain authorisation, companies must meet several requirements, including holding a valid commercial licence, installing approved tracking devices on all vehicles designated for rental, and registering with and linking to the unified electronic platform approved by the Ministry and licensing authority.
Companies must also meet any additional requirements imposed by the competent authorities or traffic control authority.
Article 124 sets out five key obligations for licensed rental offices.
These include verifying the validity of the renter’s driving licence, using a unified rental agreement for transactions and electronically registering the agreement with the licensing authority.
Rental offices may only rent vehicles registered in their name and licensed for that purpose.
The article also prohibits vehicles from being loaned between rental offices except under a notarised contract.
Employees of the same office may use its vehicles, subject to approved regulations.

Under Article 126, the relevant ministry will establish and design an electronic system to register rental office vehicles, record their data and information relating to vehicle rentals, and track the geographical scope of their movements.
Article 127 prohibits the rental or leasing of private vehicles that are not licensed for rental purposes.
It also prohibits the use of such vehicles to transport passengers or goods in return for any form of material compensation.

source_snapshot.title: Paid parking to be activated in Abu Dhabi's Musaffah sectors M10 and M17
source_snapshot.text: Abu Dhabi: Q Mobility, the company that manages and operates Abu Dhabi’s public parking and Darb road toll system, has announced that paid parking will be introduced in two more sectors of Musaffah from 16 November 2026. The move, covering sectors M10 and M17, will be implemented under the regulatory supervision of the Integrated Transport Centre (Abu Dhabi Mobility), an affiliate of the Department of Municipalities and Transport. It forms part of a gradual expansion of the paid parking system that began in January 2026. A total of 4,233 standard parking spaces will be activated in the fourth phase of the rollout, comprising 1,645 spaces in M10 and 2,588 in M17. Designated parking spaces for People of Determination will also be available. The expansion is intended to regulate the use of public parking and improve the management of available parking capacity, while reducing congestion and random parking, improving traffic flow and facilitating access to establishments in the area. Musaffah, one of Abu Dhabi’s major industrial and commercial areas, experiences heavy traffic throughout the day due to its range of economic and service activities and the large number of employees and visitors. The parking measures are also intended to support economic and commercial activity by creating a more organised environment and making it easier to move between different locations in the area. Standard parking spaces covered by the new phase will cost AED 2 per hour. Motorists can pay through the Darb and TAMM apps.

source_snapshot.title: Hamdan bin Mohammed chairs The Executive Council meeting, approves major public projects in Dubai worth over AED11 billion
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 10th November, 2026 (WAM) -- H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Defence, and Chairman of The Executive Council of Dubai, approved a plan to develop community services and facilities through 2040 with a budget of AED9.59 billion, and the extension of the Dubai Metro to Al Maktoum International Airport City with a budget of AED2 billion.During a meeting held as part of the UAE Annual Government Meetings 2026, The Executive Council also approved the findings of a study on the future of Dubai’s real estate market and the investment policy relating to endowments and minors’ funds.H.H. Sheikh Hamdan affirmed that, guided by the vision of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President, Prime Minister and Ruler of Dubai, Dubai continues to invest in future-ready infrastructure and integrated community services, turning the Dubai Plan 2033 that encompasses the Dubai Economic Agenda (D33) and the Dubai Social Agenda 33 into projects that keep pace with the emirate’s growth.H.H. Sheikh Hamdan said, “The stability and prosperity of our community remain our priority. We approved a comprehensive plan to develop integrated public services and facilities that foster social cohesion. Our goal is for the people of Dubai to experience the benefits of the city’s growth in their everyday lives.”On the Dubai Metro extension, H.H. Sheikh Hamdan said, “Al Maktoum International Airport City is one of our most significant strategic projects, reinforcing Dubai’s position as a global aviation hub. The extension is part of an integrated transport system that matches the ambitions of this global project. We continue to invest in infrastructure that anticipates future aspirations, connects the emirate and strengthens Dubai’s competitiveness.”On the real estate sector, H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum said, “Dubai’s real estate sector continues to demonstrate strong, resilient performance, bolstered by investor confidence and diverse range of investment opportunities. The findings of the new study will guide policy and development decisions made with the private sector, supporting the Dubai Real Estate Sector Strategy 2033 and further solidifying Dubai’s position as one of the world’s most competitive and sustainable real estate markets.”H.H. Sheikh Hamdan stressed the importance of strengthening the management and investment of endowment assets and minors’ funds at The Endowment and Minors’ Trust Foundation in Dubai (Awqaf Dubai), to safeguard assets, optimise investment returns and ensure sustainable benefits.H.H. Sheikh Hamdan said, “Dubai has established a pioneering model for endowment initiatives and the management of minors’ funds, with endowment assets reaching AED13.5 billion in 2025. We remain committed to advancing this model to safeguard and grow the assets while optimising their social impact. We have directed Awqaf Dubai to diversify the investment portfolio and strengthen private sector partnerships, securing sustainable returns for beneficiaries and the wider community.”The meeting was attended by H.H. Sheikh Maktoum bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, First Deputy Ruler of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance, and H.H. Sheikh Ahmed bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Second Deputy Ruler of Dubai.The community services plan aims to ensure the efficient and equitable distribution of public services and facilities across existing and planned residential communities, meeting the needs of Dubai’s citizens and residents as the city continues to develop.The plan will be implemented under the supervision of the Supreme Committee for Urban Planning in Dubai, in coordination with Dubai Municipality, in line with the Dubai Social Agenda 33 and the Dubai 2040 Urban Master Plan. It will be rolled out in phases, prioritising residential areas for citizens.It includes essential facilities for safety, security, healthcare, education and sports, alongside amenities for senior Emiratis and spaces for family and community activities, improving access to services, meeting the needs of all generations and strengthening family bonds and social cohesion.The Dubai Metro extension will give rise to a 3-kilometre route with two new stations, linking Route 2020 to Al Maktoum International Airport City.The project involves a collaboration between Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) and the Dubai Engineering Projects Establishment. Services are scheduled to begin in 2031.The extended route will connect to the West Terminal of Al Maktoum International Airport, linking with the airport express line and Etihad Rail’s high-speed rail network.It will make travel easier for passengers, airport staff and visitors; improve traffic flow on surrounding roads, and ease access to urban centres across the emirate.The study on the future of Dubai’s real estate market was conducted by the Dubai Land Department. It supports the Dubai Real Estate Sector Strategy 2033, which aims to double the sector’s contribution to Dubai’s GDP to AED73 billion, increase the volume of real estate transactions by 70% to bring the market’s total value to AED1 trillion, and double the value of real estate portfolios to AED20 billion.The study shows that residential occupancy stands at 97%, with retail occupancy at 98% and office occupancy currently at 94%, respectively.It projects the development of 365,000 new residential units and approximately 1.1 million square metres of office and retail space by 2030, providing developers insights to guide investment and development planning, enhance projects quality, accelerate delivery, and strengthen investor confidence.The study also reflects Dubai’s data-driven approach to real estate market planning, using market indicators to inform policies, respond to evolving demand and maintain a balance between supply and demand.This is supported by an adaptive regulatory framework, integrated digital services, and strong partnerships with developers and investors.The investment policy presented by Awqaf Dubai aligns with the economic and social priorities of Dubai Plan 2033, with a focus on safeguarding and growing assets to ensure sustainable benefits for beneficiaries and future generations.By 2030, the policy targets an increase of AED10 billion in the value of the real estate portfolio and over 35% growth in the securities portfolio.The policy sets out a diversified investment approach aimed at optimising returns while managing risks and strengthening private sector participation, in accordance with Sharia principles.Real estate investments will span residential, commercial, healthcare, industrial and educational developments, as well as exhibition and sports facilities, in alignment with the Dubai 2040 Urban Master Plan.

Одобрен проект продления метро до города аэропорта Аль-Мактум с бюджетом AED2 млрд.

Исследование рынка недвижимости поддержит стратегию развития сектора до 2033 года.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai tenants can now split rent payments into smaller instalments under new scheme
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Tenants living in some of Dubai’s largest residential communities will have a new way to manage their rent payments, with a scheme allowing eligible residents to split rental instalments into smaller amounts instead of paying a large sum upfront.Dubai Residential, part of Dubai Holding Asset Management, announced on Tuesday a partnership with UAE-based fintech platform Rentify to introduce the payment option across its 22 communities, which are home to more than 146,000 residents.The arrangement will be available to eligible new tenants and existing residents renewing their leases, offering an alternative to the conventional rental payment structure.For tenants who currently pay their annual rent in four equal instalments, the service will allow them to divide their first instalment into smaller payments. New tenants can also access the option when signing their rental contracts..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..What does this mean for Dubai tenants?For households managing monthly expenses, rental payments can represent a significant financial commitment, particularly when several months of rent fall due at once.The new arrangement gives eligible tenants another way to spread those payments rather than meeting the full instalment amount on its original due date.For example, a tenant paying Dh80,000 annually in four equal instalments would ordinarily need to pay Dh20,000 at each scheduled payment date. Under the new arrangement, an eligible tenant could divide the first Dh20,000 instalment into smaller payments, subject to Rentify's terms.Dubai Residential has not specified how many smaller payments tenants can make, the repayment period or the exact charges involved.The service will be accessible using credit cards issued by select banks, with rates and eligibility conditions applying. The company has not disclosed the participating banks or a detailed fee structure.The option will complement Dubai Residential's existing payment methods rather than replace them.Which Dubai communities are covered?The partnership extends across Dubai Residential's portfolio of 22 communities, which includes premium developments, family-oriented neighbourhoods and more affordable housing options.Its residential portfolio includes Bluewaters, City Walk, Nad Al Sheba Villas, The Gardens, Garden View Villas, Remraam, Layan, Ghoroob and Shorooq.While the payment option will be offered across the portfolio, access will depend on individual eligibility requirements.The companies have not specified whether every tenant will qualify or whether different payment terms will apply across communities..Dubai tenants can now register, renew, cancel Ejari, and pay DEWA on DubaiNow app .More flexibility in rental paymentsAhmed Al Suwaidi, Managing Director of Dubai Residential, said the partnership was intended to make renting simpler and give residents more control over their payment arrangements."Partnering with Rentify reflects our commitment to making the rental journey simpler, more flexible and increasingly digital, while responding to the evolving needs of our residents," Al Suwaidi said.The initiative also forms part of Dubai Residential's efforts to move more rental services online.Through its existing mobile application, residents can already renew contracts, make payments, request maintenance, arrange move-in and move-out services and manage their personal information.Rashed Hareb Al Mheiri, Co-Founder and CEO of Rentify, said tenants were increasingly seeking alternatives to traditional rental payment arrangements."Expectations around renting are changing, with residents increasingly looking for greater choice and flexibility in how they manage their payments," he said.What tenants must check before signing upAlthough the scheme offers another way to manage rental payments, tenants will need to consider the applicable charges and repayment conditions before deciding whether it suits their finances.The announcement refers to competitive rates but does not provide specific costs or explain whether charges will vary depending on the credit card used.It also does not specify when the service will become available to individual tenants or detail the application process.The companies said the arrangement would give eligible residents greater choice in managing rental payments while expanding the digital services available across Dubai Residential's communities.For tenants, the immediate benefit is the possibility of breaking down a large rental instalment into smaller payments. The actual cost and repayment schedule will depend on the terms offered through Rentify..Make Gulf News your preferred news source on Google and stay ahead of the curve

source_snapshot.title: Dubai launches five-day permit process for mosque construction
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 10th November, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Municipality and the Islamic Affairs and Charitable Activities Department in Dubai (IACAD) have launched a joint initiative to streamline mosque construction procedures, introducing a fast-track process that enables construction permits to be issued within a maximum of five days. The initiative also simplifies construction requirements to accommodate the essential and operational needs of mosques and their associated facilities, supporting more efficient use of buildings and spaces.The initiative strengthens integration between government entities to develop services and simplify the customer journey. It reflects Dubai Municipality’s efforts to improve construction permitting procedures, enhance the efficiency of the construction sector and deliver more accessible, high-quality services in line with government best practices and Dubai’s future urban growth requirements.The collaboration covers several stages of mosque construction and development, including modifications, extensions and maintenance. Under the initiative, maintenance works that do not involve specialised structural modifications will be exempt from construction permit requirements through the self-maintenance service, subject to applicable regulations. This will reduce procedural requirements and facilitate the maintenance of existing mosques.To accelerate project delivery, Dubai Municipality will also coordinate with IACAD to review mosque designs and assess technical requirements at an early stage, reducing the time required to complete permitting and approval procedures.The initiative further includes assessing land availability in areas experiencing high numbers of worshippers, enabling IACAD to respond to community needs and expand mosque capacity. Dubai Municipality will also provide landscaping support within mosque premises, ensuring that these improvements complement the surrounding roads and public spaces and contribute to a unified identity for service facilities across the emirate.Eng. Marwan Ahmed bin Ghalita, Director-General of Dubai Municipality, said, “Our collaboration with the Islamic Affairs and Charitable Activities Department reflects Dubai’s approach to government integration, bringing together the capabilities and expertise of different entities to simplify procedures and deliver more efficient services. Through this initiative, we are establishing a clearer and more streamlined process for mosque construction permits, reducing the time and effort required to complete approvals while ensuring that technical requirements respond to the essential and operational needs of mosques.”He added, “This cooperation also supports our wider efforts to improve the efficiency of Dubai’s construction sector and enhance the customer journey. By simplifying regulatory procedures and expanding digital services through the unified Dubai Building Platform, we aim to accelerate project delivery and enhance service quality. These efforts will help provide integrated infrastructure for religious facilities that keeps pace with the emirate’s future urban growth, meets the needs of Dubai’s residents and communities, and enhances quality of life.”Ahmed Darwish Al Muhairi, Director-General of the Islamic Affairs and Charitable Activities Department in Dubai, said, “Government integration is essential to translating the vision and directives of our leadership into services that respond effectively to community needs. At the Islamic Affairs and Charitable Activities Department, we place service accessibility and customer satisfaction at the centre of our development efforts, working closely with other government entities to align priorities, coordinate procedures and integrate efforts to improve operational efficiency and meet and exceed community expectations.”He added, “Our collaboration with Dubai Municipality reflects this approach by linking the planning, construction and maintenance of mosques to the emirate’s urban growth and the needs of residential communities, while simplifying and accelerating procedures across planning, permitting, construction, development and maintenance. Through this integration, we seek to accelerate project delivery, improve the quality of services provided by mosques and their associated facilities, and enhance their readiness to serve worshippers, advancing our vision of being closer to the community.”

source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 10th November, 2026 (WAM) -- Nakheel, a member of Dubai Holding Real Estate, has unveiled Palm Springs, a 3.8 million sqm residential masterplan adjacent to Palm Jebel Ali in southern Dubai. He emphasised the importance of bringing homes and supporting infrastructure together from the outset to accommodate Dubai's future growth and create lasting value, supported by connections to Sheikh Zayed Road and proximity to economic expansion around Al Maktoum International Airport and Expo City Dubai.The masterplan offers a mix of villas, townhouses and apartments, alongside two schools, a hospital, six mosques, a dedicated Country Club and Sports Club, retail destinations, and cultural and leisure facilities. It includes approximately 593,000 sqm of planned open space, parks and climate-responsive shaded corridors, with more than 35 km of cycling, jogging and walking routes linking neighbourhoods to community services and retail destinations.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai cuts airport border crossing time to just 3.4 seconds
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: An airport vision set out more than 11 years ago by Lieutenant General Mohammed Ahmed Al Marri, Director-General of the General Directorate of Identity and Foreigners Affairs – Dubai, has become reality, with registered passengers now able to clear immigration at Dubai Airport in just 3.4 seconds.The upgraded smart gate system uses integrated biometric data to speed up identity checks, reduce waiting times and make passenger movement through the airport smoother and more convenient.Al Marri said the technology is designed to streamline the entire passenger journey, rather than simply shorten the time spent at passport control..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..More than a decade ago, Al Marri predicted a future in which technology would reduce airport procedures to just a few seconds. Today, that vision is becoming a reality through Dubai’s upgraded smart gate system, which uses integrated biometric data to allow registered passengers to clear immigration in as little as 3.4 seconds, with minimal delays and fewer processing steps.Al Marri said the upgrade aims to make passenger movement faster and more seamless by using travellers’ biometric information to streamline identity checks and speed up immigration clearance.He explained that the journey begins with passengers registering their biometric data during airline check-in. They can then use this information to pass through smart gates before proceeding to the business lounge and boarding gate..Passengers registered for smart services can complete the relevant procedures with greater ease, he said, adding that the goal is not simply to reduce the time spent at passport control but to improve the entire airport experience.Rather than spending time waiting at different service points, travellers should be able to move smoothly through the airport, from the moment they arrive until they board their flights.The authority has been working to make the systems more flexible and user-friendly, ensuring technology supports passengers throughout their journey rather than simply speeding up one stage of airport processing.The upgrades also help Dubai Airport manage increasing passenger numbers, improve coordination among the various entities operating at the airport and reduce congestion, particularly during peak periods and emergencies.Al Marri stressed that innovation must continue to focus on making travel easier, with smart solutions extending beyond Dubai Airport to other airports and border entry points across the UAE. Such developments would strengthen the integration of services, improve operational efficiency and enhance the experience of travellers across the country.For Dubai, the success of an airport is measured not only by the number of flights and passengers it handles, but also by how efficiently it moves people through every stage of their journey.From a vision to realityThe 3.4-second clearance time is the realisation of an ambition Al Marri spoke about more than 11 years ago, when he discussed how technology could transform airport procedures and reduce the time needed for passenger processing to just a few seconds.What was once a forward-looking vision has now become part of Dubai's airport operations, with biometric technology turning that ambition into a practical service.The transformation goes beyond installing smart gates or speeding up immigration checks. It reflects a wider effort to rethink the passenger journey, eliminate unnecessary waiting and make airport procedures more efficient.The 3.4-second clearance time demonstrates how an idea outlined more than a decade ago is now being translated into everyday airport services, bringing Dubai closer to a future in which technology makes travel simpler and more seamless..Dubai’s biometric Red-Carpet processes 745,188 travellers in eight months of 2026.Dubai smart gates process 9.4 million travellers in 6 months.Dubai’s Red Carpet turns airport travel into a 3.4-second trip.Dubai airport’s ‘Red Carpet’ smart corridor wins global innovation award

source_snapshot.title: Ministry of Economy and Tourism and Amazon announce collaboration to enhance smart shopping and support price transparency as part of Essential Goods Prices Platform
source_snapshot.text: Amazon UAE is the first e-commerce retailer integrated onto the Ministry's Essential Goods Prices Platform, enabling consumers to compare prices across both physical and online retail channels Key takeaways Amazon UAE and the Ministry of Economy and Tourism signed an MoU to collaborate on smart shopping and price transparency. Amazon.ae is the first e-commerce retailer on the Essential Goods Prices Platform. Shoppers can compare prices across 12 major stores and Amazon.ae in one place. The platform showcases prices across 33 product categories in real time. The Ministry of Economy and Tourism announced a collaboration with Amazon UAE as part of its Essential Goods Prices Platform, which was launched in April this year, by virtue of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between both parties at the Ministry’s headquarters in Dubai. In the presence of H.E. Abdulla bin Touq Al Marri, Minister of Economy and Tourism, the agreement was signed by H.E. Abdulla Ahmed Al Saleh, Undersecretary of the Ministry, and Ronaldo Mouchawar, Vice President on behalf of Amazon Middle East, Africa, and Turkey. The collaboration aims to strengthen smart shopping for consumers, while supporting price transparency and fair competition in the UAE. As part of the MoU, Amazon UAE has been integrated onto the Essential Goods Prices Platform, with product price records now live for customers to access. This marks the first time an e-commerce retailer has been added to the Essential Goods Prices Platform, expanding price comparisons beyond physical retail outlets to include online retailers. “Digital transformation and innovation are two key pillars of the UAE’s vision to build a knowledge-based economic model in line with global best practices. The new collaboration with Amazon represents a transformative step forward in this direction by enhancing digital connectivity between government and e-commerce retailers, leveraging advanced technologies to develop digital solutions that strengthen consumer protection and increase transparency within e-commerce. This, in turn, contributes to improving market efficiency, enhancing the competitiveness of the digital economic ecosystem, and supporting greater integration between data and digital services provided to the public.” H.E. Abdulla bin Touq Al Marri Minister of Economy and Tourism His Excellency added: “The Ministry of Economy and Tourism remains committed to advancing its efforts to build an integrated digital landscape driven by data and innovation for monitoring and analysing commodity prices, promoting the concept of smart shopping, and expanding its partnerships with leading local and international e-commerce companies. This aligns with the UAE’s vision to strengthen the digital economy and further develop the e-commerce sector, in line with the objectives of the ‘We the UAE 2031’ vision to position the country as a global hub for the new economy by the next decade.” “At Amazon, we work hard to help customers make smart shopping decisions. Today, customers across the country can access millions of products on Amazon.ae, including a growing selection of everyday essentials that they need most, from groceries and household goods to personal care, delivered fast and at great value. We welcome this collaboration with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism in the UAE, which reflects our shared commitment to helping consumers shop with confidence. We are proud that Amazon.ae is now integrated onto the Essential Goods Prices Platform as the first e-commerce retailer,and look forward to continuing to support the UAE's vision of a digitally connected, consumer-centric economy." Ronaldo Mouchawar Vice President of Amazon Middle East, Africa, and Turkey The Ministry explained that the integration between Amazon and the Ministry’s Essential Goods Prices Platform will allow for the regular updating of pricing data in accordance with precise and approved technical standards. This ensures data reliability, speed and accuracy of updates, while maintaining the highest levels of data security, in compliance with governance and cybersecurity standards. This collaboration empowers consumers to make more informed purchasing decisions by providing information on the prices of essential commodities. It also marks a significant milestone in the development and efficiency of the smart shopping experience. The Essential Goods Prices Platform enables easy and transparent price comparisons, thereby contributing to the development of a smart and sustainable shopping environment across the country. Currently, the Essential Goods Prices Platform focuses on displaying prices of essential goods which are identified based on the consumer priority products list. This ensures a focus on the most frequently purchased goods while enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of monitoring their price levels. It currently includes 33 product categories, comprising 17 essential consumer goods and 16 other key commodities. Prices are monitored in real time across 12 major physical retail outlets and Amazon.ae as the platform's first e-commerce retailer in the UAE, with the minimum and maximum prices published for each outlet, enabling consumers to compare prices easily across different branches. The platform also allows users to create a customised grocery basket based on their needs and automatically directs them to the most cost-effective option in terms of price. These features contribute to enhancing transparency and promoting the optimal use of consumers’ budgets. Related Tags Economic Impact Retail Technology

evidence_passages.text: Ministry of Economy and Tourism and Amazon announce collaboration to enhance smart shopping and support price transparency as part of Essential Goods Prices Platform

Amazon UAE is the first e-commerce retailer integrated onto the Ministry's Essential Goods Prices Platform, enabling consumers to compare prices across both physical and online retail channels Key takeaways Amazon UAE and the Ministry of Economy and Tourism signed an MoU to collaborate on smart shopping and price transparency.
Amazon.ae is the first e-commerce retailer on the Essential Goods Prices Platform.
Shoppers can compare prices across 12 major stores and Amazon.ae in one place.
The platform showcases prices across 33 product categories in real time.

The Ministry of Economy and Tourism announced a collaboration with Amazon UAE as part of its Essential Goods Prices Platform, which was launched in April this year, by virtue of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between both parties at the Ministry’s headquarters in Dubai.
In the presence of H.E.
Abdulla bin Touq Al Marri, Minister of Economy and Tourism, the agreement was signed by H.E.
Abdulla Ahmed Al Saleh, Undersecretary of the Ministry, and Ronaldo Mouchawar, Vice President on behalf of Amazon Middle East, Africa, and Turkey.
The collaboration aims to strengthen smart shopping for consumers, while supporting price transparency and fair competition in the UAE.
As part of the MoU, Amazon UAE has been integrated onto the Essential Goods Prices Platform, with product price records now live for customers to access.
This marks the first time an e-commerce retailer has been added to the Essential Goods Prices Platform, expanding price comparisons beyond physical retail outlets to include online retailers.
“Digital transformation and innovation are two key pillars of the UAE’s vision to build a knowledge-based economic model in line with global best practices.

The new collaboration with Amazon represents a transformative step forward in this direction by enhancing digital connectivity between government and e-commerce retailers, leveraging advanced technologies to develop digital solutions that strengthen consumer protection and increase transparency within e-commerce.

This, in turn, contributes to improving market efficiency, enhancing the competitiveness of the digital economic ecosystem, and supporting greater integration between data and digital services provided to the public.” H.E.

Abdulla bin Touq Al Marri Minister of Economy and Tourism His Excellency added: “The Ministry of Economy and Tourism remains committed to advancing its efforts to build an integrated digital landscape driven by data and innovation for monitoring and analysing commodity prices, promoting the concept of smart shopping, and expanding its partnerships with leading local and international e-commerce companies.

This aligns with the UAE’s vision to strengthen the digital economy and further develop the e-commerce sector, in line with the objectives of the ‘We the UAE 2031’ vision to position the country as a global hub for the new economy by the next decade.” “At Amazon, we work hard to help customers make smart shopping decisions.

Today, customers across the country can access millions of products on Amazon.ae, including a growing selection of everyday essentials that they need most, from groceries and household goods to personal care, delivered fast and at great value.
We welcome this collaboration with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism in the UAE, which reflects our shared commitment to helping consumers shop with confidence.

We are proud that Amazon.ae is now integrated onto the Essential Goods Prices Platform as the first e-commerce retailer,and look forward to continuing to support the UAE's vision of a digitally connected, consumer-centric economy." Ronaldo Mouchawar Vice President of Amazon Middle East, Africa, and Turkey The Ministry explained that the integration between Amazon and the Ministry’s Essential Goods Prices Platform will allow for the regular updating of pricing data in accordance with precise and approved technical standards.
This ensures data reliability, speed and accuracy of updates, while maintaining the highest levels of data security, in compliance with governance and cybersecurity standards.
This collaboration empowers consumers to make more informed purchasing decisions by providing information on the prices of essential commodities.
It also marks a significant milestone in the development and efficiency of the smart shopping experience.
The Essential Goods Prices Platform enables easy and transparent price comparisons, thereby contributing to the development of a smart and sustainable shopping environment across the country.
Currently, the Essential Goods Prices Platform focuses on displaying prices of essential goods which are identified based on the consumer priority products list.
This ensures a focus on the most frequently purchased goods while enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of monitoring their price levels.
It currently includes 33 product categories, comprising 17 essential consumer goods and 16 other key commodities.

Prices are monitored in real time across 12 major physical retail outlets and Amazon.ae as the platform's first e-commerce retailer in the UAE, with the minimum and maximum prices published for each outlet, enabling consumers to compare prices easily across different branches.
The platform also allows users to create a customised grocery basket based on their needs and automatically directs them to the most cost-effective option in terms of price.
These features contribute to enhancing transparency and promoting the optimal use of consumers’ budgets.

source_snapshot.title: New UAE traffic regulations tighten vehicle recall and inspection rules
source_snapshot.text: Abu Dhabi: The new executive regulations of the UAE Federal Traffic Law, which will come into effect at the beginning of January, 2027, establish a new framework for handling vehicle recalls due to manufacturing defects. The regulations require commercial agents to repair manufacturing defects free of charge and give licensing authorities the power to suspend transactions involving vehicles whose owners fail to respond to recall notices. Under Article 122, commercial agents in the country must monitor manufacturers’ announcements concerning manufacturing defects and identify vehicles in the UAE affected by them. Agents must notify the licensing authority and the competent consumer protection authority of the chassis numbers, or VINs, of vehicles covered by recall campaigns, the reasons for the recalls and the approved corrective measures. They must also announce recalls of vehicles affected by manufacturing defects through the media. The article requires licensing authorities to establish a mechanism for cooperating with commercial agents, in coordination with the competent consumer protection authority, to identify the names and addresses of owners of vehicles affected by manufacturing defects. Licensing authorities are also empowered to take measures to ensure vehicle owners comply with recall campaigns. If an owner fails to respond to a recall issued by a commercial agent, the authorities must take the necessary steps to secure compliance. These measures may include preventing any action or transaction involving the chassis number of the vehicle affected by the recall. To protect consumer rights, commercial agents must repair advertised manufacturing defects free of charge. They must also ensure the availability of the necessary spare parts and qualified personnel to carry out repairs without adversely affecting customer satisfaction. Updating vehicle owner data The executive regulations also stress the importance of maintaining accurate vehicle owner information with traffic authorities. Owners are responsible for any financial or legal consequences resulting from negligence or delays in updating their contact details. Under Article 114, a vehicle owner must notify the licensing authority of any changes to their personal information, address or contact details, as well as the details of their legal representative where necessary. The vehicle owner is responsible for any financial or legal consequences resulting from a failure or delay in updating this information. Technical inspection The regulations also set out procedures for cases in which the traffic control authority refers a vehicle for technical inspection, establishing a mechanism intended to enhance road safety standards. Under Article 121, when a vehicle is referred by the traffic control authority, the licensing authority must conduct a technical inspection and verify the reasons for the referral. It must then provide the traffic control authority with the inspection results so that the necessary procedures can be carried out. If the reasons for the referral are confirmed, the vehicle owner must repair the defects, bear any transportation costs and resubmit the vehicle for technical inspection to confirm that the reasons for the referral have been addressed. If the reasons for the referral are not confirmed, the vehicle may be driven and used on the road. Its owner will not be required to bear any costs arising from the inspection or transportation process. Three-year inspection exemption The regulations provide exemptions from technical inspection in three cases. Newly manufactured light vehicles imported from the factory or authorised dealers are exempt for three years from the date of first licensing. Newly manufactured non-light vehicles imported from the factory or authorised dealers are exempt for one year from the date of first licensing. Newly manufactured vehicles in other categories imported from the factory or authorised dealers are also exempt for one year from the date of first licensing. In all cases, the licensing authority may require an exempt vehicle to undergo a technical inspection if it considers this necessary for traffic safety.

source_snapshot.title: UAE banks update terms and conditions from January 2027: What to check in your notice, from fees to facial recognition
source_snapshot.text: Abu Dhabi: Banks operating in the country have begun announcing new updates that include amendments to the terms and conditions of transactions and fee schedules, which will come into effect from the beginning of 2027. They have asked customers to review bank notices and amended versions of contracts, especially the clauses related to digital services, data use, and transaction fees. According to messages sent to customers, the anticipated changes are not uniform across the banking sector, nor do they necessarily mean a comprehensive increase in fees, as some are limited to updating the contractual and regulatory wording, while others are related to new tariff schedules, the details of which will be revealed later. A local bank announced the issuance of an updated version of the terms and conditions relating to retail banking products, which will come into effect in January 2027, replacing the current version. The bank also issued a parallel update to the terms and conditions of Islamic banking services for individuals, which will come into effect on the same date. New terms and conditions The new terms cover the entire relationship between the bank and the customer, including accounts, credit cards, loans, electronic banking services and rewards programs, along with provisions related to communication, execution of customer instructions, data updates, and account suspension or closure. The updated version included an expansion of the provisions relating to the collection, use, processing and disclosure of customer data inside and outside the UAE, as well as the customer’s obligations to update information on work, residence, nationality, tax residency, contact numbers and documents submitted to the bank. The conditions also addressed digital verification mechanisms for customer identity, the use of facial recognition for login, adding beneficiaries, transfers, data updates, and execution of financial and non-financial transactions, with the possibility of replacing some traditional verification methods, including one-time passwords, with digital authentication methods. The publication of the new terms was not accompanied by an announcement of a general increase in account or card fees, which confirms the need to separate the updating of contractual terms from the amendment of the fee schedule. The customer should review the tariff schedule and product statement to ensure there are any actual financial changes. In a related context, a branch of a foreign bank operating in the country announced its intention to issue a new tariff schedule for its corporate clients, to be implemented starting from January 1, 2027, without publishing the new fee values ​​yet. Another bank also announced a limited regulatory change, concerning customers residing in countries of the European Economic Area. Accordingly, starting from the beginning of 2027, the bank will not be able to initiate the presentation of some new products and services to them, while confirming the continuation of service for current products and that customers do not need to take action, and the announcement did not include the imposition of new fees. Notifying customers The Consumer Protection Standards issued by the Central Bank of the UAE require financial institutions to notify customers at least 60 days in advance of any permissible change to the terms and conditions of products or services, including fees, providing a clear language summary of the changes and a copy of the amended terms. Customers should not just rely on the heading ‘Terms and Conditions Update’, but should read the notices sent by their banks, especially the clauses relating to fees, digital authentication, data use and account closure, to ensure that the updates affect their banking products before they are implemented.

New terms and conditions The new terms cover the entire relationship between the bank and the customer, including accounts, credit cards, loans, electronic banking services and rewards programs, along with provisions related to communication, execution of customer instructions, data updates, and account suspension or closure.

The updated version included an expansion of the provisions relating to the collection, use, processing and disclosure of customer data inside and outside the UAE, as well as the customer’s obligations to update information on work, residence, nationality, tax residency, contact numbers and documents submitted to the bank.

The conditions also addressed digital verification mechanisms for customer identity, the use of facial recognition for login, adding beneficiaries, transfers, data updates, and execution of financial and non-financial transactions, with the possibility of replacing some traditional verification methods, including one-time passwords, with digital authentication methods.

The publication of the new terms was not accompanied by an announcement of a general increase in account or card fees, which confirms the need to separate the updating of contractual terms from the amendment of the fee schedule.
The customer should review the tariff schedule and product statement to ensure there are any actual financial changes.

In a related context, a branch of a foreign bank operating in the country announced its intention to issue a new tariff schedule for its corporate clients, to be implemented starting from January 1, 2027, without publishing the new fee values ​​yet.
Another bank also announced a limited regulatory change, concerning customers residing in countries of the European Economic Area.

Accordingly, starting from the beginning of 2027, the bank will not be able to initiate the presentation of some new products and services to them, while confirming the continuation of service for current products and that customers do not need to take action, and the announcement did not include the imposition of new fees.

Notifying customers The Consumer Protection Standards issued by the Central Bank of the UAE require financial institutions to notify customers at least 60 days in advance of any permissible change to the terms and conditions of products or services, including fees, providing a clear language summary of the changes and a copy of the amended terms.

Customers should not just rely on the heading ‘Terms and Conditions Update’, but should read the notices sent by their banks, especially the clauses relating to fees, digital authentication, data use and account closure, to ensure that the updates affect their banking products before they are implemented.

title: UAE banks update terms and conditions from January 2027: What to check in your notice, from fees to facial recognition

source_snapshot.title: KHDA launches Dubai’s student protection framework for private schools: Three risk levels and a protection team in every school
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: The Knowledge and Human Development Authority (KHDA) in Dubai has launched a unified framework for student safety and protection in private education institutions, which defines the responsibilities of institutions and mechanisms for prevention, reporting and response. It also classifies cases that threaten student safety into three levels according to their degree of severity, while specifying procedures for dealing with each level. The framework includes schools, early childhood centres, higher education institutions, and vocational training and education institutes licensed by the KHDA, and covers in-person and virtual learning environments. The KHDA announced the framework during a press conference held yesterday, in the presence of the Executive Director of the Policy, Research and Programs Sector at the authority, Dr. Saeed Mubarak bin Kharbash, and the Director of the Early Childhood and Development Policies and Programs Department, Fatima Mohammed Al Janahi. Bin Kharbash stated that the well-being, quality of life, and development of learners are fundamental pillars for building the future of society. He emphasised that the framework places children and families at the heart of the social development process and clarifies the roles, responsibilities, and accountability mechanisms for educational institutions. Executive Director of the Policy, Research and Programs Sector at the KHDA, Dr. Saeed Mubarak bin Kharbash. Picture credit: Supplied He added that the framework is based on the principles established by the Child Rights Law (Wadeema) and complements existing legislation and policies in the UAE and Dubai. It also supports the objectives of Dubai Social Agenda 33 and the Dubai Education Strategy 2033. He pointed out that protecting students requires effective leadership, qualified staff, and proactive parents, in addition to establishing an institutional culture that listens to students and provides them with support. Fatima Mohammed Al Janahi said that the framework defines the roles within educational institutions and obliges each school to form a student protection team, which includes the school principal as a supervisor, and at least two student protection officers who assume clear responsibilities in this area. She explained that student protection officers are responsible for monitoring cases, receiving and evaluating reports, and coordinating with specialists and senior management to determine the appropriate action, while the school principal is responsible for supervising the protection system and ensuring the effectiveness of its systems, without directly managing the cases. She added that the responsibilities include educational and academic staff and boards of trustees, in order to ensure the integration of roles and a swift response to concerns related to student safety. She indicated that the authority will work on preparing specialised training programs for those tasked with protecting students, in addition to qualifying the rest of the staff and members of the boards of trustees to deal with cases, and follow reporting and coordination procedures. Fatima Mohammed Al Janahi, Director of the Early Childhood and Development Policies and Programs Department at the KHDA. Picture credit: Supplied Dr. Samia Al Dhaoui, an educational expert at the authority, said that the framework classifies cases that threaten the safety of students into three levels, and specifies for each the mechanisms of intervention and the parties concerned with dealing with them. She explained that high-risk cases require immediate intervention and referral to the competent authorities, including Dubai Police and ambulance services, depending on the nature of the case. As for moderately serious cases, they require intervention and follow-up according to the assessment of the protection team, with the possibility of referring them to the Community Development Authority, or coordinating with the police and ambulance when needed, and informing the KHDA to ensure coordination with parents and relevant authorities. She added that low-risk cases include initial indicators and observations monitored by the teaching staff, which do not pose a significant risk when detected, but require treatment to prevent their escalation. The institution handles them internally, while informing the authority within 72 hours. Al Dhaoui stressed that the classification gives priority to intervention for the most serious cases and helps protection teams to choose the appropriate action, noting the importance of continuous training and studying practical scenarios to raise the efficiency of these teams. Dr. Samia Al Dhaoui, an educational expert at the authority, said that the framework classifies cases that threaten the safety of students into three levels. Emirates apologised for any inconvenience this delay may cause and expressed its appreciation for passengers' patience and understanding.
